items.title: Study Linking Solar Farms to Bird Loss Draws Scrutiny in China
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018949/Study Linking Solar Farms to Bird Loss Draws Scrutiny in China
items.summary: China’s scientific community has questioned a recent study in the country that concluded solar farms may reduce bird diversity, interrogating the paper’s data and statistical methods.
items.body_text:
Study Linking Solar Farms to Bird Loss Draws Scrutiny in China
Solar farms reduce bird diversity, a Chinese study published last week in the international, peer-reviewed journal Science, announced. But the country’s scientific community has contested the reliability of its birdwatching data and the significance of its statistical findings.
The study, published Aug. 21, was led by researchers at Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, in collaboration with other researchers from China, Vietnam, and the United States.
Examining 2,344 Chinese counties from 2014 to 2023, it found that cutting carbon emissions may come at the cost of protecting biodiversity, as birds’ cropland and grassland habitats are converted for solar projects.
China has been expanding solar power to meet its targets of peaking carbon emissions by 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2060. By 2024, solar facilities covered an estimated 4,520 square kilometers of land and are projected to make up nearly 45% of the country’s electricity generation by 2060.
“The research is not against solar expansion but rather offers policy recommendations on how to do it better,” Li Shanjun, one of the study’s corresponding authors and a professor at the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability, told Sixth Tone.
The authors suggested developing solar projects in areas where solar panels cause lower ecological impact, such as in deserts; promoting phased rollouts rather than sudden large-scale expansion; and assessing ecological recovery beyond vegetation density, as they found uniform vegetation inferior for housing bird habitats.
However, experts from the China Ornithological Society said “flaws” in the study’s bird observation data could undermine its conclusions, according to a Tuesday article published on the society’s official WeChat account. The academic group includes ornithologists from universities, research institutes, and conservation organizations nationwide.
The crowdsourced dataset from the China Birdwatching Record Center contained missing bird counts, erroneous records, and reporting differences driven by the growing popularity of birdwatching, the Society wrote.
Among the issues, over 40% of the over 500,000 reports collected during the nine years recorded the presence of species, indicated using the number “1.” However, the Society noted that this is commonly used as a placeholder when the observer did not enter a count, rather than that only one bird was seen, making the data unreliable.
The analysis also said the data had not been properly cleaned. One record from 2015, for example, reported over 2 billion little egrets at a single location. The record was retained in the dataset, contributing to bird totals “beyond a reasonable range.”
Meanwhile, the original study may have removed some migratory waterbirds’ records at wintering sites as statistical outliers, as they recorded tens of thousands of birds at a given location, “potentially underestimating true bird diversity,” the analysis said.
The analysis also noted that birdwatching records surged between 2021 and 2023 amid a growing birdwatching boom in the country, just as authorities were introducing significant solar policies. This, it argued, makes it difficult to determine whether changes in biodiversity data were driven by increased birdwatching or photovoltaic development.
Chinese ecologists generally agree that amid cutting carbon emissions, biodiversity can be protected through careful planning, Ma Zhijun, deputy director of the China Ornithological Society and a co-author of the analysis, told Sixth Tone. Ma is also a professor at Fudan University’s School of Life Sciences.
Such planning means avoiding key wildlife habitats when building solar, wind, and other renewable energy facilities, Ma said.
He added that the “easy availability” of birdwatching datasets has led researchers without a background in bird ecology to use them without “fully understanding their limitations.”

items.title: After ‘Sleep No More,’ What’s Next for Chinese Immersive Theater?
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018941/After ‘Sleep No More,’ What’s Next for Chinese Immersive Theater?
items.summary: China’s immersive productions have grown ever larger and more spectacular. Their next challenge is turning audience participation into genuine understanding.
items.body_text:
After ‘Sleep No More,’ What’s Next for Chinese Immersive Theater?
After 2,670 performances, the immersive theatrical production “Sleep No More,” co-produced by Shanghai Media Group and pioneering British theater company Punchdrunk, will conclude its 10-year run at the McKinnon Hotel in Shanghai on Aug. 30.
When it opened in Shanghai a decade ago, the production wowed local theatergoers with its novelty and impact. Audience members donned white masks and entered a dimly lit building where they could move freely between rooms: following Macbeth, searching for the witches, or wandering the corridors piecing together clues. No one could see the complete story, but “missing out” was part of the experience.
A decade on, immersive theater has blossomed across China, appearing in theaters, scenic areas, museums, shopping malls, and former factories. There are even purpose-built theatrical theme parks. “Unique Henan,” for example, in the suburbs of Zhengzhou, capital of the central Henan province, features 21 performance spaces and nearly 1,000 actors performing almost 700 minutes of material each day. Visitors can spend an entire day exploring the park and still see only a fraction of what it offers. Meanwhile, “Unique Dream of Red Mansions” in Langfang, in the northern Hebei province, takes the classic Chinese novel “Dream of the Red Chamber” as its theme, with four large theaters, eight smaller ones, and 108 interconnected immersive spaces. Its daily performances total more than 800 minutes.
Was all this brought about by “Sleep No More”? Yes and no.
In traditional theater, the theatrical world is confined to the other side of the stage, while the audience sits in darkness and watches a carefully framed reality. This model came under scrutiny in the 20th century. Avant-garde theater pioneers, including Antonin Artaud, Jerzy Grotowski, Peter Brook, and Richard Schechner, reexamined the body, space, presence, and the relationship between audiences and performers. Schechner, in particular, developed the concept of “environmental theater,” emphasizing that a theatrical event encompasses not only performers and text but also the audience, sensory stimuli, architecture, and other elements of the performance space. Modern theater has since continued to seek ways to move audiences beyond fixed seats and into cities, rivers, markets, and historical settings, making space part of the work itself.
Such practices are nothing new in Chinese theater. From 1932 to 1937, playwright Xiong Foxi went to Ding County in Hebei as part of a movement to popularize theater in rural China. His productions integrated stage scenery with the real sky and surrounding forest, while audiences crossed the fourth wall to participate directly in the performance.
Since the early 2000s, director Wang Chaoge’s pioneering “Impression” and “Encore” series have reshaped the spatial aesthetics of China’s cultural tourism performances through large-scale live productions. They took theater beyond the proscenium arch and into outdoor landscapes, familiarizing audiences with expansive, panoramic, and interactive performances. “Encore Pingyao,” which premiered in 2013 in Pingyao, in the northern Shanxi province, went further by dispensing with the traditional stage entirely. Audiences walked through streets, courtyards, and indoor spaces alongside the actors.
“Sleep No More” was therefore by no means the starting point for immersive theater in China. Long before its arrival, Chinese audiences were already familiar with shared spaces, physical participation, and collective rituals. Nevertheless, it marked an important watershed. It gave Chinese theater practitioners an internationally influential model: a mature, replicable, sustainable, and long-running production. By combining free movement, multiple narratives, repeat viewings, and word-of-mouth recommendations, it demonstrated that audiences were willing to pay for highly personalized live experiences.

items.title: Hundreds Still Missing After Deadly China-Nepal Border Mudslide
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018953/Hundreds Still Missing After Deadly China-Nepal Border Mudslide
items.summary: Search teams are still working through deep mud and broken roads as an upstream landslide dam raises fears of further flooding.
items.body_text:
Hundreds Still Missing After Deadly China-Nepal Border Mudslide
On Monday, Zhao Jianing rode his motorcycle through the Gyirong border checkpoint under clear skies, inching past export trucks and lines of BYD vehicles as traffic backed up along the China-Nepal border. He recalled seeing at least a dozen uniformed workers at their posts.
Two days later, a massive surge of water, mud, and debris descended from the Nepali side of the Himalayas and tore through the border area at around 11 a.m. Wednesday. Funneled through a steep valley toward southwestern China’s Xizang Autonomous Region, the torrent swept away police posts and buried the Gyirong checkpoint.
Surveillance footage from outside the checkpoint showed muddy floodwaters surging above the border gates and engulfing the area within seconds as people fled. Aerial footage from state broadcaster CCTV later showed the border zone blanketed in mud, with no buildings visible.
By Thursday, three people had been confirmed dead and 558 remained missing in Gyirong County on the Chinese side, while two people had been rescued. Across the affected area, at least 273 people were dead and 1,384 remained missing.
China’s Ministry of Water Resources told CCTV that a landslide dam had formed upstream, creating a lake containing an estimated 2 million cubic meters of water. The lake was already overflowing, and another 3 million cubic meters were expected to channel into it over the next three days, raising the risk that the dam could fail.
The threat further complicated rescue efforts already hampered by damaged roads and communications infrastructure.
Xizang activated its highest-level emergency response, deploying military transport aircraft, more than 800 firefighters, and armed police officers to the area. Central authorities also allocated 220 million yuan ($30.7 million) for disaster relief, recovery, and reconstruction.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived in the mudslide-hit area of Gyirong Township on Thursday to oversee rescue and relief efforts, state news agency Xinhua reported. He visited on behalf of President Xi Jinping and met rescue workers and people displaced by the disaster.
Wang Qian, an official with the Shigatse military sub-command, told CCTV that the edge of the mudslide was about 2.5 kilometers from the Gyirong checkpoint, where mud was nearly 1.5 meters deep.
Gyirong is Xizang’s largest land port and a major gateway for trade and travel between China and Nepal. As of June 23, the checkpoint had recorded more than 100,000 entries and exits this year, up 12.85% from the same period in 2025.
Crossing into Nepal two days earlier, Zhao, a 26-year-old motorcyclist from Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, remembered the checkpoint as busy but ordinary, with clear skies, lines of export vehicles, and workers directing traffic.
One of those workers, a uniformed man Zhao estimated to be in his 30s, had briefly argued with him over his speed.
After seeing footage of police posts being swept away, Zhao said he kept thinking about the encounter. “I never imagined that just one or two days later, everything would be gone,” Zhao told Sixth Tone. “It happened so fast. I think he probably had no chance to escape. I feel really guilty and upset.”
The road on the Nepalese side beyond the checkpoint was extremely difficult to navigate, he said. In some places, the mud was “as deep as half the length of an arm,” he said, forcing him to use both feet to keep the motorcycle moving. His shoes even came off.
“The cliff was on the right and the muddy road was on the left. I could barely ride. I thought I was going to die there,” he said.
No official investigation has established the cause of Wednesday’s disaster, but several experts said preliminary evidence points to a possible high-altitude ice-rock avalanche originating from a tributary of the Donglin Tsangpo River in Nepal.

items.title: America lost its longest war five years ago. This is what victory looks like for the Taliban
items.summary: A reporter who knew Kabul before the Taliban returns five years after the US withdrawal to find safer streets and fading hope Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
America lost its longest war five years ago. This is what victory looks like for the Taliban
“When Ashraf Ghani goes, we’ll go with him. And he’ll go when the Americans do.”
The conversation took place on the balcony of a luxury high-rise in Shahr-e Naw, central Kabul. The man speaking to me was a young government employee, and Ashraf Ghani was serving his second term as president of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan. It was May 2017. The republic had four years and three months left.
A city living on borrowed time
Afghanistan at the time could best be described with a line from Dickens: “It was the best of times, it was the worst of times… we had everything before us, we had nothing before us.” Kabul was both deeply Westernized and full of contradictions. The former was fueled by the abundance of foreigners and foreign aid; the latter by the unending fighting and terrorist attacks.
Downtown, you could find nightclubs throwing Valentine’s Day and Halloween parties, modeling agencies, coffee shops serving cheesecake, bowling alleys, and tattoo parlors. On the outskirts, tent camps were expanding to accommodate internally displaced people – refugees from the provinces, mostly in the south, whose homes had been destroyed by the war. Street boys begged in English: “Give me one hundred dollars!” Artists painted murals warning about domestic violence, fashionable women wore jeans and bright makeup, and Western NGOs taught Afghan children to skateboard.
At the same time, some places – including the park in Shahr-e Naw itself – were unsafe even in broad daylight because of the number of drug addicts, while robberies and kidnappings had become routine. After sunset, the city shut down. Several years later, The New York Times would call Kabul a city of hope and despair – an apt metaphor.
To protect itself from the constant bombings, Kabul grew a shell of concrete walls and checkpoints. There seemed to be as many police officers and soldiers on the streets as civilians, while American surveillance balloons hovered continuously over the city. None of it helped much. That same May, while I was there, a tanker truck packed with explosives detonated in the diplomatic quarter, killing more than 90 people and wounding around 400. Smaller incidents had long since ceased to qualify as news. One of my editors gave me a simple rule:
“If there’s a terrorist attack in Kabul and fewer than ten people are killed, don’t write about it. That’s not news.”
Politics and public life were no less remarkable. Afghanistan’s parliament had as many women as the US Congress, yet in the center of the capital a mob lynched Farkhunda Malikzada, a young Afghan woman, after a mullah falsely accused her of burning the Quran. Corruption broke every record, and the central government was weak. items.title: Incidents of AI going rogue double – Guardian
items.summary: Incidents of artificial intelligence going rogue almost doubled last month, The Guardian has reported, citing a monitoring group Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Incidents of AI going rogue double – Guardian
A record number of instances of artificial intelligence (AI) lying, ignoring users’ commands or acting in harmful ways to achieve its goals were registered last month, The Guardian has reported, citing a monitoring group.
Concerns about the safety of AI are on the rise after advanced models by OpenAI and Anthropic exhibited rogue behavior during testing this summer, with calls made to halt their development and introduce stricter government oversight of the process.
There were more than 300 incidents of real-world loss of control involving AI models employed by actual businesses and private individuals in July, which is almost double the number in June, an article in the paper said on Saturday.
The data came from the Loss of Control Observatory, which was set up by the UK government’s AI Security Institute (AISI) last November to track complaints about issues with AI made by users on X, it said.
As the monitor only gathers reports from a single social media platform, the true number of incidents must be higher, The Guardian noted.
A majority out of the 1,600 complaints on X in 2026 were made by software developers using AI bots in their work, according to AISI.
The monitor said that despite the fact that most real-world loss of control incidents did not cause significant harm, it has registered an increase in severity of AI’s deceptiveness and neglect of human commands.
Reports by users “evidence AI systems’ willingness to disregard direct instructions, circumvent safeguards, lie to users and single-mindedly pursue a goal in harmful ways,” AISI warned.
Tommy Shaffer-Shane, the senior policy manager at the Centre for Long Term Resilience, which operates the observatory, told The Guardian that it is wrong to suggest that AI only misbehaves during testing.
“We need to not be complacent that these things won’t happen in the real world and there is evidence that they already are,” he said.
The monitor has called on the British government to oblige AI companies to report loss of control incidents and to introduce emergency powers, including temporary restrictions on artificial intelligence, in order to deal with the more severe cases.

items.title: Iceland votes against resuming EU accession talks
items.summary: Iceland has rejected the idea of resuming talks on joining the EU in a referendum, public broadcaster RUV has reported Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Iceland votes against resuming EU accession talks
Iceland has narrowly rejected the idea of resuming talks on joining the EU, public broadcaster RUV has reported. Previous negotiations were halted 13 years ago.
The referendum on Saturday saw a high turnout, with more than 225,000 people out of a population of just over 394,000 coming to the polls.
After the ballot count concluded on Sunday, RUV announced that 52.8% said ‘no’ to resuming accession talks, while 47.2% backed the idea.
The ballot asked voters just a single question: “Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?”
The country’s capital Reykjavik voted ‘Yes’, while people in rural areas were overwhelmingly against the EU path, underlining a split between the two parts of the country.
Russian presidential investment envoy Kirill Dmitriev has welcomed the outcome of the referendum, saying in a post on X that “Iceland knows how to play great football and how to reject the failing EU’s migrants, bureaucrats, and warmongering.”
Icelandic Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir promised to hold a referendum by 2027, but moved it to an earlier date due to geopolitical tensions, including US President Donald Trump’s threats to annex neighboring Greenland, which is an autonomous territory of Denmark.
In January, Trump’s nominee for ambassador to Iceland, Billy Long, suggested that country could become the “52nd state” of the US, with himself as governor. However, he later apologized and called it a joke.
Before the vote, Frostadottir’s allies portrayed the EU as additional protection for the country, while Euroskeptics argued that Brussels itself was becoming increasingly militarized and confrontational. Iceland is already a founding NATO member and maintains extensive military ties with Washington.

Russian forces struck a transhipment terminal in the southern Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv on Aug. 29, the Russian Defense Ministry claimed on Telegram.

Across the border in Russia, three people have been killed and nine injured in a Ukrainian drone attack in the Russian Belgorod region. According to local authorities. Three of the injured are in serious condition, the authorities said.
In Kyiv, Russian missiles struck logistics warehouses Moscow claimed contained components for Ukraine's domestically produced Flamingo cruise missiles, which Kyiv uses to strike oil terminals and logistics hubs in Russia. The Moscow Times could not immediately confirm that the affected facility was related to Flamingo manufacturing. Local authorities said at least 37 people were killed in a secondary explosion caused by the blast.
Russian authorities also claimed to have struck a site handling shipments of military hardware from Kyiv's allies in the town of Kalinivka. The supply of weapons from the West to Kyiv was established as one of Russia's so-called red lines even before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, though that line has been crossed repeatedly since February 2022. Russia warned on Aug. 27 that it could strike British military targets inside and outside Ukraine in response to Ukraine's alleged use of British weapons to hit targets in Russia.
The Russian Defence Ministry also said on Saturday that Russian troops had captured the village of Khrapivshchyna in Ukraine's Sumy region, as well as the villages of Novoandriivka and Rubizhne in the Donetsk region.

The Strategic Missile Forces deployed a mobile launcher battery to a remote area before firing the missile across the country to the Kura test site on the Kamchatka Peninsula, located more than 6,700 kilometers (4,160 miles) to the east.

items.title: Moscow Court Jails Ex-Ukrainian Presidential Aide Oleksiy Arestovych 11 Years in Absentia
items.summary: A judge found Arestovych guilty of spreading false information about the Russian military and publicly calling for terrorism.
items.body_text:
A judge in Moscow on Friday sentenced Oleksiy Arestovych, a former adviser to the Ukrainian president’s office, to 11 years in prison in absentia after finding him guilty of spreading false information about the Russian military and publicly calling for terrorism.
Russian investigators accused Arestovych of publishing false statements about a deadly Russian missile strike on a railway station in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk in April 2022.
Prosecutors also accused Arestovych of calling on Ukrainians to sabotage railway lines used to resupply Russian troops in a March 2022 video.
A judge from the Second Western District Military Court delivered the guilty verdict against Arestovych following a closed-door trial.
In addition to the 11-year prison sentence, the judge also banned Arestovych from managing websites for four years.
Prosecutors had requested a sentence of 15 years in prison for Arestovych, according to the exiled news outlet Mediazona.
“What a sophisticated cover-up operation,” Arestovych wrote on Telegram in response to the court ruling.
Arestovych served as an adviser to the head of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s office until January 2023, when he resigned after claiming a Ukrainian air defense missile caused a deadly strike on an apartment in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro.
He has since recast himself as a critic of the Ukrainian government and amassed an online following on his YouTube channel. Arestovych now lives outside of Ukraine. Zelensky sanctioned him last year.
Russia added Arestovych to its list of “terrorists and extremists” in May 2023 and placed him on its wanted list in October 2023. Moscow’s Basmanny District Court placed Arestovych in pre-trial detention in absentia in February 2024.

items.body_text:
At least 37 killed after Russian strike hits an ammunition depot near Kyiv, triggering massive explosions. Many of the victims were residents of a nearby care home.
The Russian army struck the village of Myla on the outskirts of Kyiv on the evening of August 28, setting fire to a warehouse where ammunition was being stored. The fire triggered a series of detonations, sending flames into nearby private homes. The explosions were powerful enough that authorities shut down traffic entirely on the Zhytomyr highway between the 15th and 32nd kilometer markers. Nearly 400 people were evacuated from the area affected by the strike.
Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv Regional Military Administration, said Saturday morning that at least 27 people had been killed in the Russian strike on Myla, in Kyiv region’s Bucha district. Another 42 people, including four children, were injured to varying degrees. Among the dead was Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community in the Kyiv region, who had been helping rescue people from the fire.
Update. As of 2:00 p.m. Saturday, 37 people are known to have died in the Russian strike, Tymur Tkachenko wrote.
About 50 residential buildings were damaged. The heaviest damage was to a nearby care home for elderly and disabled residents, where 20 people died, according to local social media pages.
Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the care home had been damaged. “Those who allowed this must certainly bear responsibility for their decisions. Investigators from the National Police and the Security Service of Ukraine are conducting a pretrial investigation, and a criminal case has been opened over official negligence. There are rules: ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential buildings. There will definitely be appropriate conclusions,” the president of Ukraine said.
Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi called what happened in the Bucha district the result of “criminal negligence,” recalling the “terrible tragedy in Vyshneve,” which he said “did not serve as a lesson.” Russian forces struck a Ukroboronprom warehouse in Vyshneve, near Kyiv, in July. The resulting detonation damaged 300 residential buildings and killed nine people.
The Kyiv region declared August 30 a day of mourning for those killed in the Russian strike.
Russia’s Defense Ministry stated that its drones struck an ammunition warehouse belonging to the Ukrainian defense company Fire Point in the village of Myla, where components for FP-1/FP-2 UAVs were stored. The ministry also claimed that overnight on August 29, Russian troops struck logistics centers in the villages of Chaiky and Kalynivka near Kyiv, where components for Ukrainian “Flamingo” cruise missiles were stored as well, among other things.

items.body_text:
Washington Post: Ratcliffe secretly visited Moscow to warn Russia not to exploit perceived U.S. weakness from the Iran war, saying escalation in Ukraine would push Trump toward Zelensky
CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow on August 25 — the first trip to Russia by the head of a U.S. intelligence agency since the start of the full-scale war. The visit was not announced in advance and took place under heightened secrecy. Journalists spent several hours trying to determine who had landed in Moscow aboard a U.S. military transport plane, while the Kremlin insisted no meetings with U.S. administration officials were planned for that week.
Several days after the visit, Ratcliffe was still not known to have met with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the trip was a matter of “communication through intelligence service channels.” According to Sergei Naryshkin, director of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), he and Ratcliffe “discussed a number of issues that fall within the purview of the intelligence services.” “The meeting took place,” Naryshkin said. “There’s nothing unusual about it.”
U.S. President Donald Trump struck the same note, calling Ratcliffe’s trip routine. Yet there has still been no official word from either Moscow or Washington on what Ratcliffe discussed with Russian officials.
Russian and foreign experts, for their part, consider the CIA director’s trip to Russia a highly unusual event. Citing senior, well-placed sources, Western outlets have offered their own explanations for why Ratcliffe went to Moscow.
Here are the leading theories:
- The Wall Street Journal and Politico: Ratcliffe went to Moscow to warn the Kremlin against attacking NATO countries — in particular Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. He also urged Russian authorities to scale back military and economic aid to Iran, which is at war with the United States.
- The New York Times: Ratcliffe met with Alexander Bortnikov, director of Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB); shared with him “his grim assessment” of Russia’s position in the war against Ukraine; and urged Moscow to open peace talks.
- The Washington Post: Ratcliffe went to Moscow because the Kremlin believes the conflict with Iran has left the United States “exhausted and unable to intervene” in Russia’s war against Ukraine. Sources cited by the paper said the point of the visit was to tell Russian officials that this is not the case, and that a major escalation of the conflict with Ukraine would “only push Trump toward Zelensky.”

items.body_text:
How to prepare your mobile phone for the Russian border: Meduza’s complete survival guide
A growing number of Russians living overseas who return to the country temporarily are reporting psychological pressure and mobile-phone searches at the Russian border. These inspections can result in consequences far more severe than travel delays, including criminal charges and incarceration. Understanding your personal risk and exactly how to prepare your devices for the trip can be difficult, as the internet is full of fragmented and conflicting advice. Working with a lawyer and a cybersecurity expert, Meduza prepared this detailed guide answering the main questions on the topic. Is it true that FSB officers have a special machine that can find anything on a device? Do you have the right to refuse to unlock your phone, and is there any point in refusing? And what’s the most effective preparation strategy?
What you need to know before reading
Everything in this guide lowers the odds of trouble and limits the amount of your data that security officials could obtain. But in some cases, preparing your devices won’t matter at all, because the decision has already been made before you ever reach the passport control counter.
That’s true for anyone already facing a criminal case or a pretrial restriction imposed in absentia; anyone Russia’s Federal Financial Monitoring Service (Rosfinmonitoring) has placed on its list of “terrorists and extremists”; anyone who works for an organization designated “undesirable” or “extremist”; and anyone who has publicly criticized the war or the authorities. If you fall into any of these categories, the only advice experts offer is: don’t go.
We understand that trips to Russia are usually driven by serious reasons — a loved one’s illness, for example. But you should make that decision only after talking to a lawyer.
This article’s main takeaways
If you don’t have time to read the whole guide, if your trip is coming up fast, or if you just want to check how prepared you are, run through the experts’ advice below. If any point raises questions, the following sections explain it in more detail.
- Ideally, buy a separate phone for the trip — you likely won’t be able to fully clean your personal one.
- Also get a separate SIM card to use only for the trip.
- Try to make the new phone look used. Carry it around for a couple of weeks so the battery goes through several full charge-and-discharge cycles, take photos of food and animals, follow a few entertainment channels, and add close contacts to your contact list.
- Pay especially close attention to your contact list — it shouldn’t include Ukrainian numbers or numbers belonging to people being persecuted in Russia.
- Don’t log in to your old accounts — email, Telegram, and so on — on the new phone. Create separate ones for the trip.
- Never install foreign banking apps on the new phone — they will be checked if it comes to that.
- If you don’t have time to make the new phone look used, take it empty: it’s better to come up with an explanation for FSB officers than to take your chances on what they might find on your primary device.
- Turn off Face ID and fingerprint unlock before the trip.
- Set a long alphanumeric password instead of a four-digit PIN, and update the operating system to the latest version. These are the only steps that actually slow down a forensic extraction system.
- Keep in mind that checks can happen both when you enter the country and when you leave — prepare your phone just as carefully either way.
- Don’t be afraid to “say goodbye” to your device. It could be confiscated, and that’s not the main risk — what should worry you is the possibility that you won’t be able to leave Russia if something “wrong” turns up.

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah 
Mojtaba Khamenei

The message, issued to mark the birthday of Islam's Prophet Muhammad, also called for unity, mutual defence against âenemiesâ and cooperation among Muslims worldwide, Reuters reported.
Khamenei remains out of public view

His health and whereabouts have remained the subject of speculation in recent months. A video released earlier this month showed archival footage of Mojtaba Khamenei participating in a religious academic discussion with clerics.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had dismissed speculation about Khamenei's health, saying earlier this month that he was âcompletely healthyâ, according to Iran's ISNA news agency.
Message comes amid war and economic pressure
The latest message comes as Iran continues to face the economic impact of the war with the US and sanctions imposed by Washington.
In a written statement attributed to Khamenei on Saturday, Iran's supreme leader called on the government to address economic and livelihood challenges, including inflation, unemployment and the management of prices and markets.
âThere is a need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services,â he said.
Iranian leaders have also maintained that Tehran would continue to pursue both diplomacy and defence.
In a statement on Saturday, the Iranian government described diplomacy and defence as âtwo complementary, coordinated and inseparable wingsâ for protecting the country's national interests, security and territorial integrity.

items.title: British woman fatally stabbed at Germany train station; suspect detained
items.summary: The woman, who was attacked at the Rosenheim train station, was taken to a nearby hospital, where she died due to serious injuries, Rosenheim police said
items.body_text:
A man suspected of fatally stabbing a 31-year-old British woman with a knife early Sunday morning (August 30, 2026) in the southern German town of Rosenheim was detained, authorities said.
The woman, who was attacked at the Rosenheim train station, was taken to a nearby hospital, where she died due to serious injuries, Rosenheim police said.
Federal police officers, called to the scene, detained the suspect right after the stabbing.
Police identified him as a 27-year-old German man from the nearby county of Furstenfeldbruck.
They did not release the names of the victim or the suspect in line with German privacy rules and said they were still investigating the circumstances and motive behind the crime.
They asked any witnesses to come forward and asked whether anybody had witnessed “an argument or a physical altercation” in the early hours of Saturday night into Sunday at the train station.
Published - August 30, 2026 06:03 pm IST

items.title: Nepal flash floods LIVE: Death toll reaches 768; rescuers drill through debris towards trapped tunnel workers
items.summary: Nepal warns of rising water levels in Bhotekoshi River as combined death toll surges to 784
items.body_text:
The death toll from flash floods in Nepal rose to 768, even as over 2,500 people remain missing, its disaster authority said on Sunday (August 30, 2026), as rescue efforts entered a fifth day. Chinese state media had earlier confirmed 16 dead in Tibet and 546 people missing. That takes the overall toll to 784 dead and 3,044 missing.
Bodies have been recovered from eight affected districts as rescuers race against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded on the fifth day since the disaster.
Also read | A shared disaster, beyond borders and geopolitics
Meanwhile, rescuers in Nepal and China battled through leg-sucking mud, as well as the threat of rising rivers and a newly formed lake, to search for thousands missing after a deadly wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayas, engulfing entire villages.
Nepal said it had begun the grim task of burying some of the hundreds of bodies on Sunday, after first taking DNA samples so that families could later reclaim them and perform traditional funeral rites once they had been identified.
(With inputs from agencies)

items.title: ‘Mother was swept away’: Nepal flood survivors cling to hope amid search for missing
items.summary: Families crowded hospitals searching for missing relatives as rescuers continued digging through mud and debris amid intermittent rainfall and renewed concerns over rising river levels
items.body_text:
Five-year-old Ishara Tamang lies in a hospital bed in Kathmandu, injured and separated from her family, after surviving the flash floods that devastated Rasuwa district on the Nepal-Tibet border.
She was rescued from the floodwaters in Khalte, a village in Rasuwa, after being trapped in a net, the Onlinekhabar news portal reported. Ishara told hospital staff: “Mother was swept away. I jumped and moved forward, then got trapped in the net.” The August 26 floods - which travelled downstream through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river system - have left a trail of destruction across northern and central Nepal, with the death toll crossing 700 on Sunday (August 30, 2026), while around 2,500 people are still missing.
Nepal flash floods LIVE updates on August 30, 2026
Families, on Sunday (August 30, 2026), crowded hospitals searching for missing relatives as rescuers continued digging through mud and debris amid intermittent rainfall and renewed concerns over rising river levels.
Ishara was with her mother when the flood struck. The child was swept away, tried to move forward and became trapped in a net before rescuers found her and brought her to safety.
She was not accompanied by a family member at the hospital. When she regained consciousness, she was able to tell medical staff her name and said her father was in Kathmandu. Her mother’s whereabouts remained unknown, the report said.
In another rescue operation at the Timure border town, an Armed Police Force team searching the wreckage of a collapsed security post heard a child's cries.
The Kathmandu Post newspaper reported that the rescuers dug through the debris and pulled out a six-year-old girl alive.
The team had initially been unable to see anyone beneath the collapsed structure, but heard the child's crying while searching the site, said the report quoting a senior security official.
The girl was taken to the border outpost in Timure, but bad weather prevented her immediate evacuation to a hospital, the newspaper reported, without sharing her identity.
In another rescue operation, a five-year-old girl rescued alive from beneath rubble two days after the devastating flash floods has been reunited with her parents in a Kathmandu hospital, the BBC reported.
Manisha was found near Syabrubesi in Rasuwa district on Friday (August 28, 2026) after rescuers searching for survivors thought they heard a cat trapped under the debris. A senior official with Nepal’s Armed Police Force told the BBC that rescuers began clearing the rubble and found the girl trapped underneath. It took about two hours to pull her out.
Manisha was barely responsive, and bad weather prevented her immediate evacuation by helicopter. Rescuers took her to a force camp, gave her water and later fed her boiled rice water after she regained consciousness.
She was flown to Kathmandu on Saturday (August 29, 2026) afternoon and admitted to the Teaching Hospital’s paediatric emergency department. On Sunday (August 30, 2026), the hospital said she was recovering. The BBC reported that Manisha has since been reunited with her parents.
At Timure, businessman Nischal Tripathi escaped the flood by running from a building as water and mud surged through the settlement.
According to Onlinekhabar, Mr. Tripathi had been in Timure for about 20 days on business and was on the fifth floor of a building when he felt it shake. He ran downstairs and jumped from around the second floor before reaching the mountainside.
Mr. Tripathi and others then fled into the forest. They spent the night on noodles and biscuits before moving to a goat shed, where around 150 to 200 people gathered along with Nepali Army personnel, Onlinekhabar reported.
Mr. Tripathi told the news portal that his brother, five or six members of his team and seven truck drivers remained out of contact. “Only one or two houses appear to have survived,” he said, describing the destruction.

जेन-जी प्रदर्शन के दौरान दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर से पीएम मोदी को गाली देने वाली 15 साल की नाबालिग का एक वीडियो आम आदमी पार्टी ने पोस्ट किया है। 39 सेकेंड्स के वीडियो में उसने कहा है- मेरी जिंदगी नर्क बन गई है। मुझे हर जगह टॉर्चर किया जा रहा है।
मेरे पास जो था, वो सब चला गया मेरा। न मैं कहीं जा सकती हूं। न कहीं रह सकती हूं। ने मेरे पास कोई फ्रीडम है। मुझे हर जगह अपना मुंह छिपा-छिपाकर रहना पड़ रहा है। इसके बाद पीएम के लिए आपत्तिजनक शब्द कहे।
FIR दर्ज होने के बाद माफी मांगी थी
23 जुलाई को छात्रों के प्रदर्शन के दौरान वीडियो में नाबालिग पीएम मोदी के खिलाफ आपत्तिजनक भाषा का इस्तेमाल करते नजर आई थीं। उसके खिलाफ गाजियाबाद की रहने वाली स्मृति सिंह ने नोएडा के एक्सप्रेसवे पुलिस स्टेशन में शिकायत दर्ज कराई थी।
इसके बाद पुलिस ने 30 जुलाई को नाबालिग के खिलाफ जानबूझकर अपमान करने, सार्वजनिक उपद्रव फैलाने और मानहानि के आरोप में केस दर्ज किया था। कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने इस कार्रवाई का विरोध किया था।
एफआईआर दर्ज होने के बाद नाबालिग ने माफी मांग ली थी। हाथ जोड़ते हुए कहा था- मैंने जो किया, वह माफी के लायक नहीं था। मैं सिर्फ 15 साल की हूं। यह मेरी पहली और आखिरी गलती है। मैं दोबारा ऐसा नहीं कहूंगी। मुझे अपने किए पर शर्मिंदगी है। मैं किसी से नजर नहीं मिला पा रही हूं। प्लीज, मुझे माफ कर दीजिए। पूरी खबर पढ़ें...
36 दिन चला CJP का प्रदर्शन, प्रधान के इस्तीफे से खत्म हुआ
15 मई को सुप्रीम कोर्ट के चीफ जस्टिस ने बेरोजगारों को लेकर कॉकरोच वाला कमेंट किया। इसके खिलाफ सोशल मीडिया पर 16 मई को कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी बनी। 6 जून को इसे बनाने वाले अभिजीत दीपके भारत आए। 20 जून से जंतर-मंतर पर प्रदर्शनकारी NEET पेपर लीक के मुद्दे को लेकर धरने पर बैठे।
36 दिन तक चला यह आंदोलन 25 जुलाई को शिक्षा मंत्री धर्मेंद्र प्रधान को इस्तीफे के बाद खत्म हुआ। प्रधान ने एक बयान में इस्तीफे की घोषणा करते हुए कहा- पिछले 10 दिन की घटनाओं ने उन्हें बहुत दुखी किया है और यह मुद्दा व्यक्तिगत प्रतिष्ठा का मामला नहीं है।
इसके अलावा, छात्रों के साथ अनशन पर बैठे सोनम वांगचुक ने भी 26 दिन की भूख हड़ताल सरकार के आश्वासन के बाद खत्म कर दी थी।

आतंकी पोर्न वेबसाइट्स पर सीक्रेट चैटिंग कर रहे:पाकिस्तान में बैठे हैंडलर्स इसी पर मैसेज भेजते; एन्क्रिप्टेड ऐप्स के जरिए पहचान छिपाने की कोशिश
- कॉपी लिंक
पाकिस्तान में बैठे आतंकी सीक्रेट चैटिंग के लिए अब पोर्न वेबसाइट्स का इस्तेमाल कर रहे हैं। सुरक्षा अधिकारियों ने रविवार को बताया कि आतंकी संगठन और पाकिस्तान की खुफिया एजेंसी ISI इसका सबसे ज्यादा यूज कर रहे हैं।
आतंकी इसके जरिए जम्मू-कश्मीर में भर्ती किए गए लोगों तक मैसेज पहुंचा रहे हैं। ताकि सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफॉर्म पर निगरानी से बचा जा सके।
अधिकारियों ने बताया कि इन पोर्नोग्राफी प्लेटफॉर्म पर रियल-टाइम चैट टूल मौजूद होते हैं। जो आसपास डेट (पार्टनर) ढूंढने में मदद करने के नाम पर काम करते हैं। लेकिन हैंडलर्स इनका इस्तेमाल आतंकी गतिविधि के लिए कर रहे हैं।
आतंकी टोर नेटवर्क का भी इस्तेमाल कर रहे
सुरक्षा एजेंसियों ने कई खास डिजिटल टूल्स की जांच शुरू की है। आतंकी हैंडलर कोटेक्स और कोनियन जैसे टोर आधारित मैसेजिंग ऐप्स का भी इस्तेमाल कर रहे हैं।
ये ऐप्स डेटा को एन्क्रिप्टेड नोड्स के जरिए भेजते हैं और यूजर की पहचान छिपाते हैं। अधिकारियों के मुताबिक, भारत में कोनियन की एपीके फाइल तक पहुंच पर रोक है।
एपीके यानी एंड्रॉयड पैकेज किट वह फाइल फॉर्मेट है, जिसका इस्तेमाल एंड्रॉयड ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम मोबाइल ऐप्स को बांटने और इंस्टॉल करने के लिए करता है।
चीन, फ्रांस के ऐप भी आतंकियों के फेवरेट
इसके अलावा, आतंकी फ्रांस बेस्ड ऐसे ऐप का भी इस्तेमाल कर रहे हैं, जिसमें सिम कार्ड या फोन नंबर की जरूरत के बिना एंड-टू-एंड एन्क्रिप्टेड मैसेजिंग की सुविधा है। इससे यूजर की पहचान करना मुश्किल हो जाता है।
एजेंसियां वियतनाम आधारित ऐप्स की भी निगरानी कर रही हैं। इसके साथ ही मूनचैट जैसे गुमनाम प्लेटफॉर्म भी जांच के दायरे में हैं।
मूनचैट में पीजीपी-एन्क्रिप्टेड वर्जन शामिल हैं, जिनके चीनी मूल के होने का शक है और इनमें पारंपरिक रजिस्ट्रेशन की जरूरत नहीं होती।
मूनचैट के कई वर्जन ऐसे हैं, जिनका इस्तेमाल आसपास मौजूद सिंगल लोगों को खोजने के लिए किया जाता है।
भारत में पोर्न एप्स VPN के जरिए डाउनलोड हो रहे
अधिकारियों के मुताबिक, भारत में पोर्नोग्राफी वाले कई ऐप्स पर रोक है। इसके बावजूद इन्हें वर्चुअल प्राइवेट नेटवर्क यानी वीपीएन के जरिए गैरकानूनी तरीके से डाउनलोड किया जा रहा है।
VPN इंटरनेट पर एक सुरक्षित और एन्क्रिप्टेड कनेक्शन बनाता है। यह इंटरनेट प्रोटोकॉल एड्रेस छिपाता है और ऑनलाइन ट्रैफिक को एन्क्रिप्ट करता है, जिससे ऑनलाइन गतिविधियों पर नजर रखना और डेटा तक पहुंचना मुश्किल हो जाता है।
2जी नेटवर्क पर भी चलने वाले ऐप्स का इस्तेमाल
सुरक्षा अधिकारियों ने पाया कि हैंडलर और घाटी में मौजूद आतंकी भर्ती किए गए लोग ऐसे खास ऐप्स पर निर्भर थे, जो धीमी 2जी या एज नेटवर्क स्पीड में भी काम करते हैं।
इनमें से कुछ ऐप्स पर रजिस्ट्रेशन के लिए यूजर को फोन नंबर या ईमेल तक देने की जरूरत नहीं होती।
नई रणनीति का खुलासा सुरक्षा बलों की विदेशी कंपनियों द्वारा बनाई गई वर्चुअल सिम के इस्तेमाल को रोकने की कोशिश के दौरान हुआ।
वर्चुअल सिम ऐसी तकनीक है, जो कंप्यूटर को फोन नंबर बनाने की सुविधा देती है। इन नंबरों का इस्तेमाल खास ऐप्स के जरिए स्मार्टफोन पर किया जा सकता है और इससे डिजिटल निशान बहुत कम बचते हैं।
इसका पहली बार खुलासा 2019 के पुलवामा आतंकी हमले की जांच के दौरान हुआ था। इस हमले में सीआरपीएफ के 40 जवानों की मौत हुई थी।

items.title: India and Uzbekistan elevate strategic ties, plan long-term uranium supply
items.summary: India and Uzbekistan elevate strategic ties plan longterm uranium supply
items.body_text:
India and Uzbekistan elevate strategic ties, plan long-term uranium supply
Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the decision after talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The move coincides with the 15th anniversary of the strategic partnership between the two countries.
India and Uzbekistan on Sunday elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and agreed to work towards a long-term uranium supply arrangement, as the two countries moved to expand cooperation in defence, trade, energy and connectivity.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the upgrade after talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The decision coincides with the 15th anniversary of the strategic partnership between the two countries.
“On this special occasion, we have decided to elevate our relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. We will move forward by setting concrete goals within this new framework,” PM Modi said at a joint press conference.
The two countries will establish a Coordination Council led by their foreign ministers to guide different areas of bilateral cooperation. Their existing joint commission will also be upgraded from the secretary level to the ministerial level.
The Prime Minister described Uzbekistan as being “at the heart of Central Asia” and central to India’s engagement with the region.
DEFENCE TIES, ZERO TOLERANCE ON TERROR
PM Modi said close defence and security cooperation between India and Uzbekistan reflected the deep mutual trust between the two countries.
“In the coming years, we will promote direct linkages, co-production and co-development between the defence industries of our two countries,” he said.
The Prime Minister said India and Uzbekistan viewed terrorism, extremism and separatism as major challenges to regional stability and shared a policy of zero tolerance towards them.
TRADE TARGET SET AT $5 BILLION
PM Modi said bilateral trade had crossed $1 billion, with the two countries now aiming to raise it to $5 billion by 2030. He said they would work systematically to improve market access, connectivity, banking and payment systems.
India and Uzbekistan will also organise a joint business summit and explore infrastructure projects that create opportunities for both countries.
“We will work together to enhance win-win cooperation in infrastructure development,” PM Modi said, adding that collaboration in digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, space and nuclear energy was making the relationship future-ready.
As part of the push for deeper energy ties, the two sides are working to establish a long-term arrangement for the supply of uranium to India.
New Delhi has been exploring uranium imports from Uzbekistan to support nuclear power generation for civilian purposes. Clean energy was among the key areas discussed during PM Modi’s two-day visit.
‘TIES MUST GO BEYOND NATIONAL CAPITALS’
PM Modi said the partnership should not remain limited to New Delhi and Tashkent. India and Uzbekistan will establish partnerships between their cities and states to widen engagement at the local level.
Highlighting the similarities between the development goals of the two countries, he said youth, innovation, inclusive growth and modern technology were central to both “New Uzbekistan” and “Viksit Bharat 2047”.

items.title: How a Nepali teacher's quick thinking saved 1,643 children from monster floods
items.summary: How a Nepali teachers quick thinking saved children from monster floods
items.body_text:
How a Nepali teacher's quick thinking saved 1,643 children from monster floods
A Nepali school principal rushed 1,643 children to safety after a warning that muddy floodwaters were surging towards their school. His split-second decision came as a glacier-triggered disaster tore through the region and left hundreds dead.
"He said the village was gone: taken by the river. He told me to run."
The warning came at 9:20 am on Wednesday from a friend to Rajendra Dawadi, principal of Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Nepal's Trishuli Valley. He had 1,643 children in and around the three-storey school as a devastating flash flood, triggered by a glacier collapse, tore through mountain river systems, killing over 750 people in Nepal and 16 in Tibet.
Buildings, bridges and power stations were swept away as torrents of rock, ice, mud and debris surged through the region. About 2,498 people remain missing in Nepal, while another 546 are missing in Tibet's Gyirong County, according to the latest figures.
With the floodwaters rising rapidly, Dawadi, a 47-year-old English teacher, had just minutes to act. He was responsible for the children at the school in flood-hit Nuwakot that morning, and their safety now depended on his decision.
Dawadi initially thought the school was safe. Built of concrete and about 60 metres above the river, it stood on the same level as the steel bridge linking the village to the eastern bank, The Times reported.
Then a parent rushed in with a more alarming message: the water was rising fast.
Dawadi rang the school bell and ordered teachers to evacuate the classrooms. He called the school bus drivers, telling all but one to turn back. Then he saw the bus he could not reach crossing the bridge.
By then, the children were beginning to realise they were in danger. One girl suffered a panic attack and was taken uphill on a motorbike. The others fled on foot, with Dawadi following behind, according to The Times.
The children eventually took shelter beneath a bodhi tree as the floodwaters swept away their school buildings.
Dawadi's quick thinking saved 1,643 children and all but one member of the teaching staff. Social history teacher Santos Pariyar, 32, was washed away after returning to his rented room beside the river to cook breakfast. The school's janitor, Sultan Lama, was also killed after returning to close the doors.
'WHAT ELSE COULD I DO?'
Locals have called Dawadi a hero for saving the children. But he is less convinced. "What else could I do?" he said while surveying the muddy ruins where the school once stood.
The flash flood was triggered by a huge chunk of ice and rock that broke away from Langtang Lirung peak and plunged about 1,200 metres into the steep upper gorge of the Lhende Khola river near the Tibet border.
Daniel Shugar, a geomorphologist at the University of Calgary, estimated the mass covered nearly 50 acres, roughly the size of Green Park in London.
The region has endured tragedy before. In April 2015, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake that killed 8,962 people across South Asia triggered an avalanche that buried all 300 residents of Langtang, which falls in flood-ravaged Rasuwa district.

items.title: Want to become UP CM? Bring Asaduddin Owaisi: AIMIM to Akhilesh Yadav
items.summary: Want to become UP CM Bring Asaduddin Owaisi AIMIM to Akhilesh Yadav
items.body_text:
Want to become UP CM? Bring Asaduddin Owaisi: AIMIM to Akhilesh Yadav
AIMIM leader Shadab Chauhan said Akhilesh Yadav would need Asaduddin Owaisi's support to become Uttar Pradesh chief minister. His remarks sharpen the contest among Opposition parties over minority and backward-caste votes in the state.
The All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) has taken a swipe at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, saying he would need the support of AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi if he wants to become Uttar Pradesh chief minister.
AIMIM leader Shadab Chauhan said Yadav's political strategy would remain incomplete without Owaisi and claimed that the “A” in the Samajwadi Party's PDA — referring to the party's formulation of “Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak” — should stand for Asaduddin Owaisi.
Chauhan made the remarks while advising Yadav on his political strategy and the prospects of the Opposition ahead of the next Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.
“If Akhilesh Yadav wants to become the chief minister, he will have to take the support of Asaduddin Owaisi,” Chauhan said.
He further claimed that Muslims had made up their minds that their votes should contribute to electing a leader who represents their interests.
AIMIM TAKES AIM AT AKHILESH'S PDA
Taking a direct dig at the Samajwadi Party's PDA strategy, Chauhan said Yadav could not hope to return to power unless the alliance's “A” also represented Asaduddin Owaisi.
“Until there is ‘A’ for Asaduddin Owaisi in Akhilesh Yadav's PDA, he cannot even dream of coming to power,” Chauhan said.
The AIMIM leader's remarks come amid efforts by political parties in Uttar Pradesh to consolidate different social and electoral groups ahead of the next Assembly polls. The Samajwadi Party has sought to build its political strategy around backward classes, Dalits and minority communities.
Chauhan claimed that AIMIM remained an important political option for Yadav and suggested that cooperation with Owaisi's party would be necessary if the SP chief wanted to strengthen his electoral prospects.
AIMIM LEADER ATTACKS IMRAN MASOOD
Chauhan also targeted Congress MP Imran Masood, accusing him of praising the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) despite being part of the Opposition.
He said Masood was praising the BJP in a manner that suggested he had effectively aligned himself with the ruling party.
Chauhan also urged Akhilesh Yadav to focus on his own social base, claiming that sections of it were moving towards the BJP.
The remarks highlight the continuing political competition among Opposition parties in Uttar Pradesh, particularly over minority and backward-caste votes. AIMIM has previously sought to expand its electoral footprint in the state, while the Samajwadi Party has positioned itself as a major Opposition force against the BJP.
Chauhan's comments are likely to add another layer to the political debate over Opposition unity and vote consolidation in Uttar Pradesh.

items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav.
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday condemned the alleged rape and murder of a six-year-old girl in Greater Noida, calling the incident "spine-chilling" and questioning the law and order situation in Uttar Pradesh.
 
In a post on X, the SP chief said, "The case of the rape and murder of a 6-year-old innocent girl from the minority community in Greater Noida is spine-chilling. It has instilled fear in the parents of every daughter across the entire state regarding the safety of their little girls. The question is, how has the law and order situation in the state become so lax that criminals no longer fear those in power?"
Akhilesh Yadav added, "The answer to this question lies in the fact that the way crimes by people from the same community in power are being suppressed and concealed is emboldening other criminals as well."
He further alleged that corruption had affected the functioning of the police and accused some officers of colluding with criminals.
 
"The BJP has expanded the scope of its corruption to such an extent that it has forced the police to become complicit too, and taking advantage of this, some corrupt police officers are colluding with criminals to shelter their sins. Utterly condemnable! Justice must be done!!!" Yadav added.
 
A six-year-old girl was allegedly abducted and murdered in Greater Noida's Haldoni village after she went missing from home on August 28. Police recovered her body stuffed in a sack and arrested a suspect after tracing CCTV footage and other leads. The accused, identified as Balraj, was later killed in a police encounter, officials said.
 
The incident came to light after the girl's family filed a complaint on Friday, August 28, reporting that she had gone missing from home without informing anyone. Police registered an FIR and launched a search operation.

items.summary: The deceased has been identified as Vuke Shirisha, who was working as a nurse at Prime Care Hospital in Thukkuguda and was residing in the residential rooms of the hospital along with her friends, according to Shamshabad Police.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. Representative image.
A 21-year-old nurse was found dead under suspicious circumstances in a room in the Pahadishareef area here, with police suspecting that she may have been assaulted by unidentified persons.
 
The deceased has been identified as Vuke Shirisha, who was working as a nurse at Prime Care Hospital in Thukkuguda and was residing in the residential rooms of the hospital along with her friends, according to Shamshabad Police.
 
According to the police, Shirisha was a native of Chowtigudem village in Mulakalapalli mandal of Bhadradri Kothagudem district. She had come to Hyderabad around seven months ago along with her friend Kaka Sarika, also aged 21 and working as a nurse at Prime Care Hospital.
 
According to Shamshabad Police, on Saturday at around 2:30 pm, Sarika telephoned the complainant and informed her that Shirisha had not come out of her room since morning. Despite knocking on the door several times, Shirisha did not respond.
 
The police said that Shirisha's friends subsequently entered the room through a window and found her lying dead with bleeding injuries on her face. The complainant then reached the room and observed Shirisha's body.
 
Based on the complaint, it was suspected that some unidentified persons might have assaulted Shirisha and killed her by beating her with an unknown object, police said.
 
A police team, along with the clues team, reached the spot and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death.
 
"The deceased has been identified as Shirisha, working as a nurse in a private hospital. We have reached the spot and are currently investigating the matter. We will provide further details later. The body has been shifted for post-mortem examination," Shamshabad Police said.
 
Further details are awaited.

Image Credit: AI. Representative image.
West Bengal Police have uncovered a cross-border kidney smuggling racket after vulnerable youths were allegedly targeted with promises of jobs in other states. Investigators have found fake Indian identity documents, private hospital papers and a rate chart linked to kidney requirements. Now, in a significant development that exposes the organised nature of the racket, the Special Task Force has arrested Bangladeshi national Russel Ahmed in Kolkata, whose name emerged during the interrogation of another accused.
The investigation took a major turn late on Saturday night when STF officers arrested Russel Ahmed from the Baguihati area on the northern outskirts of Kolkata.
After his arrest, Ahmed was handed over to officers of Bidhannagar South Police Station under Bidhannagar City Police in the North 24 Parganas district.
Police are now questioning him to establish the identities of his alleged local associates and understand how the network operated.
Ahmed is scheduled to be produced before a district court in North 24 Parganas later on Sunday.
Ahmed's name came to the investigators after the STF arrested another alleged member of the kidney smuggling racket.
Prabhas Mondal was arrested on August 18 following a complaint filed by the father of a young victim. The investigation found that the victim had undergone an operation involving one kidney and had received only a nominal amount of money.
During Mondal's interrogation, investigators reportedly came across Ahmed's name.
Police then began examining Ahmed's alleged role in a network that operated across India and Bangladesh.
Investigators believe the alleged racket mainly targeted young people from financially backward families.
The operators allegedly approached vulnerable youths with promises of jobs in other states. Instead of the employment they were promised, police say the victims were taken for kidney operations.
A state police officer described how the alleged racket operated.
“The racket operators took these youth to other states promising jobs. There their kidneys were operated on, and victims were paid a nominal amount against that,” he said.
The investigation is now focused on identifying everyone involved in recruiting the victims and arranging their movement and medical procedures.
One of the most important pieces of evidence recovered during the investigation was a rate chart reportedly found in Ahmed's possession.
Police also recovered papers from private hospitals in different states. The documents contained details about kidney requirements at the hospitals.
Investigators are examining these documents to determine how the alleged network connected victims with medical facilities and whether more people were involved.
This is not the first time Ahmed has faced police action.
Records show that he was arrested by the Delhi Police in 2024 for his alleged involvement in a kidney smuggling racket.
Delhi Police had then discovered that Ahmed had allegedly entered India illegally and managed to obtain Indian identity documents.
These documents included an Aadhaar card and a PAN card.
He was also found to have been living on rent in West Bengal for a long period, according to the earlier investigation.

Police suspect that the operation involved multiple people performing different roles, from identifying vulnerable youths to arranging their travel and connecting them with medical facilities.
The documents recovered from Ahmed may help investigators establish the extent of these alleged links.
Ahmed's interrogation is expected to focus on his alleged associates and the people connected with the racket.

items.title: Who is Kajal Sheikh, TMC goon and sand mafia kingpin who was snubbed by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari in Birbhum
items.summary: Social media has been rife with misleading claims that Suvendu Adhikari interacted with the notorious TMC MLA Kajal Sheikh and was somehow planning to rehabilitate him into the BJP or the Ritabrata Banerjee-led TMC faction.
items.body_text:
On Saturday (29th August), West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited the Birbhum district, prayed at the Tarapith, and held an administrative meeting in Rampurhat. The local Trinamool Congress MLA from the Hasan constituency, Kajal Sheikh aka Fayezul Haque, was also present at that gathering (as per protocol).
Since then, social media has been rife with claims that Adhikari interacted with the notorious TMC MLA and was somehow planning to rehabilitate him into the BJP or the Ritabrata Banerjee-led TMC faction.
The disinformation came days after Kajal Sheikh resigned from the post of Zilla Parishad Sabhadhipati (Chairperson). Earlier, several members of the Trinamool Congress moved a no-confidence motion against him at the Zilla Parishad.
Nonetheless, his presence at the official event sparked intense speculations about alleged acceptance of his antics by the BJP and Suvendu Adhikari in particular.
But a careful persual of the videos from the administrative meeting in Rampurhat shows a starkly different picture. While it is true that Kajal Sheikh stood behind Suvendu Adhikari during his press briefing, it is evident that the Chief Minister had avoided him throughout the meeting.
This was despite multiple attempts by the TMC leader to strike a conversation with Adhikari. It is highly unlikely that Kajal Sheikh will ever find refuge in the BJP (as some people are speculating online).

You carefully used one screenshot from the entire video to show Kajal Sheikh standing right behind Suvendu.

About 10 days earlier, BJP State President Samik Bhattarcharjee pointed how how Kajal Sheikh is considered a ‘miscreant‘ by his own party. “Who is Kajal Sheikh? Will our State be remembered for this kind of a man?”
It must be mentioned that the TMC MLA had initially joined the Ritabrata faction but later moved away after his arch rival Anubrata Mondal went to that side.
Their rivalary goes decades back, with each striving to control the illegal multi-million rupee businesses of riverbed sand extraction and quarry stones in the Nanoor region and greater Birbhum district.
A 2016 report by the India Today reads –
“The sand mafia was once close to the Left parties, now it has become a battleground for two TMC satraps.One of the alleged warlords, Kajal, is the younger brother of Sheikh Shahnawaz, the face of the Trinamool in the region from 1998 to 2000, when the party was struggling to get a toehold in this red bastion. On July 27, 2000, Shahnawaz and Kajal planned the first-ever village takeover operation in Nanoor.
It was a fierce and bloody skirmish, since declared a ‘black day’ by the TMC. Kajal, with the backing of Shahnawaz, now the MLA from Ketugram in Burdwan, started dabbling in illegal sand mining and gradually took control of all 10 ghats in Nanoor’s lower belt. Gone underground for the last seven months, today he has arrest warrants out against him in 43 cases, including murder.”
Ahead of the 2016 election, Kajal Sheikh was accused of working for the Communist Party of India (Marxist) and facilitating the defection of more than 3000 Trinamool Congress workers. But within 3 years, his dynamics with the party supremo Mamata Banerjee and her nephew changed.
In May 2019, he was elevated to the position of Nanoor’s block executive President, much to the dislike of TMC leaders Anubrata Mondal and Firhad Hakim.
Around the time of the 2023 Panchayat election, Kajal Sheikh was prominently featured in posters pasted outside TMC party offices from Bolpur to Nanoor. It was clear that he was increasingly being favoured over the likes of Anubroto Mondal by the high command.

items.title: What is the Sonia Gandhi memoir controversy? As Congress plays ‘victim card’, publisher sets the record straight

items.body_text:
Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s upcoming memoir, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, was scheduled for international release on 10th November through Alfred A. Knopf, an imprint of Penguin Random House. However, the book has now become the centre of a political controversy after Penguin Random House India clarified that it is not the publisher of the memoir in India.
The clarification came on Friday, 28th August, after reports said Penguin Random House India had decided not to publish the book in India following the discrepancies in the fact-checking process.
Congress leaders have since alleged that the publisher was being pressured by the BJP to drop the memoir or seek changes in it. Penguin, however, has given a different explanation, saying that fact-checking and recommendations to authors are a normal part of the publishing process and that it had remained “willing and keen” to publish the book.
Congress alleges BJP pressure over Sonia Gandhi’s memoir
The controversy began after Penguin Random House India said it was not the publisher of ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ in India. The development came days after Alfred A. Knopf announced the international publication of the memoir.
Congress leaders quickly questioned the decision and alleged that the publisher was facing pressure because of the political content of the book. Senior Congress leader Ashok Gehlot asked why the Indian arm of Penguin would not publish the memoir when the book was being released internationally by its global imprint.
“Penguin Worldwide is ready to publish Smt. Sonia Gandhi Ji’s upcoming book worldwide in its original form, but Penguin Random House India wants changes made to launch it in India. After all, what is the reason or what pressure is there, that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?” Gehlot wrote on X.

He pointed to books such as Exam Warriors and books about the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) being published by Penguin India and alleged that the publishing house was now afraid of the ruling party.

items.title: As Modi govt extends humanitarian support to Nepal, read how India has helped 7 other disaster-torn countries in the past several years
items.summary: India has been among the first responders whenever its neighbours faced any natural disaster or any other calamity. It has stood by its Himalayan neighbour, which often faces natural disasters, through thick and thin.
items.body_text:
As the neighbouring Nepal is grappling with ravaging flash floods, India rose to the occasion and extended swift humanitarian assistance to the Himalayan country. India sent 62 tonnes of emergency aid to Nepal. India was the first country to provide physical assistance to the country in the middle of the deadly disaster.
As the death toll from the catastrophic flash floods rose above 600 and the number of missing people crossed 2000, India is actively taking part in the intensified rescue and relief operations, along with local authorities in Nepal. The Indian government is also sending consignments of relief material to Nepal.
On Saturday (29th August), India sent a fourth tranche of relief material to the country along with an 11-member team of doctors, paramedics and tunnel rescue specialists. According to the Indian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Indian government has also offered a tunnel rescue team, a medical team and personnel from its National Disaster Response Force to the disaster-hit country.
India has been among the first responders whenever its neighbours faced any natural disaster or any other calamity. It has stood by its Himalayan neighbour, which often faces natural disasters, through thick and thin. The Indian government extended similar support to Nepal following the devastating 2015 earthquake. The Indian government and the Indian armed forces launched a massive rescue and relief operation under Operation Maitri.
During the operation, the Indian Air Force and the Army flew 2223 sorties, rescued/evacuated about 11,200 people (including 780 casualties) to safer places and transported and dropped about 1700 tonnes of relief materials. Besides, the Rapid Action Medical Teams of the Indian armed forces extended medical assistance to 4762 injured.
Let’s take a look at how India has emerged as the ‘first responder’ and a true friend in need during times of crisis for not just its neighbours but also for countries located afar.
Operation Amistad after twin earthquakes in Venezuela
About two months ago, in June 2026, the South American country of Venezuela was jolted by twin apocalyptic earthquakes. The calamity caused horrifying visuals of high-rise buildings turning into rubble, huge loss of life and devastation. The Modi government presented an example of friendship and support in times of crisis by sending urgent humanitarian assistance to Venezuela under Operation Amistad (the word Amistad means friendship in Spanish).
Under the operation, which was part of India’s HADR mission, the Indian government dispatched two Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster aircraft carrying humanitarian relief supplies and a 41-member rescue team to assist the ongoing relief and rescue efforts in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. The relief consignment included a self-reliant Indian medical task force, an Indian Army Field Hospital unit with HADR pallets and medicines, 30 tonnes of relief supplies, 6 tonnes of medicines and medical equipment and two BHISHM cube portable hospitals.
The Indian government expressed solidarity with the people of Venezuela and assured the government of Venezuela of all possible assistance in the time of crisis.
Operation Sagar Bandhu after Cyclone Ditwah hit Sri Lanka
In November 2025, a deadly cyclone hit the coasts of Sri Lanka, causing massive floods, loss of life and destruction. The Indian government launched Operation Sagar Bandhu to provide urgent emergency assistance to the country. Two Indian Navy ships immediately transported food supplies and relief material, tents, tarpaulins, blankets, hygiene kits, ready-to-eat food items, medicines and surgical equipment to Colombo.
India deployed troops from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the Air Force to provide search, rescue, and relief assistance. items.title: Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
items.summary: The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
items.body_text:
Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
“I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline.
If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Advertisement
But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night.
Advertisement
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal.
Both countries had reason to step back from the brink. Nearly 72% of Canada’s goods exports last year went to the United States. And the Trump administration would be taking a risk by imposing a hefty new tariff — paid by U.S. importers who try to pass along the cost to consumers via higher prices — ahead of November’s midterm elections. U.S. voters are already frustrated with the high cost of living.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official, said before the delay was announced. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off-ramp here.’’
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has hit Canadian goods with tariffs — in a push to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. — and has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Trump has made tariffs the centrepiece of his second-term economic agenda. Last year, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he’d overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.
So Trump has looked for other legal authority to impose tariffs.
To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50% tariffs on products that account for about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States.
Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs, named for their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.
Section 338 tariffs have never been used before.
Section 338 authorises the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from count
