items.body_text:
Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s newly elected Prime Minister Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani called on his party’s leadership in Lahore on Sunday, with the latter stressing the need for the “immediate resolution” of issues of the Kashmiri people.
The huddle included PML-N President Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, according to a post on the party’s X account.
During the meeting, Nawaz shared a “reform plan for the first 100 days” of Gillani’s tenure, the post said, adding that it was aimed at strengthening health, education, cleanliness, infrastructure and other sectors.
He instructed Gillani to set AJK on the course of development, similar to Punjab, it said.
Gillani and Farooq expressed gratitude to the party’s senior leadership for “their confidence” in him, while the latter congratulated Gillani and Farooq.
A day earlier, the AJK PM had assured the business community and students that his government would restore internet services at educational institutions and remove restrictions on road links with Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa within the next few days.
PM Gillani had also expressed concern over the situation in Rawalakot, saying his government would make every effort to bring it under control.
AJK has been gripped by protests, including in Rawalakot, staged by the now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee that had announced a boycott of the recently held elections in the region over its demand for abolishing 12 seats reserved in the assembly for families displaced from occupied Kashmir.
The protests have been marred by violence while AJK continues to face internet disruptions.
Against this backdrop, the elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10.
Meanwhile, the third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.
However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.

items.body_text:
Published August 30, 2026
Liza Minnelli has opened up about the heartbreaking loss of her longtime friend Dolly Parton.
The actress admitted she is struggling to find the right words after Dolly died on Tuesday at the age of 80 following a short battle with cancer.
Liza, also 80, shared an emotional message on Instagram and said the news had left hearts “cracking all over the world.”
She remembered Dolly as a loving and supportive friend who was always there when things became difficult. The two stars had been friends for many years after meeting through their shared former agent, Sam Haskell.
Liza said they often supported each other and enjoyed spending time together after their concerts. She also hinted at the private moments they shared, including what she called their “spicy girl gossip” over meals.
The Cabaret star became so emotional that she admitted she was “struggling to get any words out.”
“My throat … my heart … are full,” she wrote.
Liza then shared a touching tribute written by Haskell, who remembered Dolly for her kindness, humor and generosity.
He said Dolly made people feel seen and used her success to help others.
For Liza, Dolly was not just a huge star. She was a close friend whose loss has left her heartbroken.

items.body_text:
Boat with around 270 people on board capsizes off North Cyprus; one dead
- By Reuters -
- Aug 30, 2026
NICOSIA: One person died after a boat with around 270 people on board capsized off North Cyprus on Sunday, Turkish Cypriot media reported.
Turkish Cypriot Transport Minister Erhan Arikli told Anadolu that one passenger had died when the ferry capsized. He said there were 267 people on board, 259 of whom were passengers and eight of whom were crew.
The privately owned ferry left the North Cyprus port of Kyrenia at 12:30 p.m. (0930 GMT) and immediately started taking on water for an unknown reason, Turkey’s state-run news agency Anadolu reported.
It was heading for the Turkish port of Tasucu in Mersin province in the eastern Mediterranean.
Those rescued from the vessel were taken to Kyrenia port to be transferred to hospitals, he added.
Murat Senkul, the mayor of Kyrenia, told broadcaster CNN Turk that 159 passengers on board the vessel had been reached.
Video footage showed people in red life jackets sitting or standing on top of the overturned vessel as authorities scrambled coastguard and private vessels for assistance to bring them to shore.
The Kibris newspaper reported that the vessel, which some reports said was a catamaran, began taking in water about four miles off the shore.

items.title: Dutch federation calls for football summit without Infantino
items.summary: Dutch federation calls for football summit without Infantino
items.body_text:
Dutch federation calls for football summit without Infantino
- By AFP -
- Aug 30, 2026
The Dutch football federation (KNVB) on Sunday said “FIFA needs new leadership” and that it would like to host a summit on the future of football’s world governing body which does not involve beleaguered president Gianni Infantino.
The 56-year-old Swiss has taken a pummelling over his now shelved FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to bring private investment into FIFA events, including the jewels in the crown, the men’s and women’s World Cups.
The KNVB in a letter to Aleksander Ceferin, president of European football’s governing body UEFA, said it had lost confidence in Infantino and things had to change radically within FIFA.
Infantino, who was elected in 2016 after Sepp Blatter stood down, had looked set to be re-elected unopposed to a fourth and final term in Rabat next March as he basked in the afterglow of a highly successful World Cup.
However, his botched proposal has resulted in a steady loss of support, the Norwegian FA demanded he resign and now the Dutch are envisaging an overhaul of FIFA without him at the helm.
Anyone wishing to challenge Infantino — CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is seen as the likeliest to put his name forward as Ceferin has declared himself a non-runner — has to do so by November 18.
“The KNVB no longer has confidence in the leadership of FIFA President Gianni Infantino,” read the KNVB statement.
“We believe FIFA needs new leadership from 2027 onwards. But a new President alone is not enough. The way FIFA is governed must change as well.”
‘Critical voices’
Although UEFA has led the fight against Infantino — their latest salvo threatening legal action accusing him of “criminal mismanagement” — KNVB insisted its proposal for change “should not be a European plan for the rest of the world”.
“We want to develop this new direction together with FIFA’s 211 Member Associations and the confederations from all parts of the world,” it said.
The KNVB listed three priorities: Good governance for a better balance of power, putting football’s social power at the heart of FIFA and investing more in football worldwide.
One of the main accusations aimed at Infantino has been a lack of transparency — contradicting what he had promised when first elected — and taking decisions unilaterally or with just a few of his inner circle involved.
Such was the case with the FFE when according to The New York Times five FIFA senior directors were apprised of the proposal at a meeting in a hotel in New York on the eve of the World Cup final in the US last month.
“FIFA should not depend on one individual. The President, FIFA Council, Congress and Secretary-General each have their own role and responsibility,” said the KNVB.
“The President represents and unites. The Council governs and supervises. Congress decides. The Secretary-General leads the organisation.
“This requires greater transparency, independent oversight and room for critical voices.”
To this end the KNVB said it would like all these matters to be discussed by “football associations and confederations”.
“We therefore propose an International Summit on the Future of FIFA,” it said.
“The KNVB is willing to host this summit in Amsterdam, a city with a special place in FIFA’s history.
“The 2027 presidential election should not only be about who leads FIFA.
“First, we need to determine what kind of FIFA we want. Then we can identify the leadership needed to deliver that change.”
UEFA when contacted by AFP preferred to keep its own counsel regarding the letter.
“We would prefer not to comment on correspondence that was intended to be private,” it said.
“We can only add that we have a long-standing, productive working relationship with KNVB, which we greatly appreciate.”

items.title: Julian Alvarez returns to Atletico team training after illness
items.summary: Julian Alvarez returns to Atletico team training after illness
items.body_text:
Julian Alvarez returns to Atletico team training after illness
- By AFP -
- Aug 30, 2026
MADRID: Wantaway Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez returned to group training on Sunday after recovering from the illness that kept him out of training earlier this week and Saturday’s 3-1 La Liga win over Sevilla.
With two days remaining before the transfer window closes at midnight Tuesday, the Argentina international is back with the squad as Barcelona continue to pursue his signature.
Atletico have repeatedly ruled out negotiating Alvarez’s departure to Barcelona, with director of football Mateu Alemany reiterating the club’s firm stance on Saturday.
“The club has been very clear and very firm,” Alemany told Movistar.
“The plan is very clear,” he continued. “(Alvarez) had a few days when he wasn’t feeling well, he already trained (by himself on Friday), and we hope he’ll reintegrate with us quickly and be available, I hope, for the next league match.”
Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said Thursday that Atletico would “not negotiate with Barcelona under any circumstances”, a position backed by the club’s board.
Spanish media have reported that a move to England could provide an alternative, although that option is not believed to appeal to 2022 World Cup winner Alvarez, who said this summer he would like to leave Atletico.
Alvarez was jeered by the club’s own supporters last weekend when he came on against Villarreal as a substitute, and he walked off down the tunnel by himself while his team-mates applauded Atletico’s fans.

items.title: Meghan Markle receives major warning about her UK return
items.summary: Royal couple once again faced their long-standing security concerns. The post Meghan Markle receives major warning about her UK return appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have often faced public attention and criticism because of their strained relationship with the royal family over the past few years.
After deciding to return to the United Kingdom, the royal couple once again faced their long-standing security concerns.
Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan Markle, stepped down from their royal duties in 2020. Since then, security has remained a major concern for the couple, with Harry fighting several legal battles over the issue in recent years.
Before their return to the United Kingdom, the Duchess of Sussex received a warning from longtime reporter Desalu-Vold, who expressed concern for Meghan’s well-being.
“Meghan, you haven’t even arrived and look at the chaos. For your mental health, emotional health and physical health, I would reconsider,” she said.
Royal commentator John McDermott said the couple could potentially play an important role within the royal family in the future.
“We are going to enter an interesting period of dueling courts. Harry is quite capable of championing the causes important to him without help from the Firm, as we have seen over the past few years,” he said.
McDermott said the bigger issue could be the possibility of a shortage of working royals during Prince William’s future reign.
“To me, the interesting piece is that Harry and Meghan could potentially help solve the future problem of there simply not being enough working royals, something that could become more apparent during William’s reign,” he said.
He added that if Prince Harry and Prince William are able to repair their relationship, the anniversary of Princess Diana’s death next year could provide an opportunity for reconciliation.
“Harry and Meghan could be major assets to the Crown. But in the short term, I do not anticipate a return to royal duties,” he suggested.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle reportedly arrived in the United Kingdom on a private jet on Aug. 26.

items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority has sealed three buildings in the city’s commercial hub for failing to comply with fire safety regulations, officials said Monday.
The Shaheed-e-Millat Secretariat, State Life Building and Trade Development Authority of Pakistan Building in Blue Area were shut down after inspections revealed unresolved safety deficiencies, according to the CDA’s Fire & Emergency Services Directorate.
CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf ordered the enforcement action and directed authorities to adopt a zero-tolerance approach toward fire safety violations.
“No building, institution or organization can be permitted to compromise the lives and safety of people by ignoring essential fire prevention and emergency response requirements,” Ashraf said in a statement.
The fire safety directorate has been conducting building inspections across Islamabad to identify violations related to emergency exits, firefighting equipment, evacuation plans and other life-safety measures.
The CDA’s Building Control Section has been instructed to give building administrations a prescribed timeframe to correct deficiencies.
Officials said the enforcement drive is not merely an inspection exercise but a practical initiative aimed at preventing avoidable loss of life and property.
Ashraf directed relevant departments to maintain close monitoring of compliance and ensure that safety observations are followed by corrective measures.
The CDA urged all government departments, public sector organizations, commercial establishments and private building owners to review their fire safety arrangements immediately.
“Fire safety is a collective responsibility,” Ashraf said. “Timely installation and maintenance of firefighting equipment, clear emergency exits, proper evacuation arrangements and compliance with safety protocols can save lives during an emergency.”
The authority said it would provide opportunities for building administrations to rectify deficiencies but warned that continued noncompliance would not be tolerated.
“Protection of human lives is the first and foremost responsibility,” the CDA said. “No compromise will be made on fire and life safety.”

items.title: Pakistan’s Dar arrives in Turkey after UK visit for regional security talks
items.summary: Deputy PM to attend R-4 meeting in Istanbul as US-Iran negotiations stall The post Pakistan’s Dar arrives in Turkey after UK visit for regional security talks appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Ishaq Dar, arrived in Istanbul on Sunday for official engagements after concluding a visit to the United Kingdom, the Foreign Office said.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 arrived in Istanbul, Türkiye today for official engagements.
He was received by Deputy Chief of Staff for Administration Brig. Gen. Şenol Varol, Pakistan’s Ambassador to Türkiye Dr. Yousaf Junaid,… pic.twitter.com/nT6AWjy1dR
— Ministry of Foreign Affairs – Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) August 30, 2026
Ishaq Dar was received at the airport by Turkish Deputy Chief of Staff for Administration Brig. Gen. Senol Varol, Pakistan’s Ambassador to Turkiye Dr. Yousaf Junaid, Turkish Foreign Ministry Ambassador Cihad Erginay and other senior Turkish officials, according to the Foreign Office.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 departed London for Istanbul, where he will undertake official engagements.
He concluded a successful official visit to the UK, during which he held meetings with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband,…
— Ministry of Foreign Affairs – Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) August 30, 2026
In an earlier statement, the Foreign Office said Dar had concluded “a successful official visit to the UK,” during which he met with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Minister of State for Pakistan Stephen Doughty, National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, International Maritime Organisation Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez and Commonwealth Secretary General Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey.
Dar also spoke with British parliamentarians of Pakistani origin and members of the Pakistani diaspora in the UK during the trip.
The Foreign Office did not provide specific details of Dar’s engagements in Turkiye. However, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan invited Dar earlier this month to the Regional-4 meeting, which includes Saudi Arabia and Egypt along with Turkiye and Pakistan. Dar accepted the invitation and confirmed his participation in the meeting, which was scheduled for August, the Foreign Office said.
The R-4 group, focused on regional security, emerged in March amid efforts for mediation between the U.S. and Iran. The Istanbul meeting is planned as negotiations remain stalled and the nearly six-month-old war continues with little sign of resolution.
The last R-4 meeting was held in June in Cairo, where the countries welcomed the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the U.S. and Iran. The first meeting took place in Riyadh on the sidelines of a consultative ministerial meeting, and the second was held in Islamabad; both occurred in March.

items.title: New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi
items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A new intellectual biography examining the life and critical scholarship of Iraq’s founding father of sociology, Ali Al-Wardi, has been released by the American University of Iraq, […] The post New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A new intellectual biography examining the life and critical scholarship of Iraq’s founding father of sociology, Ali Al-Wardi, has been released by the American University of Iraq, Baghdad (AUIB) Press.
Authored by Iraqi philosopher and translator Ali Hakim Saleh, the 300-page volume—titled Ali Al-Wardi: An Intellectual and Social Biography — traces Al-Wardi’s transformation into an urban modern intellectual (effendi), his systemic deconstruction of official state narratives, and the subsequent censorship and institutional marginalization he faced.
The biography structures Al-Wardi’s life and academic legacy across several defining phases:
- The Rise of the “Effendi” and the Public Intellectual: Tracing Al-Wardi’s emergence from traditional quarters to Western academia (earning his Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin in 1950) and his creation of a broad reading public outside elite scholarly circles.
- Theorizing the Iraqi Persona: Examining his foundational sociological frameworks, notably the dialectic between nomadism (Badawa) and urban civilization (Hadara), and the concept of psychological duality (Izdawajiyya) within Iraqi society.
- Direct Critique of Political Power: Analyzing Al-Wardi’s rigorous critique of state structures and his disruption of official historiography, most prominently captured in his multi-volume opus, Social Glimpses from Modern Iraqi History.
- State Friction, Censorship, and Disillusionment: Documenting the political suppression, academic sidelining, and personal disillusionment that followed his confrontation with authoritarian state narratives.
The publication has generated significant interest across Iraqi cultural and academic circles. Prominent author and University of Basra professor Louay Hamza Abbas praised the work as a major cultural milestone:
“The release of this book is a distinguished cultural event… not merely because it is the first comprehensive socio-intellectual biography of the father of Iraqi sociology, but for deeper considerations: No thinker remains from modern Iraqi culture to whom we return whenever calamity strikes us other than Ali Al-Wardi. They have all departed.”

items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official data released by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Sunday, August 30, 2026, shows that United States imports of Iraqi crude oil fell back to […] The post U.S. crude oil imports from Iraq drop to zero appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
U.S. crude oil imports from Iraq drop to zero
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official data released by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Sunday, August 30, 2026, shows that United States imports of Iraqi crude oil fell back to zero barrels per day (bpd) during the past week, down from an average of 6,000 bpd recorded the previous week.
The fluctuation follows an extended summer lull where direct crude shipments from Iraq to U.S. refiners remained largely suspended amid ongoing maritime transit adjustments in the Gulf.
Canada maintained its dominant position as the primary foreign crude supplier to American refineries, while Latin American and West African exporters filled the bulk of remaining import volume:
Note: The EIA recorded zero crude imports during the same reporting week from Algeria, Angola, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Kuwait, Norway, Russia, Trinidad and Tobago, and the United Kingdom.
Market Dynamics Behind the Zero-Import Week
- Shift to Asian Offtakers: The temporary drop to zero barrels for U.S.-bound cargoes contrasts with steady flows to Asia, where the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) directs the vast majority of Basrah Medium and Heavy grades to contracted refiners in India and China.
- Freight and Route Economics: Elevated maritime shipping rates and fluctuating Gulf routing lead U.S. Gulf Coast refiners to prioritize nearby heavy and medium crudes from Canada, Venezuela, Brazil, and Mexico.

items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government has successfully recovered public funds, financial assets, and real estate valued at over 1.359 trillion IQD (approximately $1.04 billion) during its anti-corruption campaign, […] The post Iraq recovers 1.35T dinars in anti-corruption drive appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Iraq recovers 1.35T dinars in anti-corruption drive
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government has successfully recovered public funds, financial assets, and real estate valued at over 1.359 trillion IQD (approximately $1.04 billion) during its anti-corruption campaign, “Sawlat al-Fajr” (Dawn Assault), government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi announced on Saturday, August 29, 2026.
In a statement delivered to Al Iraqiya News and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Aboudi revealed that the Federal Commission of Integrity has received more than 26,000 formal corruption reports, reflecting heightened institutional activity and public reporting.
Key Operational Milestones & Asset Recovery Figures
- Total Asset Value Recovered: Surpassed 1.359 trillion IQD in seized liquid funds, frozen financial instruments, and confiscated real estate properties.
- Integrity Commission Reports: Over 26,000 tips and corruption filings registered with the Federal Commission of Integrity during the ongoing enforcement phase.
- Whistleblower Financial Incentives: In accordance with the Informants Law (قانون مكافأة المخبرين), individuals who submit verified information leading directly to the recovery of stolen public funds are entitled to financial rewards of up to 5% of the total recovered sum.
Al-Aboudi outlined that the government’s anti-corruption strategy balances punitive judicial enforcement with systemic preventive reforms:
- Judicial Safeguards: Emphasized that the Iraqi judiciary stands as the core guarantor supporting the legitimacy, evidence verification, and success of anti-corruption actions.
- Direct Prime Ministerial Oversight: Highlighted the Prime Minister’s recent field visit to the Commission of Integrity, confirming direct executive backing for specialized investigative judges and investigators.
- Preemptive Contract Auditing: Instituting mandatory advance audits on high-value public procurement contracts to identify irregularities before fund disbursements take place.
- Digital Transformation and Automation: Accelerating the digitization of state transactions and public registries to minimize arbitrary human interference, extortion, and bribery opportunities across ministries.
Al-Aboudi characterized systemic corruption as a deeply entrenched web linking financial schemes, administrative loopholes, and political influence that drains public wealth and stalls infrastructure projects.
He reiterated that there will be no halt or political compromise in the government’s anti-corruption drive, noting that institutional transparency, automated governance, and aggressive asset recovery remain long-term priorities.

items.title: Trump remains vague on sanctions plan for Iran’s partners
items.summary: President Donald Trump remained vague Friday when asked about his campaign to choke off Iran’s economy, refusing to say whether he planned to sanction Chinese banks or if he’d discussed the matter with foreign counterparts. The administration announced earlier this week Operation Economic Outcast, which threatened tough new sanctions on Iran’s trading partners if they … The post Trump remains vague on sanctions plan for Iran’s partners appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
President Donald Trump remained vague Friday when asked about his campaign to choke off Iran’s economy, refusing to say whether he planned to sanction Chinese banks or if he’d discussed the matter with foreign counterparts.
The administration announced earlier this week Operation Economic Outcast, which threatened tough new sanctions on Iran’s trading partners if they didn’t cut off ties to Tehran.
But the administration stopped short of putting in place any new measures, and so far hasn’t listed any major financial institutions from China — Iran’s largest trading partner — as being subject to US sanctions.
Trump bristled when asked why he wasn’t applying new sanctions on Chinese banks doing business with Tehran.
“Who said I’m not? You don’t know if I’m doing it,” he said. “I don’t have to announce everything, do I?”
Later, asked which world leaders he’d discussed the pressure campaign with, Trump suggested it wasn’t on his agenda, even though Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Monday that Trump was placing calls to foreign counterparts “with specific requests to cease their interactions with the regime.”
“There’s not a lot to speak to. We don’t want to speak to them,” Trump said Thursday. “We’re not looking to meet or anything.”

items.title: Iceland rejects EU membership plan in referendum held under the shadow of Trump’s Greenland threats
items.summary: Reuters — Icelanders have voted to stay out of the European Union, broadcaster RUV reported on Sunday, rejecting a government push to reopen membership talks and siding with those who said Iceland’s fishing waters were too important to risk. Some votes from one constituency are pending but these were not expected to change the outcome, RUV … The post Iceland rejects EU membership plan in referendum held under the shadow of Trump’s Greenland threats appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
Icelanders have voted to stay out of the European Union, broadcaster RUV reported on Sunday, rejecting a government push to reopen membership talks and siding with those who said Iceland’s fishing waters were too important to risk.
Some votes from one constituency are pending but these were not expected to change the outcome, RUV said.
A ‘no’ vote will disappoint Brussels, as some officials had cast the island nation of 40,000 as a low-risk case that could help ease scepticism toward EU enlargement and strategically strengthen the bloc when Arctic security is in focus.
The government has framed membership as a shield against trade wars and Arctic rivalry and presented the referendum as a “now or never” moment, with Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadóttir warning that a “no” would put the membership question aside.
The government is due to hold a press conference at 1 p.m. (1300 GMT).
Decades of membership debate
Iceland first applied to join the EU in 2009 when a financial crisis hit the country’s small, exposed economy. A Eurosceptic government ended talks in 2013.
Geopolitical turmoil, including war in the Middle East and US import tariffs, has brought urgency to an issue Icelanders have debated on and off for decades.
“Yes” campaigners have said joining the bloc could help to lower interest rates and offer more security in a world unsettled by the war in Ukraine and US President Donald Trump’s rhetoric about annexing another Arctic island, Greenland.
“No” campaigners said EU membership would threaten the island’s sovereignty and fishing waters.
The referendum campaign has fueled debate about Iceland’s place in the world, Frostadóttir told reporters after casting her ballot in the capital on Saturday.
“This is a great day. We’ve been waiting for this for years to be able to have a vote,” Frostadóttir said, adding that her government would continue its work regardless of the outcome.
Interest rates and the cost of living
Debates inside Iceland have focused on interest rates, fishing rights and the cost of living rather than on security.
Iceland has grappled with high inflation and interest rates that have made mortgages expensive. Supporters of a “yes” vote have said EU membership, and possibly adopting the euro, could bring relief. Iceland’s central bank interest rate is 8%, compared with 2.25% at the European Central Bank.
“It would not solve Iceland’s structural faults, but it could become a catalyst to a more healthy economy,” said chief economist Vilhjalmur Hilmarsson at Viska, one of Iceland’s largest labour unions.
Opposition leader Gudrun Hafsteinsdottir, who has led the “no” campaign, said the economic case is overstated. “These are not problems that Brussels will solve for us. These are problems that Icelandic politicians must solve,” she said.
Voter Ragnhildur Skarphedinsdottir, 70, said Iceland was managing well on its own and that she was voting “no.”
“By staying independent as we are, we look brightly to the future,” she said before casting her ballot in Reykjavik.
Under EU rules, fishing quotas are based on historical fishing patterns, among other factors. Some Icelandic officials have said Iceland would therefore retain control of its waters, since no EU country has fished there for decades.
Hafsteinsdottir disputes that. “I know that the European Union will come up with some promises of some flexibility, especially in the beginning, but we know that it will not be for good,” she said.
This story had been updated.

items.title: Here’s what Meta’s $18 billion multistate settlement could mean for kids — and for its bottom line
items.summary: New York — Meta on Wednesday agreed to make sweeping changes to its platforms as part of an $18 billion settlement with dozens of states over claims its platforms contributed to a youth mental health crisis. Regulators and online safety advocates called it a watershed moment, and both Meta and state attorneys general called on TikTok … The post Here’s what Meta’s $18 billion multistate settlement could mean for kids — and for its bottom line appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
Regulators and online safety advocates called it a watershed moment, and both Meta and state attorneys general called on TikTok and YouTube to make similar changes.
But whether the settlement fundamentally alters the business of one of the world’s most powerful tech giants remains an open question.
The $18 billion agreement is a drop in the bucket for the nearly $1.5 trillion company (META) and a fraction of what states were seeking at trial, although Meta still faces hundreds of other similar cases. The litigation so far has revealed internal documents suggesting that Meta knew of the risks its platforms posed to young people, despite public statements about its commitments to safety.
Still, some online safety advocates say they wish the deal went further to upend Meta’s core, ad-based business model. And many are now calling on Congress to codify the changes in industry-wide federal legislation.
What is clear: Meta will no longer be able to grade its own homework on youth safety. An independent auditor will review its implementation of the required changes — a crucial step that parents and advocates have been demanding for years.
“It’s transformational,” California Attorney General Rob Bonta told CNN’s Richard Quest on Wednesday. “There’s a real, durable enforcement mechanism here and safeguard in place now.”
Meta did not admit wrongdoing as part of the settlement.
“The framework we’ve negotiated will empower parents to easily manage how their children access our platforms,” Meta Chief Legal Officer C.J. Mahoney said in a statement Wednesday, adding that the changes “set the right path forward for our whole industry.”
Changes to protect kids
Among the changes for users aged 13 to 17 are a two-hour daily time limit across Facebook and Instagram, a “night mode” making the apps unavailable from midnight to 6 am and a “school mode” limiting notifications during school hours. Only parents will be able to adjust those settings.
Meta will also turn off “like” counts by default on teens’ content and “extreme makeup” beauty filters.
Teens will have the option to turn off autoplay, so videos don’t start automatically when they open the apps, and select a feed not based on algorithmic recommendations.
Meta will have six months to implement the changes.
For Lori Schott, a founding member of the online safety parent advocacy group Parents RISE!, the changes are a “movement in the right direction.” But she said she wishes Meta had made them earlier, without litigation.
Schott says her daughter, Annalee, died by suicide at 18 in 2020 after Meta’s platforms repeatedly served her harmful content.
“For this, the mental health aspects are really important to me — the aspects of no beautification filters and the like buttons that are going to be removed — that impact so many little girls,” Schott, whose own individual lawsuit against Meta is pending, told CNN.
But while the settlement includes some “meaningful” changes, others don’t go far enough, said Sebastian Mahal, co-chair of the youth online safety organization Design It For Us. For example, while teens can opt-in to a non-algorithmic feed, the default remains a personalized version that’s better for Meta’s business, Mahal said.
“They’re really allowing users a semblance of a different experience,” Mahal said. “But we would rather see that these safest experiences be switched on automatically for users.”
The settlement also includes several carve-outs. “Night Mode,” for example, will still allow access to messaging on Instagram and Facebook when the apps are otherwise blocked for teens, according to court documents.
The effectiveness of many of the changes will largely depend on whether Meta can accurately detect teen users.

Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council          
        Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here.
Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.
US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.
Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.
Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.
Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.
In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.
Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment.
On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro.
Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.
Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.
RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.
Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.
And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations.
Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.

Once bitter enemies Amhara, Tigray reach understandings in fight against Ethiopian govt          
        In mid-August, the leader of the Amhara insurgency fighting to overthrow Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed made a surprising announcement.
The collection of armed Amhara movements fighting in the country’s northwest under the unified Fano umbrella would join an alliance of seven other anti-government groups across the country, Fano leader Zemene Kassie told the Swiss publication, Le Temps.
What makes the move surprising is that the alliance includes members of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), whom the Amhara forces that make up the Fano fought against during the 2020-2022 war.
In addition to the TPLF, the alliance includes forces from Gumuz, Oromo, the Berta people and Somalia, Zemene said.
At the national level, the fight between Ethiopian oppositional groups and the government comes against the backdrop of a struggle over the future of the country’s multinational federal system and state’s right to self-determination.
However, this tension has a larger regional dynamic given Ethiopia’s involvement in the war in Sudan and its expressed desire to secure access to the Red Sea either by diplomatic coup or by force.
While fighting between the Fano and the Ethiopian government has transformed much of the Amhara Region into an active war zone since late 2023, the beginning of August saw clashes between TPLF forces and the Ethiopian military that threatened to transform long standing simmering tensions between the groups into an active war.
An African Union diplomat based in Addis Ababa told Mada Masr at the time that any expansion of the fighting in Tigray would have an impact on the calculations of every regional actor because the borders linking Sudan, Ethiopia and Eritrea are no longer merely dividing lines between states. They now form part of an interconnected regional security system in which domestic wars and geopolitical interests overlap, the diplomat added, making any new outbreak of fighting in Tigray a potential factor in reshaping the security landscape of the entire East African region.
The government has responded to the early August clashes with increased military activity.
In a statement issued on Friday, the Tigray regional government warned the international community that the region is nearing “another catastrophic war.”
An economic and security blockade has escalated following clashes that broke out on August 1, the statement added, with air strikes and artillery shelling hitting civilian areas, causing casualties and destruction and disrupting cultural activities.
In an interview with Oromia Broadcasting Network on August 7, Abiy criticized the TPLF leadership, accusing it of clinging to outdated political methods and forging alliances that he said threaten stability.
TPLF deputy chair Amanuel Assefa pointed to a strike on August 20, when a drone hit a residential area in Mekelle, Tigray’s capital. Residents speaking to Mada Masr confirmed the strike and said several homes were damaged.
Medical sources at Mekelle’s Ayder Specialized Hospital said 13 people were brought in with injuries following the strike, including five women and children, with three in serious condition. The injured ranged in age from two to 60, the sources said.
Tigrayan authorities also said a second strike hit near Mekelle University, though there is no confirmed information on casualties or damage as of the time of publishing.
The strike on Mekelle came only days after another attack that Tigrayan authorities attributed to the Ethiopian military, where a drone struck a farmers’ training center in the Dandera village, about 15 km from Mekelle, on August 18.
While the government hit Tigray, Fano forces continued to secure strategic wins against the Ethiopian military.

items.body_text:
Warraq residents demonstrate to protest ‘state ignoring legitimate demands’          
        Hundreds of Warraq Island residents held a protest march on Tuesday, after the head of the authority tasked with developing the island failed to respond to demands they submitted last week, one of the participants in the march told Mada Masr.
Hundreds of residents gathered in the street on Tuesday morning, on the deadline they had given authorities to respond to demands they submitted last week, including that they be granted lands within the state development project, according to the participant as well as videos published by other residents who attended the march.
The crowd then marched toward the New Warraq City Development headquarters, where a heavy security deployment awaited them. Security officials told them that the head of the authority asked for a small group to enter for negotiations.
The protestors refused, instead demanding that the authority’s head come down to meet them, in an attempt to get a direct response to the demands they had already submitted in writing.
The resident who took part in Tuesday’s march said the authority head’s refusal to come down and meet the residents sparked anger among many of them, but that they kept it in check out of their keenness to keep the protest peaceful.
But it showed “a lack of consideration, especially since he didn’t meet us when we came to hand over the demands,” the resident said.
The same sentiment was clear at the protest. “Nobody has paid us any attention,” one of the protesters called out to the assembled crowd. “At this moment, we register our objection to the state’s disregard for our legitimate and just demands by saying just one thing: God is sufficient for us, and he is the best disposer of all affairs,” indicating the group’s loss of faith in the authorities’ seriousness.
The residents then continued their peaceful protest march along the route that had been agreed to in advance. While the march had been planned without chants, still, the residents raised similar cries of “God is sufficient for us” and “one hand.”
At the end of the march, the residents agreed to meet again on Friday to discuss their next steps, and raised the possibility of disrupting ongoing development work on the island.
The residents had submitted a list of demands to the authority on August 18, foremost among them that they be allocated a plot of land within the island’s redevelopment area, where residents who have chosen to stay could build their own homes, according to a defined timeline, with clear and specific implementation mechanisms and fair conditions. They also put forward other demands concerning living and security conditions on the island.
The group handed their written demands to the authority’s deputy chair at the time, with the head elsewhere with another group of Warraq residents, inspecting one of the island’s schools, supposedly to assess potential upgrades.
The resident described to Mada Masr the authority head’s meeting with that group as part of security attempts to “divide.”
One of the people in the group that did not join Tuesday’s march said there were some who had not attended the recent meeting that produced the list of demands. The group who went with the authority head on his school visit opposes holding marches to the authority’s offices, they told Mada Masr. Instead, they have been trying to communicate with officials at the authority and pressure them to implement “as many things as possible that would allow us to keep living on the island,” they continued, adding that they are convinced the government would not agree to give residents land on the island to replace their homes.
The source pointed to what they saw as officials responding to some of the residents’ service-related demands, including bringing back sewage pumping trucks and beginning to clear demolition waste that had piled up along the island’s roads.

items.title: Iran’s IRGC claims complete control of Hormuz as US forces redirect 82 ships under blockade
items.summary: The naval force of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) declared on Saturday that it retains “complete control” over the Strait of Hormuz, asserting that the waterway will remain closed to vessels attempting to cross without coordination with Tehran as the US military continues to enforce a naval blockade. Iran’s state news agency IRNA […] The post Iran’s IRGC claims complete control of Hormuz as US forces redirect 82 ships under blockade first appeared on Dailynewsegypt.
items.body_text:
The naval force of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) declared on Saturday that it retains “complete control” over the Strait of Hormuz, asserting that the waterway will remain closed to vessels attempting to cross without coordination with Tehran as the US military continues to enforce a naval blockade.
Iran’s state news agency IRNA quoted the IRGC Navy as stating that the closure will continue “until the end of the US military’s hostile actions against Iran and the implementation of the agreed commitments”. Meanwhile, US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated on Saturday that its forces have redirected 82 commercial vessels, disabled three ships, and boarded two others to ensure compliance as part of the ongoing US blockade against Iran, sharing imagery on social platform X of a watchstander aboard the guided-missile destroyer USS John Paul Jones (DDG 53).
In a statement published by state media on Saturday, the Iranian government pledged to stand “firmly” against US sanctions and what it described as US-Israeli “conspiracies”. The government affirmed that diplomacy and defence are “complementary, coordinated and inseparable tools” for protecting national interests and regional security, adding that it is pursuing both paths simultaneously while focusing on curbing inflation, creating employment, supporting domestic production, and gradually reducing reliance on the US dollar.
The IRGC Navy dismissed US assertions that the Strait of Hormuz remains open to maritime traffic as a “clear lie”. The statement followed reports on Friday by news outlet Axios, citing US officials, claiming that Iran had lost a significant portion of its control over the strait, with the US military effectively controlling most of the waterway.
The IRGC’s assertion follows statements on Friday by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who said Tehran had established a route for crossing the Strait of Hormuz following consensus with Muscat based on the “Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding”. Speaking in a televised interview, Pezeshkian stated Iran would open the agreed transit corridor if four conditions are met: lifting the “blockade”, removing sanctions on fuel and petrochemicals, releasing frozen assets, and halting Israeli attacks on Lebanon. He provided no further details on the proposed passage or the parties involved in implementing the commitments.
Separately, US diplomats and their families have begun a gradual return to embassies across the Middle East after ordered departures during the early days of the Iran war, following the lifting of certain personnel restrictions by the US State Department this week. According to the Associated Press, the measures stem primarily from legal frameworks within human resources policy regarding paid leave limits rather than a shift in President Donald Trump’s administration policy toward Iran. By Friday, US embassies in Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain permitted family returns—restricted to those over 18 in Kuwait and Bahrain—following earlier allowances for families of US government personnel in Israel and those over 21 in Lebanon.

items.title: Egypt issues 907 livestock licenses and injects EGP59.850m into National Veal Project in August
items.summary: Egypt’s Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation issued 907 operating licenses for livestock, poultry, feed, and dairy collection projects in August, whilst approving EGP 59.850m in new financing for the National Veal Project. The figures were detailed in an official August report submitted to Minister of Agriculture Alaa Farouk by Tarek Soliman, head of […] The post Egypt issues 907 livestock licenses and injects EGP59.850m into National Veal Project in August first appeared on Dailynewsegy
items.body_text:
Egypt’s Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation issued 907 operating licenses for livestock, poultry, feed, and dairy collection projects in August, whilst approving EGP 59.850m in new financing for the National Veal Project.
The figures were detailed in an official August report submitted to Minister of Agriculture Alaa Farouk by Tarek Soliman, head of the livestock and poultry development sector.
Soliman stated that the new Veal Project financing will support 47 beneficiaries raising 855 head of cattle. This brings the total funding granted since the project’s inception to over EGP 11.514bn, benefiting 46,398 small breeders, graduates, and women across “Decent Life” initiative villages, and covering more than 543,417 head of cattle.
Of the 907 operating licenses issued during the month, 167 were permits granted to small breeders for livestock rearing, coordinated with the General Authority for Veterinary Services. The ministry also granted 28 technical approvals for new animal and poultry production projects in desert hinterland areas to enforce biosecurity requirements and distance major production activities from residential blocks.
In addition to licensing, the sector supervised the destruction of a shipment of non-compliant imported feed additives totalling 2,304 tonnes and 1,200 litres via joint inspection committees. Soliman noted that the ministry continued surprise inspection campaigns on factories and warehouses across governorates to confront monopolies and the withholding of goods.
The ministry approved 777 registrations for feed mixtures, additives, and concentrates, comprising 416 local and 361 imported registrations. This was conducted in cooperation with the Regional Center for Food and Feed and the Animal Production Research Institute. Soliman stated that the oversight and registration aim to reduce production costs and improve food conversion rates and final product quality.
Technical support and homogeneity tests were also provided for 47 feed factories, encompassing 106 production lines dedicated to poultry, livestock, and fish, in preparation for their licensing. The ministry, overseen by Deputy Minister Mostafa Al-Sayyad, organised eight extension seminars and practical training sessions in several governorates to transfer modern feeding and care practices to breeders.
Soliman added that during August, Egypt exported quantities of fish feed, feed additives, frozen poultry, table eggs, and frozen birds—including quail, duck, pigeon, and turkey—to several Arab and foreign markets.

items.summary: Egyptian Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Esmat and the CEO of the UAE’s Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar), Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi, reviewed the progress of large-scale wind, solar, and battery storage projects as Egypt aims to increase its renewable energy share to 45% by 2028. During their meeting, the two […] The post UAE’s Masdar and Egypt review wind, solar and battery storage projects to meet 2028 energy targets first appeared on Dailynewsegypt.
items.body_text:
Egyptian Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Esmat and the CEO of the UAE’s Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar), Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi, reviewed the progress of large-scale wind, solar, and battery storage projects as Egypt aims to increase its renewable energy share to 45% by 2028.
During their meeting, the two sides discussed accelerating the implementation of ongoing generation and storage projects under signed memorandums of cooperation, to ensure their swift connection to the unified national grid.
Esmat reviewed the progress of a 200-megawatt (MW) wind power plant in the Gulf of Suez, which is scheduled to be connected to the national electricity grid in December next year.
The discussions also covered major developments managed by the Infinity-Hassan Allam consortium. These include a 1,000 MW wind energy project in Ras Shukeir, a 1,000 MW solar project paired with a 600-megawatt-hour (MWh) battery storage system in Minya, and a 200 MW solar project with a 120 MWh battery storage system in Benban, which is slated for grid connection by the end of this year.
Esmat stated that adding renewable generation capacities, accompanied by connected and independent energy storage systems, is part of the state’s plan to reduce fossil fuel consumption. He noted that increasing reliance on clean and sustainable energy aims to secure electricity supplies across all uses and achieve stability for the unified grid.
The minister affirmed that reaching the 45% renewable energy target by 2028 relies on cooperation and expanded partnerships with both the local and foreign private sectors, highlighting the ongoing collaboration with Masdar in the renewable energy sector.

items.title: Khmara on Ukraine's long-range strikes: Enemy has no 'rear area,' Russia must get used to it
items.summary: Strikes deep inside Russian territory are part of a clear strategy to weaken Russia's war machine and destroy the aggressor's military and economic potential.
items.body_text:
Khmara on Ukraine's long-range strikes: Enemy has no 'rear area,' Russia must get used to it
According to Ukrinform, Ukraine's Ministry of Defense stated this in a Telegram post.
"Strikes deep inside enemy territory are part of a clear strategy to weaken the Russian war machine," the ministry's press service quoted Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara as saying.
According to the Ministry of Defense, over the past 24 hours alone, the Kirishinefteorgsintez oil refinery in Leningrad Region was hit. This means hundreds of thousands of tonnes of fuel that will no longer make it into the tanks of Russian forces. At the Yeysk airfield in Krasnodar Krai, a large-scale fire broke out following a successful strike. A Shahed drone preparation and launch base in Millerovo, Rostov Region, from which Russia launches drones at Ukraine, was also hit. The "Kover" plan, airspace closures, and air raid alerts were introduced across 10 Russian regions simultaneously. The Chkalovsky airfield near Moscow and Sochi Airport in Adler were temporarily shut down.
The Ministry of Defense added that the following facilities in Russia had been hit during the week:
- August 25 — the Afipsky Oil Refinery, one of the major oil refineries in Krasnodar Krai;
- August 26 — the Lukoil-Nizhegorodniinefteproekt refinery in Kstovo, Russia's fourth-largest refinery and second-largest by gasoline production;
- August 28 — the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl.
"For our Deep Strike systems, there is no such thing as a 'rear area.' The Russian war machine will burn wherever it prepares to commit crimes," the Ministry of Defense stressed.
As Ukrinform reported, Russia's total combat losses since the beginning of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, amounted to approximately 1,486,600 personnel as of August 30, 2026, including 1,400 over the previous 24 hours.

items.title: Ukraine Reaches Winter Gas Reserve Target of 14.6B Cubic Meters Early
items.summary: Ukraine has reached its target of 14.6 billion cubic meters of natural gas reserves a month ahead of schedule, ensuring baseline coverage for the 2026-2027 winter season. The early accumulation comes as the government pushes to decentralize the energy grid and protect infrastructure from anticipated Russian attacks.
items.body_text:
Ukraine has accumulated enough natural gas to meet its baseline requirements for the upcoming 2026-2027 winter season, reaching its target a month ahead of schedule.
First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal announced on Telegram on Friday, Aug. 28, that the country’s underground storage facilities now hold 14.6 billion cubic meters of gas.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Shmyhal confirmed that the reserves ensure the country is prepared for the autumn-winter period, though work on physical infrastructure protection continues.
He expressed gratitude to Ukrainian gas production companies, the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine (GTSOU), the state-owned oil and gas company Naftogaz, and the broader energy sector for achieving the milestone early.
Nationwide winter preparations and infrastructure resilience
The early accumulation of gas reserves aligns with a broader national effort to prepare critical infrastructure and residential areas against anticipated Russian attacks.
On Aug. 21, Minister of Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport Mykola Kalashnyk announced that approximately 100,000 residential buildings – representing 70% of the government’s target – had already been prepared for the heating season. Kalashnyk noted that preparations were also completed for 12,400 boiler houses and 11,700 kilometers (7,270 miles) of heating networks.
The government has allocated nearly Hr. 6.8 billion ($152 million) for repair works and infrastructure protection. The primary focus of this funding is decentralizing the energy system, maintaining reserve capacity, and ensuring heating and water networks can operate autonomously during potential blackouts.
EU Prepares New Sanctions Package Targeting 1,600 Russian Entities
Preparations have been a central focus for the Cabinet since Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi – a former executive recognized for reforming Ukrnafta and leading Naftogaz through previous winter strikes – took office in mid-July.
While the national energy staff pushes companies to expedite protective measures, local authorities are simultaneously preparing for worst-case scenarios.
Earlier in August, Kyiv officials announced they were compiling lists of residents who may require temporary relocation in the event of prolonged heating outages this winter.

items.title: Khmara Details Plan for $27B Defense Deficit, Appoints New Team
items.summary: Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara outlined strategies to resolve a $27 billion defense funding deficit by advancing European loans and engaging new international partners. Speaking to journalists, Khmara emphasized institutional continuity within the ministry, revealing new leadership appointments for frontline operations, human capital, and international partnerships. Khmara also confirmed he had reached out to his predecessor, Mykhailo Fedorov, to find a model for continued collaboration, though
items.body_text:
Ukraine’s Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara outlined a strategy to bridge a $27 billion defense funding gap, proposing to advance portions of a planned European loan and solicit contributions from new international partners, Ukrinform reported.
Speaking to journalists, Khmara stated the ministry has identified specific partners for targeted communications to secure additional funding for concrete defense needs.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
He emphasized that Kyiv will present allies with a clear vision detailing the military’s objectives, required projects, and timelines for achieving results.
Addressing the internal structure of the Defense Ministry, Khmara stressed the importance of institutional continuity and announced he had offered his predecessor, Mykhailo Fedorov, an open format to continue collaborating on defense projects. Khmara noted he had not offered a specific position and is still awaiting a response following their meeting in July.
The minister also announced new appointments to strengthen the ministry’s leadership. Mykola Shvydkyi will oversee frontline operations, while Liubov Halan is tasked with human capital development.
Serhii Boiev has returned to manage international partnerships, and Hanna Hvozdiar is slated to lead the defense-industrial complex and export division. Khmara added that candidates are also being finalized for digital transformation and cognitive warfare roles.
Missile Strike on Kharkiv Memorial Run Leaves 3 Dead
Khmara emphasized that the military, government, defense industry, and international partners, must operate as a unified system, adding that he and the commander-in-chief share a common vision and are working as a cohesive team.
Addressing domestic defense capabilities, Khmara revealed that Ukraine has developed four potential interceptors designed to counter jet-powered “Shahed” attack drones.
He stated that the systems have already passed field tests, and the immediate goal is to refine the technology and scale production to thousands of units.
Military background and recent leadership changes
Khmara’s team-building efforts follow his formal appointment by the Verkhovna Rada on Aug. 19, following a proposal from President Volodymyr Zelensky. To comply with Ukrainian law requiring a civilian defense minister, Khmara – a major general in the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) – was discharged from military service prior to the vote.
Khmara replaced Fedorov, whose abrupt dismissal triggered a wave of street protests across Ukraine that have continued in recent weeks. Khmara is the fifth defense minister since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion, taking over a ministry that has seen rapid turnover over the past year.
Prior to his appointment, Khmara spent most of his career in special operations, eventually commanding the SBU’s Alpha special operations center. Under his leadership, the unit claimed to have destroyed more than $5.5 billion worth of Russian military equipment. He also briefly served as the acting head of the SBU earlier this year.

items.title: Belgium Rejects Renewed EU Push to Fund Ukraine With Frozen Assets
items.summary: Belgian Defense Minister Theo Francken stated that utilizing €200 billion ($232 billion) in immobilized Russian assets to support Ukraine remains “non-negotiable,” pushing back against a renewed effort by Sweden, Poland, the Netherlands, and Spain. Speaking on television, Francken warned Baltic nations against cornering Belgium over the issue, given the assets are largely held at the Belgian clearinghouse Euroclear.
items.body_text:
Belgium is standing firm against using frozen Russian assets to support Ukraine, as four EU countries push to resurrect the scheme.
“This is non-negotiable, the door is closed,” Theo Francken, the defence minister, told Terzaken, on Flemish TV channel VRT, on Friday night.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
This week Sweden, Poland, the Netherlands and Spain called upon the European Commission to explore new ways to harness around €200 billion in immobilised Russian assets to support Ukraine.
At a dramatic European summit last December, Bart De Wever, the Belgian leader, shot down an effort led by Germany and the European Commission, to fashion a €210 billion ($243 billion) ‘reparations loan’ for Ukraine, arguing it would leave the Benelux nation exposed to Russian legal retribution.
Most of the assets are held at Euroclear in Belgium. “Our prime minister will stand firm,” Francken added.
Noting that Belgium’s resistance has generated resentment, he singled out the Baltic states – who are the strongest supporters of the reparations loan – for refusing to drop it.
“They should also be careful about constantly bringing this issue up again and putting us in a corner. I don’t think that is wise,” Francken said, pointing at the Baltics. Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia receive a lot of support from Belgium, he pointed out.
Russian Strikes Hit Odesa Food Hub, Kill 1 in Zaporizhzhia Drone Attack
Francken’s tough tone differs somewhat from the way Maxime Prévot, the Belgian foreign minister, has talked about the scheme this month. Prévot appeared to leave the door open to using the immobilised assets, this month, on the condition that all legal responsibility is fairly shared out among EU countries.
The Swedish letter acknowledged the legal risks inherent in using the Russian assets, and stated that no country should bear a disproportionate burden.
European foreign ministers will discuss the topic at an meeting in Ireland next week.
Ukraine, in sore need of air defence, is preparing for a brutal winter and Volodymyr Zelenskyy said this week that his administration faces a €23.5 billion ($27.2 billion) funding gap.

items.title: Мартинес перешел из «Астон Виллы» в «Челси»
items.body_text:
Вратарь сборной Аргентины Эмилиано Мартинес перешел из «Астон Виллы» в «Челси», подписав трехлетний контракт с лондонским клубом. Об этом объявила пресс-служба «Челси».
По данным журналиста Фабрицио Романо, сумма трансфера составила 7,5 миллиона фунтов (8,7 миллиона евро). Мартинес может дебютировать за новый клуб уже 30 августа во втором туре АПЛ против «Брайтона».
«Я рад оказаться в этом футбольном клубе. Переход в «Челси» был простым решением для меня и моей семьи, и я просто невероятно счастлив — не могу дождаться начала работы», — заявил голкипер.
По информации The Guardian, Мартинес получал и другие предложения, но выразил желание играть под руководством главного тренера «Челси» Хаби Алонсо.
За «Астон Виллу» аргентинец выступал с 2020 года и провел 256 матчей за шесть сезонов. В мае он стал победителем Лиги Европы. Вместе со сборной Аргентины Мартинес выиграл чемпионат мира 2022 года и Кубок Америки в 2021-м и 2024-м. В 2023-м и 2024-м голкипер получал приз имени Льва Яшина как лучший вратарь года.

items.title: Врач оценила правдивость утверждения о связи кофе и высокого давления
items.body_text:
Влияние кофе на артериальное давление не так однозначно, как принято думать, заявила кардиолог сети клиник «Семейная» Наталья Соловьева. Правдивость утверждения о связи кофе и гипертонии она оценила в разговоре с «Лентой.ру».
«Сразу после выпитой чашки кофе артериальное давление действительно повышается. Однако этот показатель, как правило, меняется незначительно и самостоятельно возвращается к норме в течение пары часов. Также стоит отметить, что при регулярном употреблении кофе на протяжении длительного времени этот эффект исчезает. Организм адаптируется к постоянной стимуляции, и напиток больше не влияет на давление», — рассказала Соловьева.
Врач подчеркнула: на тему влияния кофе на артериальное давление проведено много исследований. Их результаты показали, что стойкого повышения этого показателя не было зафиксировано ни в молодом возрасте, ни у людей старшей возрастной группы. Более того, часть исследователей отметили парадоксальное снижение уровня артериального давления при длительном употреблении умеренного количества кофе, отметила кардиолог.
Она добавила, что безопасным количеством считается до 400 граммов кофеина в день. Это эквивалентно трем-четырем чашкам эспрессо.
Ранее онколог Владимир Ивашков рассказал, что здоровье мозга может незаметно разрушать гипертония. Он объяснил, что высокое давление разрушает сосуды во всем организме, вызывая со временем тяжелые поражения.

items.title: РСТ: сведений о пострадавших при крушении парома на Кипре россиянах пока нет
items.summary: Подтвержденных сведений о присутствии российских граждан среди пассажиров парома, который перевернулся у берегов непризнанной Турецкой республики Северного Кипра, пока нет. Об этом сообщила пресс-служба Российского союза туриндустрии (РСТ).
items.body_text:
РСТ: сведений о пострадавших при крушении парома на Кипре россиянах пока нет
Подтвержденных сведений о присутствии российских граждан среди пассажиров парома, который перевернулся у берегов непризнанной Турецкой республики Северного Кипра, пока нет. Об этом сообщила пресс-служба Российского союза туриндустрии (РСТ).
Организация продолжает следить за ситуацией, отметили в пресс-службе. «РСТ уточняет информацию о возможном присутствии российских организованных туристов среди пассажиров», — указывается в публикации.
В посольстве России на Кипре сообщали ТАСС, что у властей Северного Кипра пока нет информации о том, пострадали ли при крушении российские граждане. Дипмиссия продолжит прояснять этот вопрос, пообещали дипломаты.
Сегодня днем у берегов непризнанной Турецкой республики Северного Кипра перевернулся пассажирский паром с 279 людьми на борту. Инцидент произошел примерно в 2–2,5 км от побережья города Кирения. Капитан судна заметил поступление воды в носовую часть парома и попытался повернуть обратно к берегу, однако вскоре судно опрокинулось и начало тонуть. Власти Северного Кипра развернули спасательную операцию. По словам главы Кирении Мурата Шенкула, судьба 99 пассажиров пока неизвестна.

items.title: Премьер Черногории обвинил соседей в препятствовании вступлению страны в ЕС
items.summary: Черногорский премьер Милойко Спаич обвинил «два государства региона» в планах дестабилизации Черногории на ее пути в Евросоюз. Хотя он не назвал конкретно ни одну соседнюю страну, практически никто в Черногории не сомневается, что премьер указал прежде всего на Сербию.
items.body_text:
Премьер Черногории обвинил соседей в препятствовании вступлению страны в ЕС
Черногорский премьер Милойко Спаич обвинил «два государства региона» в планах дестабилизации Черногории на ее пути в Евросоюз. Хотя он не назвал конкретно ни одну соседнюю страну, практически никто в Черногории не сомневается, что премьер указал прежде всего на Сербию. В последнее время руководство двух соседних государств обменялось жесткими взаимными выпадами, что привело к новому обострению отношений между ними.
«У нас есть серьезная оперативная информация, что предстоящее завершение наших переговоров с ЕС о вступлении будет сопровождаться скоординированными гибридными действиями, в которые вовлечены официальные лица как минимум двух государств региона. Целью этих действий является дестабилизация Черногории при поддержке отдельных политиков и СМИ в нашей стране»,— объявил в конце минувшей недели в соцсетях Милойко Спаич.
Подробнее — в материале «Ъ» «Балканские соседи обменялись риторическими ударами».
В марте 2026 года на межправительственной конференции с ЕС в Брюсселе Черногория завершила переговоры по одному из пунктов программы вступления, после чего премьер Милойко Спаич заявил о готовности страны стать членом Евросоюза к 2028 году. Для этого Черногории предстоит завершить переговоры по 19 из 33 несогласованных областей до конца текущего года, что считается крайне сложной задачей. Еврокомиссар по расширению Марта Кос предупредила, что страны, которые подрывают ЕС изнутри, не могут стать его членами, и подчеркнула, что вступающие в союз должны быть сильными демократиями, способными противостоять вредоносному влиянию.
В июне 2024 года Хорватия пригрозила заблокировать вступление Черногории в Евросоюз после того, как черногорский парламент принял резолюцию о геноциде в Ясеноваце. Власти Хорватии расценили это как антихорватский жест и «политизацию жертв», принятый под давлением президента Сербии Александра Вучича. При этом Милойко Спаич изначально заверял, что резолюция не будет вынесена на голосование, но обещание не сдержал.
В феврале 2024 года президент Черногории Яков Милатович подал в отставку со всех постов в правящей партии, где он был заместителем лидера Милойко Спаича, что вызвало политическую нестабильность и угрозу досрочных выборов. Эксперты полагают, что Сербия может извлечь выгоду из этой ситуации, так как она не заинтересована в ускоренной евроинтеграции Черногории и стремится усилить свое влияние в регионе.

items.title: Песков: Европе нужен «внешний враг» в лице России ради сбора налогов
items.summary: Пресс-секретарь президента России Дмитрий Песков заявил, что Европа, лишившись дешевого «американского зонтика» в сфере безопасности, вынуждена строить собственную оборонную идентичность. Это, уточняет господин Песков, требует значительных финансовых затрат.
items.body_text:
Песков: Европе нужен «внешний враг» в лице России ради сбора налогов
Пресс-секретарь президента России Дмитрий Песков заявил, что Европа, лишившись дешевого «американского зонтика» в сфере безопасности, вынуждена строить собственную оборонную идентичность. Это, уточняет господин Песков, требует значительных финансовых затрат.
Фото: Дмитрий Азаров / Коммерсантъ
В интервью журналисту ИС «Вести» Павлу Зарубину пресс-секретарь подчеркнул, что для финансирования этой новой системы европейским налогоплательщикам придется платить больше — увеличить налоги, расходы на коммунальные услуги, электричество и бензин.
По словам господина Пескова, такая нагрузка на бюджет вызывает недовольство среди граждан, и в сложившейся ситуации европейские власти стремятся убедить избирателей в необходимости дополнительных расходов, придумывая образ внешнего врага. «Как убедить избирателей? Придумать врага. Какой враг убедительнее всего? Большой враг, крупный, мощный»,— отметил представитель Кремля, уточнив, что именно России придается такой статус.
Дмитрий Песков также указал, что Москва заинтересована в построении новой архитектуры безопасности на европейском континенте. В то же время он заявил, что Россия не намерена вести войну с Европой, но готова защитить свои интересы в случае агрессии.
Пресс-секретарь президента России Дмитрий Песков 2 июля 2026 года заявил, что Евросоюз вступил на путь милитаризации и посвящает себя конфронтации с Россией, что усугубляет напряженность на европейском континенте. Это, по его словам, вынуждает Россию планировать дополнительные меры для обеспечения собственной безопасности. Ранее, 24 июня 2026 года, Дмитрий Песков отмечал, что независимость Европы от США в сфере обороны будет выстроена на вражеском отношении к России, и назвал это важным для России вопросом.
7 июля 2026 года Дмитрий Песков заявил, что Россия не представляет угрозы для европейских стран, однако если Брюссель продолжит игнорировать позицию Москвы, то у Евросоюза возникнут проблемы. Он подчеркнул, что европейцам следовало бы как можно скорее возобновить диалог с Россией, поскольку Москва открыта и готова к этому.

items.title: В Индии назвали самые популярные маршруты на Гоа
items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Понда, Ривона и Нетравали — популярные маршруты на Гоа для любителей активного и познавательного отдыха, где сосредоточены исторические достопримечательности и природные объекты.
- На маршруте Старый Гоа — Дивар — Чорао — Кумбарджуа можно увидеть исторические церкви и памятники, паромные переправы, островные деревни и мангровые заросли.
- Маршрут Канакона — Кепем — Кабо-де-Рама подойдет туристам, предпочитающим тихие пляжи, прибрежные деревни, живописные дороги и заповедники дикой природы.
МОСКВА, 30 авг - РИА Новости. Наиболее популярными маршрутами на Гоа в Индии для любителей активного и познавательного отдыха являются Понда, Ривона и Нетравали, здесь сосредоточены исторические храмы, святые места, древние пещеры, плантации специй, леса и водопады, рассказал РИА Новости глава департамента туризма штата Кедар Наик. 
 Исторические церкви и памятники, паромные переправы, островные деревни, мангровые заросли можно увидеть на маршруте Старый Гоа — Дивар — Чорао — Кумбарджуа, добавил он. 
Россияне стали чаще ездить в Индию на йога-ретриты
22 августа, 04:28
Туристам, предпочитающим тихие пляжи, прибрежные деревни, живописные дороги и заповедники дикой природы, подойдет, по его словам, маршрут Канакона — Кепем — Кабо-де-Рама. 
В ведомстве также рекомендовали обратить внимание на форт Рейш-Магуш, традиционные исторические дома, высеченные в скалах пещеры и плантации специй. 
"Эти маршруты особенно подходят путешественникам, предпочитающим длинные поездки, неспешный темп и индивидуально составленные программы вдали от переполненных туристических зон", - сказал собеседник агентства.
