items.title: Isländer stimmen gegen EU-Beitrittsgespräche
items.summary: Sie wollen es nicht: Beim Referendum in Island über die Wiederaufnahme von Beitrittsverhandlungen mit der Europäischen Union haben sich die Gegner knapp durchgesetzt.
items.body_text:
Referendum über Wiederaufnahme :Isländer stimmen gegen EU-Beitrittsgespräche
Sie wollen es nicht: Beim Referendum in Island über die Wiederaufnahme von Beitrittsverhandlungen mit der Europäischen Union haben sich die Gegner knapp durchgesetzt.
Die Einwohnerinnen und Einwohner Islands haben mehrheitlich gegen eine Wiederaufnahme der Gespräche über einen EU-Beitritt ihres Landes gestimmt. Das Ergebnis des Referendums fiel mit 52,8 zu 47,2 Prozent der Stimmen knapp aus, wie die Auszählung ergab.
Gegen die Fortsetzung der vor 13 Jahren unterbrochenen Verhandlungen stimmten rund 12.000 Menschen mehr als dafür. Zur Abstimmung aufgerufen waren gut 270.000 Isländerinnen und Isländer. Ein Fünftel von ihnen hatte nach Angaben des isländischen Fernsehens bereits vorab abgestimmt.
Gespräche mit EU 2013 abgebrochen
Die sozialdemokratische Regierungschefin Kristrún Frostadóttir hatte vorab angekündigt, sie werde sich an das Ergebnis der Volksabstimmung halten. Bereits während der Finanzkrise 2009 hatte das gerade einmal rund 400.000 Einwohner zählende Land einen Antrag auf eine Mitgliedschaft in der Europäischen Union gestellt. Doch nach der Parlamentswahl 2013 legte die neue EU-skeptische Regierung die Beitrittspläne auf Eis.
Es geht um Sicherheit, Souveränität und Fischereirechte: Island stimmt darüber ab, ob Beitrittsgespräche mit der EU wieder aufgenommen werden.
29.08.2026 | 2:16 min
Regierung warb um Zustimmung
Frostadóttir hatte die Wiederaufnahme der Gespräche kurz vor dem Referendum im isländischen Fernsehen als "einen der bedeutendsten Schritte" bezeichnet, mit dem sich Risiken für die Insel reduzieren ließen. In unsicheren Zeiten wie diesen, in denen sich internationale Beziehungen veränderten, sei die Frage, ob ein kleines Land wie Island sich größeren Staaten und Bündnissen annähern sollte.
Diese Aussagen wurden vor allem als Anspielung auf den Konflikt um Grönland verstanden. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte wiederholt damit gedroht, die zu Dänemark gehörende Arktisinsel den USA einzuverleiben - und damit auch auf Island Unruhe ausgelöst.
Sorgen um eigene Fischerei
Wirtschaftlich ist Island bereits stark in Europa integriert: Das Land gehört zum Europäischen Wirtschaftsraum und genießt die Vorteile des Binnenmarkts - hat aber bei wichtigen Entscheidungen kein Mitspracherecht.
Auf Island wird noch immer legal Jagd auf Wale gemacht. Trotz politischer Widerstände besitzen zwei Unternehmen weiter Lizenzen.
01.07.2026 | 2:10 min
Die Gespräche über einen EU-Beitritt waren im ersten Anlauf vor allem an der Debatte um die Fischerei gescheitert - den größten und identitätsstiftenden Wirtschaftszweig der Insel. Auch jetzt waren wieder große Zweifel aufgekommen, ob ein Beitritt ohne die Aufgabe zu vieler eigener Rechte möglich wäre.
Regierungschefin Frostadóttir hatte ihren Landsleuten zwar versprochen, Island werde den Verhandlungstisch schnell wieder verlassen, sollte man nicht die volle Kontrolle über die eigenen Fischereiressourcen behalten dürfen. Die Sorge war aber nun wohl zu groß.

items.title: Schweiz: Eine Tote, mehrere Verletzte nach Schüssen bei Rave-Party
items.summary: In Aarau in der Schweiz sind bei einer Veranstaltung in der Nacht Schüsse gefallen. Die Polizei spricht von einem Todesopfer und mehreren, zum Teil schwer verletzten Personen.
items.body_text:
Großeinsatz - Täter noch unbekannt:Schweiz: Eine Tote, mehrere Verletzte nach Schüssen bei Rave-Party
|
In Aarau in der Schweiz sind bei einer Veranstaltung in der Nacht Schüsse gefallen. Die Polizei spricht von einem Todesopfer und mehreren, zum Teil schwer verletzten Personen.
Bei einer Rave-Veranstaltung ist in der Schweiz eine 22-jährige Frau durch einen oder mehrere Schüsse getötet worden. Vier Männer und eine Frau im Alter von 24 bis 27 Jahren seien teils schwer verletzt worden, berichtete die Kantonspolizei Aargau.
Alle Opfer hätten ihren Wohnsitz in der Schweiz, so die Behörden weiter. Ein oder mehrere Täter hatten am frühen Sonntagmorgen zahlreiche Schüsse abgegeben. Das Motiv für das Geschehen ist noch unklar. Nach dem oder den Tätern wurde intensiv gefahndet.
Kantonspolizei Aargau auf X

Die Behörden riefen die Bevölkerung dazu auf, das Gebiet zu meiden. Aarau im Kanton Aargau liegt etwa 40 Kilometer westlich von Zürich.
Der Kanton Aargau liegt zwischen Basel und Zürich.
Quelle: ZDF
Schüsse zunächst für Feuerwerk gehalten
Die Polizei bat darum, Video- und Bildmaterial an den Instagram-Kanal der Kantonspolizei Aargau zu senden. Tatort war das Rave-Event auf dem Gelände des Aargauischen Rennvereins. Der Verein sprach allen Angehörigen sein Mitgefühl aus.
Augenzeugen sagten der Zeitung "Blick", sie hätten die Schüsse zunächst für Feuerwerk gehalten. Anschließend seien viele Besucher der Technoparty in eine nahegelegene Turnhalle geflüchtet.
- Zeitpunkt: Bei einer Veranstaltung in Aarau in der Schweiz sind in der Nacht Schüsse gefallen.
- Opfer: Nach Angaben der Polizei handelt es sich bei dem Todesopfer um eine 22-jährige Frau, die noch vor Ort starb. Vier Männer und eine Frau im Alter von 24 bis 27 Jahren wurden leicht bis schwer verletzt. Alle Opfer sind laut Polizei Besucher eines Rave-Festivals gewesen und hatten ihren Wohnsitz in der Schweiz.
- Tatort: Tatort war die Pferderennbahn in Schachen, auf der zum Zeitpunkt des Geschehens laut Polizei ein Rave stattfand.
Quelle: dpa
- Zusammenhang mit dem Festival: Bisher gibt es von den Behörden keine Angaben dazu, wo genau die Schüsse fielen und welchen Zusammenhang es genau zu der Rave-Veranstaltung gab.
- Täter: Wer geschossen hat, ist bislang nicht bekannt. Die Fahndung nach der "unbekannten Täterschaft" läuft. Es ist bislang ebenfalls nicht bekannt, ob es einen oder mehrere Täter gab.
- Ablauf: Warum die Schüsse fielen, die genauen Umstände und der Ablauf der Tat sind bisher noch unklar und Gegenstand der Ermittlungen.
Quelle: dpa
Tatort war wohl Rave-Party
"Die Aarauer Rave-Party wurde von einem schweren Ereignis überschattet. Die zuständigen Einsatzkräfte wurden umgehend alarmiert und waren mit den notwendigen Mitteln vor Ort, um die Situation zu bewältigen und die erforderlichen Massnahmen einzuleiten", schrieb der Verein in einer Mitteilung.
Die Veranstalter hatten rund 3.500 Personen erwartet, wie es auf der Website hieß. Wie viele Personen zum Zeitpunkt der Schüsse auf dem Gelände waren, blieb vorerst unklar.
Aarau im Schweizer Kanton Aargau liegt etwa 40 Kilometer westlich von Zürich. Der Tatort liegt Luftlinie knapp 20 Kilometer von der deutschen Grenze entfernt.
Deutsche Polizei an Fahndung beteiligt
Auch die Polizei auf deutscher Seite ist an den allgemeinen Fahndungsmaßnahmen beteiligt. Dies sei reine Routine in der Polizeiarbeit, betonte ein Sprecher des Polizeipräsidiums Freiburg. Angaben zu den konkreten Maßnahmen machte er nicht.

items.title: Knappe Mehrheit im Referendum Island hat keine Lust auf EU-Beitrittsgespräche
items.summary: Island will auch weiterhin nicht in die EU. Schon die Aussicht auf neue Verhandlungen mit Brüssel geht einer knappen Mehrheit der Isländer zu weit. Vor allem außerhalb Reykjavíks setzt sich die Sorge vor einem Verlust der Selbstbestimmung durch. Dieser Beitrag Knappe Mehrheit im Referendum Island hat keine Lust auf EU-Beitrittsgespräche wurde veröffentlich auf JUNGE FREIHEIT.
items.body_text:
REYKJAVÍK. Die Isländer haben sich mit knapper Mehrheit gegen die Wiederaufnahme der Beitrittsverhandlungen mit der Europäischen Union ausgesprochen. Nach dem Endergebnis des Referendums stimmten 52,8 Prozent dagegen und 47,2 Prozent dafür. Zwischen beiden Lagern lagen damit lediglich rund 12.000 Stimmen.
Die Beteiligung erreichte 82,5 Prozent. Mehr als ein Fünftel der rund 270.000 Wahlberechtigten hatte seine Stimme bereits vor dem Abstimmungstag abgegeben.
Die sozialdemokratische Ministerpräsidentin Kristrún Frostadóttir hatte angekündigt, das Ergebnis unabhängig vom Ausgang zu akzeptieren. Abgestimmt wurde nicht über einen EU-Beitritt, sondern lediglich über die Fortsetzung der seit 2013 ruhenden Verhandlungen. Bei einem erfolgreichen Abschluss hätten die Isländer in einem zweiten Referendum über die Mitgliedschaft entschieden. Mit dem Nein bleibt der vor 13 Jahren eingeschlagene EU-Kurs vorerst eingefroren.
Fischerei wird für EU-Kurs zum Stolperstein
Den Ausschlag gaben vor allem die Gebiete außerhalb der Hauptstadt. Während Reykjavíks Wähler mehrheitlich für neue Gespräche votierten, überwog im ländlichen Raum die Sorge um Fischerei, Landwirtschaft und nationale Selbstbestimmung. Die Hauptstadt war laut der Auswertung des Ergebnisses die einzige Region, in der das Ja-Lager vorne lag.
Besonders umstritten war die Frage, ob Island unter der gemeinsamen EU-Fischereipolitik die Kontrolle über seine Fanggebiete behalten könnte. Fisch und andere Meeresprodukte machen rund 40 Prozent der isländischen Warenexporte aus. Frostadóttir hatte zwar versprochen, die Verhandlungen abzubrechen, falls Brüssel keine ausreichenden Sonderrechte gewähren sollte, konnte damit jedoch nicht genügend Wähler überzeugen.
Die Regierungschefin hatte zugleich mit der verschärften Sicherheitslage im Nordatlantik für die Annäherung an die EU geworben. Dabei verwies sie auf den Konflikt um Grönland und die Drohungen von US-Präsident Donald Trump, die zu Dänemark gehörende Insel den Vereinigten Staaten einzuverleiben. Die Gegner neuer Verhandlungen hielten dem entgegen, Islands Schutz sei durch die Nato und das bilaterale Verteidigungsabkommen mit den USA ausreichend gewährleistet.
Island stellte 2009 den ersten Antrag
Island gehört zu den Gründungsmitgliedern der Nato, verfügt jedoch über keine eigene Armee. Wirtschaftlich ist das Land über den Europäischen Wirtschaftsraum und das Schengen-Abkommen bereits eng mit der EU verbunden. Es besitzt damit Zugang zum Binnenmarkt, hat bei Entscheidungen in Brüssel aber kein Stimmrecht.
Den ersten Antrag auf EU-Mitgliedschaft hatte Island 2009 während der Finanzkrise gestellt. Nach der Parlamentswahl 2013 setzte eine EU-skeptische Regierung die Verhandlungen aus. Der Versuch Frostadóttirs, das Land erneut an den Verhandlungstisch zu führen, ist nun an den Wählern gescheitert. (rr)

items.title: Italian composer to present Elvish language piece at Oxford Tolkien 'moot'
items.summary: Abruzzo-born Pierpaolo Battista to perform Quenya composition
items.body_text:
An Italian musician, composer and
lecturer is to present a piece written in J.J.R. Tolkien's
Elvish language Quenya at the annual Oxonmoot celebration of the
Lord of the Rings and Hobbit author's works at his alma mater
Oxford on September 6.
                                    
                                       
				A 'moot' is a meeting of the living tree Ent characters in the
classic works.
                                    
                                       
				Abruzzo-born Pierpaolo Battista will give a lecture on 'Quenya
as an Instrument of Narrative Revelation' before performing the
composition in Tolkien's old university.
                                    
                                       
				Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni's has often cited The Lord of the
Rings as a foundational work for her values, as it is for her
right-wing party Brothers of Italy (FdI), which has neofascist
roots.
                                    
                                       
				FdI is steeped in Good vs Evil Tolkien lore and many of its
members, including Meloni, attended party-run Hobbit Camps as
youngsters.
                                    
                                       
				Meloni's September 2022 general-election win "is the Tolkien
generation getting into the premier's office", her friend the
right-wing intellectual Pietrangelo Buttafuoco, now the Venice
Biennale chief, told liberal la Repubblica daily after she
became Italy's first woman premier, referring to the camps where
the future FdI chief and her generation nurtured their cult
admiration for the work of Tolkien as expressing "what
conservatives believe in" as she herself had told the New York
Times.
                                    
                                       
				"It is the win of the (working class Roman beach) Coccia di
Morto over (highbrow liberal watering hole) Capalbio",
Buttafucoo went on.
                                    
                                       
				"It is the ex-baby sitter who made it, scorning all the little
ladies of the Roman upper class".
                                    
                                       
				
photo: Meloni at a Tolkien show in Rome

items.title: Venice dolphin sightings mean Adriatic fish stocks depleted
items.summary: Due to overfishing and water heating
items.body_text:
The increasing sightings of dolphins
in the waters off Venice indicate that fish stocks in the
Adriatic are being progressively depleted by overfishing and
water heating, forcing the marine mammals to come closer to
shore to feed, authorities said Friday.
                                    
                                       
				There are two 'official' dolphins in the lagoon, which have been
named Mimmo and Nane by Venetians.
                                    
                                       
				Another dolphin washed up dead in the lagoon this week.
                                    
                                       
				Tourists and fishermen have recently reported seeing other
exemplars.

items.title: Messico, oltre 40mila desaparecidos ancora 'attivi'
items.summary: Registrate pratiche successive a loro sparizione. Governo intensifica la ricerca
items.body_text:
Il governo messicano ha
rilevato che 40.628 persone registrate come scomparse hanno
realizzato pratiche o attività successive alla data della
sparizione, sebbene finora solo 6.939 casi contino su un
rapporto di ritrovamento confermato. Il dato emerge dalla
revisione del registro nazionale avviata in seguito alle riforme
del luglio 2025.
                                    
                                       
				Per chiarire i casi, l'esecutivo di Claudia Sheinbaum
incorporerà 10 specialisti in analisi dei dati, statistica e
intelligenza artificiale. Le autorità precisano che una traccia
successiva alla denuncia non implica automaticamente la
localizzazione dell'individuo. Parallelamente, le nuove
strategie hanno permesso di rintracciare migliaia di cittadini,
inclusi 1.075 individuati dalle brigate territoriali (l'86% dei
quali per allontanamento volontario).
                                    
                                       
				Il Messico affronta una crisi con oltre 130.000 desaparecidos. I
casi sono conteggiati dal 1964, ma oltre il 97% risale
all'inizio della guerra al narcotraffico nel 2006. La ministra
degli Interni Rosa Icela Rodríguez ha garantito che il governo
sta "modificando schemi di lavoro, innovando strategie, formando
il personale e usando gli strumenti necessari" per accelerare le
ricerche.

items.summary: Un morto e numerosi feriti nell’attacco israeliano nella Striscia di Gaza centrale. Lo riporta Al Jazeera. L’attacco è stato portato da un raid aereo di Israele su su...
items.body_text:
Gaza, raid di Israele: un morto e diversi feriti
Ieri l’esercito israeliano ha ucciso un capo di Hamas nascosto vicino a un ospedale
1' di lettura
1' di lettura
Un morto e numerosi feriti nell’attacco israeliano nella Striscia di Gaza centrale. Lo riporta Al Jazeera. L’attacco è stato portato da un raid aereo di Israele su su Deir el-Balah, nella Striscia di Gaza centrale. E’ rimasto ferito anche un gruppo di civili, trasportato all’ospedale dei martiri di al-Aqsa.
Chiedilo al Sole
In precedenza l’esercito israeliano ha riferito di aver ucciso dei miliziani comandanti di Hamas nell’attacco di ieri nella Striscia di Gaza, nella zona di Jabalia. Uno di loro - riferisce Al Jazeera - aveva preso parte all’attacco del 7 ottobre 2023. Un comandante di Hamas che stava pianificando attentati è stato ucciso in un attacco israeliano nella parte centrale della Striscia di Gaza, ha dichiarato l’esercito dello stato ebraico.
Le Idf (Forze di Difesa israeliane) hanno riferito che il comandante è stato preso di mira in un attacco nella zona di Deir al-Balah, mentre «si nascondeva nelle immediate vicinanze dell’ospedale Shuhada al-Aqsa». L’esercito ha dichiarato di aver adottato misure per ridurre al minimo i danni ai civili presenti nella zona.
“Questo è un altro esempio dell’uso cinico da parte di Hamas delle infrastrutture umanitarie e dell’inserimento sistematico dell’organizzazione terroristica all’interno di strutture mediche per portare avanti e compiere attività terroristiche”, ha denunciato l’esercito.

«L’accordo Usa-Venezuela sul petrolio? È perfetto, ma solo per Washington»
La geologa Irúa Euribe, ex Pdvsa, illustra i rischi per Caracas dell’intesa sul petrolio annunciata da Trump
2' di lettura
2' di lettura
Non ci sono dubbi, è l’accordo del secolo. Per Trump, naturalmente. È un «negocio redondo», un affare perfetto. Lo dice chiaro Irúa Euribe, geologa venezuelana che ha lavorato a Pdvsa, la società energetica di Stato, la cassaforte di Caracas. Ne parla da Houston, dove ha partecipato al Global energy summit dei giorni scorsi.
Chiedilo al Sole
Dottoressa Euribe, Donald Trump annuncia un grande accordo che pare un esproprio. É così?
Sì, ora “controlleranno” 65 miliardi di barili di greggio, una quantità importante, considerato che le riserve provate del Venezuela ammontano a 300 miliardi di barili e sono le più grandi del mondo.
Un’intesa di questa portata avrà bisogno di un passaggio al Parlamento del Venezuela. O forse persino una riforma della Costituzione. No, purtroppo no. La nuova Legge degli idrocarburi, che Trump ha surrettiziamente imposto lo scorso gennaio, prevede un allegato, il “Regolamento”, i cui contenuti sono stati resi noti solo in luglio, che omette di indicare la durata delle concessioni alle società americane e quindi Trump può fare ciò che vuole senza alcun passaggio parlamentare di Caracas. Ovviamente gli Stati Uniti non saranno proprietari dei bacini ma avranno il diritto di sfruttarli. Poi un altro punto chiave: la creazione di una società-veicolo, di cui l’Amministrazione Trump controllerà il 51%. Questa “società-ombrello” consentirà alle compagnie americane di effettuare scelte operative senza alcuna complicazione tecnica o giuridica.
Come si è arrivati a un accordo di questo tipo senza inciampare nei vincoli giuridici che i Paesi petroliferi prevedono per le compagnie straniere?Vi è stato un progressivo svuotamento di Pdvsa, all’idea iniziale di uno “spezzatino” ne sono seguite altre. Ed è stata sfruttata la debolezza economica in cui attualmente versa Pdvsa. Proprio a Houston c’è la sede di Schlumberger, la più grande società di servizi petroliferi al mondo. Ebbene, Schlumberger avrà il monopolio degli “studi integrati”. Ovvero la mappatura dettagliata di tutti i dati tecnici necessari per avviare la fase di esplorazione e produzione. É una posizione di concorrenza sleale che mette totalmente fuori gioco Pdvsa. Ma le operazioni “sleali” sono state anche altre.

Mosca: pronti a sferrare massicci attacchi contro settori energetici ucraini
Nella notte le forze ucraine hanno preso di mira un’importante raffineria di petrolio nell’oblast di Leningrado, nella Russia nord-occidentale, e una base aerea nel territorio di Krasnodar
1' di lettura
1' di lettura
La Russia si prepara ad “attacchi massicci” contro i siti energetici ucraini in risposta ai raid di Kiev contro siti civili, riferiscono gli alti vertici del Cremlino, scrive l’agenzia Tass.
Chiedilo al Sole
Intanto il direttore della Cia, John Ratcliffe, ha proposto un incontro trilaterale tra Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin e Volodymyr Zelensky durante la sua visita a Mosca all’inizio di questa settimana. Lo riferiscono ad Axios due fonti. La visita di Ratcliffe, aggiungono le fonti, aveva anche l’obiettivo di capire se i vertici dei servizi di intelligence russi potessero contribuire a convincere Putin a riprendere i negoziati con l’Ucraina sotto la mediazione degli Stati Uniti.
Nella notte le forze ucraine hanno preso di mira un’importante raffineria di petrolio nell’oblast di Leningrado, nella Russia nord-occidentale, e una base aerea nel territorio di Krasnodar, riferisce The Kyiv Independent. Secondo quanto riportato dal canale Telegram Exilenova Plus, una delle più grandi raffinerie di petrolio della Russia (l’impianto Kirishi Petroleum Organic Synthesis, noto anche come impianto Kinef) è stata data alle fiamme dopo essere stata attaccata dalle forze ucraine nell’oblast di Leningrado.
La struttura è soggetta alle sanzioni occidentali contro la Russia emanate dagli alleati dell’Ucraina, comprese le misure imposte dagli Stati Uniti. Il governatore dell’oblast di Leningrado, Aleksandr Drozdenko, ha confermato che «è stato segnalato lo schianto di un drone nelle vicinanze di una raffineria nel distretto di Kirishi, con conseguente incendio», mentre 42 droni sono stati abbattuti nella regione. Nel frattempo, una base aerea è stata colpita nella città di Yeysk, nel territorio di Krasnodar, in Russia, dove testimoni oculari hanno riferito di una serie di forti esplosioni.

items.title: Política
items.summary: Un mes después de la entrada masiva, ante la desesperación de los ceutíes y el pasmo del Gobierno, el Estado no ha sido capaz de devolver la normalidad a una ciudad amenazada ni de gestionar racionalmente la relación con Marruecos
items.body_text:
- Primer plano Jabaroot, el hacker que ha provocado el mayor golpe a la inteligencia de Rabat tras la crisis de Ceuta: "Es un ex espía marroquí que vive en Alemania"
- Política Feijóo exige que comparezca la directora del CNI y anuncia que el PP se personará en la causa por Ceuta: "Alguien miente"
España se asoma a su Historia en la crisis de Ceuta. Se cumple un mes de la entrada, masiva y sin precedentes, de 72.000 personas de Marruecos por la frontera de la ciudad autónoma española. Lo que el presidente del Gobierno calificó como un «ataque contra la integridad territorial» ha derivado en el colapso de la vida cotidiana en la ciudad Ceuta, con problemas de orden público.
Entre 5.000 y 8.000 inmigrantes, el Gobierno no sabe cuántos, deambulan por las calles, plazas y playas imposibilitando la vida cotidiana de sus habitantes. La desesperación de los ceutíes ha ido avanzando este mes en paralelo con el pasmo, el desconcierto y la incredulidad de un Gobierno atónito por lo que estaba sucediendo. Tres semanas después de la llegada masiva, Pedro Sánchez decretó el mando único que el presidente Juan Jesús Vivas le había pedido el primer día. Moncloa ha ido tomando decisiones que suponían una rectificación en toda regla de la reacción inicial. El alivio por el regreso de la inmensa mayoría de los que llegaron confundió al Ejecutivo, que no reparó en los que se habían quedado, y en las consecuencias de no tener donde alojarlos.
«No es sólo la peor crisis a la que se ha enfrentado el Gobierno en toda la legislatura. Es una crisis de Estado en la que el Estado no ha sido capaz de desplegar todos sus recursos para recuperar la vida gravemente alterada en una ciudad históricamente amenazada por Marruecos. Nos ha pillado en un momento electoral, el peor para afrontar una situación tan grave para la que no hay soluciones mágicas. Una crisis de Estado exigiría responsabilidad de Estado, primero al Gobierno, y después a todas las instituciones; desgraciadamente en la España actual no hay posibilidades de entendimiento ni generosidad por parte del Gobierno ni de la oposición. Nadie se quiere elevar por encima del combate electoral. Al Gobierno le pilla débil y al PP con ganas de dar la puntilla a Pedro Sánchez. El resultado es la imagen de un Estado aparentemente inerme para recuperar la normalidad en Ceuta y gestionar con inteligencia las relaciones con Marruecos, que siempre han sido difíciles». Así es cómo resumen dirigentes políticos actuales y ex altos cargos de Estado el reto al que se enfrenta nuestro país en Ceuta. «Con aromas de pequeño 98 del régimen del 78», resume un buen conocedor del funcionamiento del Estado.
«El presidente del Gobierno lleva callado un mes, no sabemos lo que nos va a decir en su entrevista el lunes en la Ser y después en su comparecencia en el Congreso. El Gobierno ha ofrecido una penosa imagen de impotencia, el PSOE se encuentra completamente bloqueado y la marca bajo mínimos. Es necesario un plan para devolver a todos los que entraron el 30 de julio. Marruecos ha evidenciado que puede ocupar la ciudad de Ceuta sin disparar un solo tiro ni mandar al Ejército. En el fondo, esta crisis también ha dejado en mal lugar la habilidad diplomática del Gobierno en sus relaciones con el régimen marroquí. Ellos van provocando poco a poco y si no estás atento y no lo percibes, al final te acaban montando un gran lío. Lo han hecho siempre. Nunca de forma tan grave como la entrada de 72.000 personas de golpe. España tiene que tener garantías de que esto no va a volver a pasar», aseguran fuentes socialistas y ex altos cargos del PSOE consultados.
A la espera de lo que diga Pedro Sánchez, la estrategia de mandar a los ministros al Parlamento para suplir la no comparecencia del presidente no ha salido muy bien. Ha sido «como un funeral», señala un parlamentario. La discrepancia de versiones entre la ministra de Defensa, Margarita Robles, que afirmó con rotundidad que el CNI había avisado a las Fuerzas de Seguridad de un aumen

items.title: Política
items.summary: La FEMP ha convocado concentraciones en los ayuntamientos el 2 de septiembre que la izquierda crítica por haberlo hecho de forma "unilateral"
items.body_text:
- Política Feijóo y la cúpula del PP se ponen al frente de las manifestaciones por Ceuta el día antes del cara a cara con Sánchez
- Análisis La parálisis de Sánchez en Ceuta hunde a España en una crisis de Estado
El PSOE ha dado instrucciones a sus alcaldes y concejales para que no secunden las concentraciones del 2 de septiembre convocadas por la Federación Española de Municipios y Provincias (FEMP) a las puertas de todos los ayuntamientos para protestar por la gestión del Gobierno central de la situación en Ceuta tras la llegada masiva de 72.000 personas de forma ilegal. Según el socio mayoritario de la coalición al frente de La Moncloa, esta acción ha sido decidida por el PP "de forma unilateral, sin acuerdo y vulnerando el funcionamiento democrático" de la propia organización que representa a las entidades locales.
En una circular remitida este sábado a todas las federaciones del partido, la dirección de Ferraz argumenta que la formación de Alberto Núñez Feijóo está tratando de "manipular esta crisis humanitaria" como "elemento de movilización y confrontación" para "ir en contra" del Ejecutivo de Pedro Sánchez. Por ello, comunican a sus cargos que se ha decidido "no participar" en unas protestas convocadas a las 20.00 horas del miércoles, la víspera de la comparecencia del presidente del Gobierno en el Congreso para dar explicaciones sobre esta cuestión.
"Que no manipulen nuestra posición con respecto a Ceuta. Estamos con el pueblo de Ceuta y con los/las ceutís, pero no toleramos la utilización partidista y electoral", añaden en la cúpula socialista. Asimismo, manifiestan su "profunda condena y rechazo a toda forma de violencia, sin equidistancias ni ambigüedades", tras los incidentes registrados en los últimos días en la ciudad autónoma, incluidas la agresión a militares y la destrucción de chabolas de inmigrantes que permanecen en la playa del Trampolín.
También IU-Compromis-Comuns-Podemos, ERC y Junts han denunciado esta semana que la presidenta de la FEMP, María José García-Pelayo, ha llevado a cabo "actuaciones unilaterales" en referencia a la convocatoria de la protesta. Asimismo, han tratado de presionar para que hubiera una rectificación, porque consideran que la alcaldesa del PP ha actuado "a hechos consumados, sin contar con el respaldo ni la aprobación del resto de grupos políticos".
Pese a las críticas internas sobre la gestión de la crisis, incluso en el PSOE menos alineado con Ferraz critican que el partido líder de la oposición se ha "saltado los órganos de gobierno de una institución para hace partidismo". Así lo ha expresado la regidora de Palencia, Miriam Andrés, que ha trasladado que lo que hará su Ayuntamiento será presentar una "declaración de apoyo a Ceuta".
Comparecencia de la directora del CNI
Por otro lado, los socialistas han respondido al presidente del PP que la directora del CNI podría comparecer en el Congreso pero no en el Senado, después de que Feijóo dijera que la van a citar allí para dar explicaciones sobre la crisis migratoria. En concreto, quiere que Esperanza Casteleiro esclarezca las discrepancias dentro del Gobierno sobre la existencia o no de informes previos de inteligencia avisando de la llegada masiva del 30 de julio.
En declaraciones remitidas a los medios, el portavoz del PSOE en la Cámara Alta, Juan Espadas, ha acusado al dirigente popular de querer "hacer de líder de la extrema derecha" en España ya que, tal y como ha recordado, fue Vox quien solicitó el viernes la comparecencia de la directora del CNI en el Senado. Asimismo, ha recalcado que la Mesa la rechazó "por unanimidad" esta solicitud porque, según señaló, "solo puede comparecer ante la Comisión de Secretos Oficiales del Congreso de los Diputados, como marca la normativa vigente".

items.title: Sucesos
items.summary: Los cuatro reconocieron la agresión y un juzgado sustituyó la pena de dos años de cárcel por cinco años de expulsión de España
items.body_text:
- España Los militares temen más emboscadas de inmigrantes en Ceuta y piden ser agentes de la autoridad
- Interior Un sargento herido y cuatro marroquíes detenidos tras una segunda emboscada contra militares en Ceuta
Cuatro migrantes marroquíes, de los que protagonizaron la entrada masiva en la ciudad el pasado 30 de julio, han sido expulsados a Marruecos por orden judicial después de haber sido detenidos en la ciudad por agredir a tres agentes de la Guardia Civil que requirieron su documentación.
Los hechos se produjeron este pasado miércoles a las 20.30 horas en las inmediaciones de la barriada del Sarchal cuando los cuatro acusados estaban en la zona junto a otro grupo de migrantes y portaban objetos punzantes y armas blancas con las que habían amenazado a varios vecinos del barrio.
La Guardia Civil acudió a la zona para su localización tras el requerimiento de los ciudadanos, procediendo a detener a cuatro de ellos después de una persecución en el transcurso de la cual se abalanzaron sobre tres de los agentes, produciéndoles lesiones leves, según han informado a Efe fuentes judiciales.
Un juzgado de Ceuta ha ordenado su expulsión de España tras haber reconocido su implicación en los hechos y aceptar una condena de dos años de prisión cada uno de ellos por un delito de atentado, que se ha sustituido por cinco años de expulsión de España.

OTRO FALLECIDO EN EL MAR
La presión migratoria dejó además este fin de semana una nueva víctima mortal. La Guardia Civil localizó a última hora del sábado el cadáver de un joven subsahariano en aguas próximas a Punta Almina, en la bahía norte de Ceuta, después de que un buque militar alertara de la presencia de un cuerpo en el mar.
Los GEAS recuperaron el cadáver, que únicamente vestía un traje de neopreno y llevaba poco tiempo sin vida. Por el lugar en el que fue encontrado, alejado de la frontera, los investigadores barajan que tratara de alcanzar Ceuta a nado desde Marruecos o que se hubiese lanzado al agua desde una embarcación sin conseguir llegar a tierra. El cuerpo fue trasladado a la base del Servicio Marítimo para practicarle la autopsia.

CULTOS
Doce horas junto a la Virgen de la Salud de San Gonzalo
La hermandad inicia un nuevo culto con la dolorosa en besamanos
Doce horas de besamanos para rendir pleitesía a la Virgen de la Salud en San Gonzalo en el cierre de agosto, coincidiendo con el regreso de las vacaciones y el inicio de un nuevo curso cofrade.
Doce horas de largas colas para rezar, venerar ... y besar las manos de la Virgen de la Salud, una de las devociones más arraigadas al barrio de San Gonzalo y a la propia hermandad desde sus orígenes. Una jornada también para dar gracias, pedir y reencontrarse con la que cada año reúne a cientos de fieles en torno a su devoción.
Desde primera hora de la mañana, en la plaza de San Gonzalo, hermanos y fieles aguardaban la apertura de las puertas para visitar a la Virgen de la Salud, situada en la nave lateral del templo, delante del Señor del Soberano Poder.
Los primeros devotos que acudieron al besamanos de la Virgen de la Salud pudieron deleitarse con el aroma de los nardos, una de las flores más destacadas de este tiempo y de las más arraigadas a la ciudad, junto al azahar, que envolvían a la dolorosa junto a las clavellinas en color buganvilla, entre otras.
En el primero de los besamanos de la Virgen de la Salud, ya que el segundo, el de reglas, tiene lugar en el mes de octubre, suele destacar la cerámica de Triana y las dos fuentes de agua natural, restauradas recientemente, que representan la advocación de la titular de San Gonzalo.
El conjunto, de marcado carácter trianero, pone de manifiesto la unión de la hermandad con Triana. Asimismo, los detalles de la cerámica y las fuentes sirven como marco para una de las estampas más esperadas por sus hermanos y fieles en el inicio de un nuevo curso.

Mansilla de las Mulas (León) exhibe en su Feria del Tomate un producción «abundante y de muy buena calidad y sabor»
La recolección de este año alcanza los 300.000 kilos
León
Mansilla de las Mulas (León) celebra este domingo la jornada central de su XXXVII Feria del Tomate, que congrega a numerosos asistentes en el entorno de la Plaza del Grano de la localidad, donde se instalan los puntos de venta del preciado producto, en una ... cita que premia los mejores ejemplares entre las muestras recogidas en los expositores.
Este año la producción se considera «muy buena, abundante, de muy buena calidad y sabor, con un tomate muy limpio y de buen tamaño», según explicó a la agencia Ical el presidente de la Promotora de la Indicación Geográfica Protegida del Tomate de Mansilla de las Mulas, José Miguel Olmo, quien señaló que el intenso calor vivido durante varias jornadas no perjudicó la evolución del cultivo; más bien contribuyó a aumentar el tamaño de las piezas. Además expresó su confianza en que las frescas jornadas vividas en días pasados tampoco causen problemas.
Noticia relacionada
Sin querer aventurar cifras concretas, la producción de este año se considera similar a la de otras campañas sin sobresaltos, con unos 300.000 kilogramos recolectados entre los integrantes de la cooperativa y una veintena de agricultores profesionales que tienen en el tomate uno de sus principales cultivos, aunque los datos ofrecidos en alguna ocasión superaron ampliamente los 400.000.
Respecto al proceso para la obtención de la Indicación Geográfica Protegida (IGP) para el tomate de Mansilla, iniciado hace ya un lustro, el presidente de la Promotora reconoce una vez más que el asunto «sigue parado de momento». «Seguimos con el objetivo» asegura al tiempo que detalla que no se ha remitido nueva documentación no realizado más gestiones al respecto desde entonces.
La Feria del Tomate de Mansilla, inaugurada a mediodía, contó también con una nutrida representación institucional, con la presencia entre otras autoridades y cargos institucionales y políticos del vicepresidente primero y consejero de Desregulación, Familia y Ayudas Sociales, Carlos Pollán, el subdelegado del Gobierno en León, Héctor Alaiz, la secretaria general de la Unión del Pueblo Leonés, Alicia García, la vicesecretaria general del Partido Socialista de Castilla y León, Nuria Rubio, el diputado de Turismo, Octavio González o el líder provincial del PSOE, Javier Alfonso Cendón, quienes arroparon a la alcaldesa de Mansilla, Vicenta García, y tuvieron ocasión de recorrer los puestos instalados, comprobar la calidad y sabor de los tomates e incluso comprarlos, en algún caso.

items.body_text:
Productores ecológicos piden usar forrajes convencionales de forma «puntual» por la sequía
Proecogal reclama a las administraciones mecanismos excepcionales para garantizar la alimentación del ganado y evitar que se agoten las reservas de las explotaciones
ABC
Santiago
La Asociación de Productores de Ecolóxico de Galicia (Proecogal) ha reclamado «medidas urgentes» para hacer frente a los efectos de la sequía y de las elevadas temperaturas en las explotaciones de este tipo. Entre las sugeridas, citan la posibilidad de autorizar temporalmente el uso de ... hierba seca o forrajes convencionales de proximidad para paliar la pérdida de alimento ecológico causada.
A través de un comunicado, recogido por EP, la asociación explica que la falta de pastos y forrajes está provocando que las reservas destinadas para el invierno se estén agotando. Esto, según expone, está obligando a las explotaciones a acudir antes de lo previsto al mercado para garantizar la alimentación del ganado, «en un contexto de escasez e incremento de los precios generalizado».
Por ello, Proecogal considera «imprescindible» que las administraciones «actúen ya» y articulen «mecanismos excepcionales para una situación excepcional». En ello, incluyen la posibilidad de autorizar temporalmente el uso de hierba seca o forrajes convencionales de proximidad en las explotaciones afectadas por la carencia de alimento ecológico.
Precisa que esto se trataría de un uso «muy reducido y puntual» de alimento convencional, «limitado a las circunstancias excepcionales actuales y siempre dentro del marco de la normativa europea», incide. Esta tendría el objetivo de garantizar la alimentación de los animales y la continuidad de las explotaciones.
La asociación ya ha mantenido una reunión con el Consejo Regulador de la Agricultura Ecológica de Galicia (Craega) para trasladar directamente la problemática que están viviendo los productores. A su vez, el organismo remitió la cuestión a la Axencia Galega de Calidade Alimentaria (Agacal), adscrita a la Consellería do Medio Rural. De este modo, Proecogal considera «fundamental» que los dos entes actúen «coordinadamente» para buscar una solución.
«Desde Proecogal estamos llamando a todas las puertas que tienen responsabilidad para defender los intereses de nuestros asociados y, en general, de los productores y productoras del sector ecológico. No vamos a dejar de insistir hasta que se adopten medidas que permitan afrontar esta situación», señala la entidad.
Además, considera que la prioridad ahora es «tomar decisiones antes de que las reservas se agoten completamente». Al mismo tiempo, reclama avanzar en un plan específico de adaptación del sector ecológico gallego a la sequía y a los episodios de calor extremo.

items.title: Darializa Ávila Chevalier, the Afro-Latina socialist with one foot in Congress: ‘We need an economic system that gives people dignity’
items.summary: Backed by Mamdani, the Dominican American candidate stunned New York’s political establishment with an upset victory in the Democratic primary
items.body_text:
Darializa Ávila Chevalier, the Afro-Latina socialist with one foot in Congress: ‘We need an economic system that gives people dignity’
Backed by Mamdani, the Dominican American candidate stunned New York’s political establishment with an upset victory in the Democratic primary
She is slender, dressed in a blue linen shirt, high-waisted jeans and Veja sneakers. Her curls are neatly arranged, she wears white-framed glasses and a nose piercing. But none of these things define Darializa Ávila Chevalier quite as much as the way her calm face changes when confronted with an injustice. She describes it as a “visceral reaction.” The moment she says it, her expression shifts, and the 32-year-old graduate student from Upper Manhattan begins to resemble the politician she has become: the first person of Dominican descent who could make it to Washington as a member of Congress.
One afternoon during the second week of August, as students across New York headed back to school, Chevalier could be seen in St. James Park in the northeast Bronx handing out backpacks and school supplies to children and parents from the neighborhood lined up in an endless queue. One by one, they approached her, and she let them choose between a pink backpack, a gray one, one with blue flowers and a green one. Chevalier smiled shyly. “Hi, how are you? What’s your name?” she greeted them, in English or Spanish.
At her side stood Gustavo Rivera, a Democratic New York State senator from Puerto Rico who has represented the Bronx’s 33rd Senate District for the past 16 years. As Darializa handed out the gifts, Rivera stepped forward: “Do you know who she is? This is Darializa Ávila Chevalier. She’s going to be your next congresswoman,” he told the crowd.
The children and their parents looked at her, nodded, took their backpacks and moved on. Rivera knows exactly what he is doing: the veteran politician is introducing his community to a new generation of leadership, offering the trust and political capital he has spent more than a decade building in the neighborhood.
“A lot of people still don’t know her, and I’m telling them: trust me. She’s going to do the job she’s supposed to do. She puts the interests of the working class at the center of her political plan,” Rivera says.
Today her face appears in some of the city’s most prominent magazines and television programs, but until a few months ago Chevalier was virtually unknown, someone who had spent the previous 14 years as a community organizer, work that, in her words, “nobody thanks you for and that goes largely unnoticed.”
In fact, when veteran Congressman Adriano Espaillat, 71, faced her in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for New York’s 13th Congressional District, which includes Upper Manhattan neighborhoods such as Harlem and Washington Heights as well as part of the Bronx, he repeatedly reminded voters that she had never held elected office. Another line of attack was to portray her as an outsider, emphasizing that she was originally from Florida and even suggesting at one point that people like her should be sent “back home.”
Espaillat arrived as a child from the Dominican Republic, lived as an undocumented immigrant and was one of the first migrants to enter Congress, a seat he has held since he succeeded Charles B. Rangel 10 years ago. New York made him a New Yorker, just as it had done for Chevalier after she moved to the city at 18 to attend Columbia University.
“I love this city; it made me the woman I am,” Chevalier says. If you ask her for a recommendation on a place to party or eat in Miami, where she was born in 1993, she wouldn’t know what to tell you. But if you ask about a spot in Harlem or Washington Heights, she’ll quickly name Harlem’s Hub, Barawine, or Papasito on Dyckman Street. “I used to go there with my friends, but it closed during the pandemic; we miss it a lot,” she says.
At some point, Chevalier stopped being a long-shot challenger and became a serious threat to Espaillat. It happen

items.title: The shadow of the United States lengthens over southern Greenland: ‘We are going to lose our homes’
items.summary: Donald Trump’s interest in controlling the vast Danish island and exploiting its natural resources worries the population
items.body_text:
The shadow of the United States lengthens over southern Greenland: ‘We are going to lose our homes’
Donald Trump’s interest in controlling the vast Danish island and exploiting its natural resources worries the population
The Narsarsuaq Museum no longer has set opening hours. Since the airport closed in the spring, few visitors come to this remote settlement in southern Greenland. However, if someone asks for Ole Guldager’s house and goes to ask him to open it, he is happy to oblige. The museum occupies one of the barracks of the former military base, a long wooden building painted red with a brick chimney. Beside the entrance sits the radial engine of a World War II aircraft, corroded by decades of exposure to the elements. Behind the building stretches the airstrip that U.S. soldiers built in record time. Today, however, that same country appears not as an ally from the past but as a growing threat to the island’s sovereignty and natural resources, especially in places like Narsarsuaq, one of three bases the United States would seek to reopen.
When Guldager turns on the lights, uniforms, rifles and carbines, field telephones, a metal stretcher from the old hospital, slot machines and letters confiscated by censors that described extreme isolation and never reached their destination emerge from the gloom. The rooms reconstruct the daily life of the thousands of U.S. servicemen, pilots, and nurses who passed through the former base. Among the hundreds of photographs are several of Marlene Dietrich, taken in 1944. For a few hours, the actress brought a bit of Hollywood glitz to that inhospitable corner of fjords and mountains to lift the troops’ spirits.
Guldager arrived in Narsarsuaq as a child. He was born in Denmark, but his father worked at the civil airport into which the former military installation was converted after the Americans left in the late 1950s. A historian and archaeologist — and one of the island’s few beekeepers — he has devoted much of his 58 years to researching the place where he grew up and chose to stay.
The last plane landed in April. The airport was closed because another one opened in Qaqortoq, the regional capital, where about 3,000 people live, and it made no sense to maintain two for such a small population. But the reality is that since then Narsarsuaq has been emptying out. Guldager estimates that of the 150 residents it had, about 40 remain. Everything revolved around the airport, which for more than six decades was the main gateway to the island’s south, handling thousands of passengers each summer. Now there are weeks when barely a dozen visitors arrive. The hotel, one of Greenland’s largest, closed its doors the same day the airfield shut down.
Among those who do not plan to leave is Storch Lund. The grandson of Henrik Lund — the poet who wrote the lyrics to Greenland’s anthem — he grew up on a farm across the fjord and moved to this shore as a teenager to work as a mechanic’s apprentice. He went on to run the airport for more than two decades, and also ran a café and a souvenir shop that closed a few months ago. He also started a company to transport tourists to other settlements. Today, only one of his boats still operates with low demand; the other two remain moored. At 69, he finds it hard to accept that “nothing happens in Narsarsuaq anymore.”
It is into that void that the United States now reappears.
As the village withers, the shadow of Donald Trump lengthens over it. The U.S. president, who tried to buy Greenland from Denmark during his first term, threatened earlier this year to take control of the island “the easy way or the hard way.” Tensions eased after several European allies deployed troops to the Arctic territory in support of Danish sovereignty, and the crisis moved onto a diplomatic track. items.title: A three-year-old’s broken world after his father’s immigration detention
items.summary: When a parent is taken away by ICE, a child’s world implodes. The long-term consequences include depression, anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder
items.body_text:
A three-year-old’s broken world after his father’s immigration detention
When a parent is taken away by ICE, a child’s world implodes. The long-term consequences include depression, anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder
This report was produced by MindSite News, a nonprofit news website covering mental health that publishes a free newsletter. It was produced in collaboration with CatchLight as part of its three-year Visual Reporting on Mental Health Initiative.
When the father of pre-schooler Carlos Carino* was taken into custody in Los Angeles last September by ICE agents and brought to a detention center in California’s Central Valley, the changes in Carlos were immediately evident.
He refused to participate in circle time at preschool. He cried frequently in school and at home. And he started calling everyone ‘Papi,’ — Daddy in English, but also a term of endearment for children in Latin American countries.
For six months, the family navigated the separation as they fought in court for the release of Carlos’s father, Miguel Carino*. They had reason for hope — or so they believed.
Carlos is like one of every five children in California — they live in mixed-status families in which at least one member is undocumented; across the country, there are some 4.7 million mixed-status households. As these families cope with aggressive immigration enforcement, a parent’s detention can launch them into multiple layers of trauma, buffeted by events they can’t control. The consequences are severe: A report by six psychiatrists in Psychiatric News noted that prolonged separation between children and their immigrant parents “can undermine attachment security and increase children’s vulnerability to anxiety, depression, and behavioral problems.”
Carlos’ father had been living in Los Angeles for nearly 25 years, owned a small construction business in his neighborhood of East Los Angeles and employed other workers. Jazmin, his wife of five years, is a U.S. citizen, and Miguel had applied for an “adjustment of status” based on his marriage. Then he was detained during what his attorneys assumed would be a routine check-in with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Enforcement (USCIS).
Jazmin, 24, tried to keep the family connected while taking on extra house-cleaning shifts. She and Carlos started making the five-hour round-trip to the Central Valley twice a month. But the visits were painful, and they distressed Carlitos.
“We couldn’t hold hands, we couldn’t get up from our seats,” Jazmin recalled. “When it was time to say good-bye, my son didn’t want to let go of him.” But after a while, even these constrained visits seemed to help Carlos. One morning, he arrived at his pre-school wearing a hand-knit beanie that his father had made for him.
“He kept it on all day and was happier than he had been,” recalled Ana Soto*, an early education assistant at the preschool. He wore the beanie daily, as if he were wearing a piece of his father.
“One day, I called for him: ‘Papi, come over here,’” Soto said. “He looked at me and said, ‘I am not Papi, I am Carlos.’” To Soto, that signaled a greater sense of security.
But in March, faced with the prospect of his likely deportation and exhausted by the brutal conditions at the detention center, Miguel decided to self-deport to Tijuana, Mexico. Jazmin tried to cope, taking Carlos to visit him in Tijuana. Then, in April, Miguel moved further south to Mexico City so he could seek work to support himself. Mexico City is far away, and the family does not have the resources to fly there. Carlos hasn’t seen his father in person for three months and it’s unclear when he will see him again. Now the family must try to stay connected through video and phone calls, and Carlos’s confidence and ease are fading again.

Amsterdam Centraal stabbing suspect identified after four injured
The suspect in the Saturday evening's stabbing at Amsterdam Centraal has been identified as a 43-year-old man from Naarden. Four people, including the suspect, were stabbed at around 19:30 p.m. and taken to a hospital. The suspect was then arrested. Some passerby at De Ruijterkade, at the back of the station, witnessed the incident, NU.nl reported.
The police have also confirmed that the altercation between the suspect and the others was indeed livestreamed on TikTok.
According to NU.nl, the livestream recording shows an escalating argument. First, the person filming yelled, "Do not touch," a couple of times. "I am not afraid of six or seven men," the person said. “They are all going to fall."
The footage then indeed reportedly shows someone falling and the person filming making stabbing motions towards them.
The police are still unsure about what led to the fight.

items.summary: The Dutch football association KNVB wants for the FIFA President Gianni Infantino to be replaced,
items.body_text:
Dutch football association KNVB wants Infantino to be replaced as the FIFA president
The Dutch football association KNVB wants for the FIFA President Gianni Infantino to be replaced, NOS reports based on a letter from the KNVB to Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) President Aleksander Ceferin. The Dutch association also does not want Infantino to attend an international summit in Amsterdam, where KNVB wants to discuss the change in leadership.
"The KNVB no longer has confidence in FIFA President Gianni Infantino. We believe that FIFA needs new leadership, but a new president alone is not enough. The way FIFA is governed must also change," the association stated. FIFA is the top international football governing body.
Gijs de Jong, Secretary General of the KNVB, said he does not want Infantino to attend the meeting because “we have lost the trust. He is not welcome at this meeting about the future. He is the past."
NOS reported that KNVB itself made proposals for a new FIFA in the letter and offered to host the international summit in Amsterdam.
"The KNVB would like to organize such a summit in Amsterdam, a city with a special place in FIFA's history. Where, in 1928, almost a century ago, the decision was made for the first time to hold a World Cup," the football association wrote to UEFA President Ceferin.
KNVB does not just want Infantino gone - it also argues for some changes, such as making sure the president does not interfere with daily operations. It also argues that the new leadership itself would need to be supervised by an independent body and to be open to explaining its decisions in press conferences.
"Everyone who is open to a new FIFA is welcome," de Jong said about the summit.
European football officials recently met up in Monaco, where, among other things, it was announced that UEFA is preparing a criminal case against Infantino.

items.body_text:
Amsterdam’s baby raves: families reconnect with toddler techno
Hannah Docter-Loeb
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
It’s 1pm on a Sunday, and a line has already formed outside Noorderlicht in Amsterdam. Some attendees are dressed in flowy shirts, glitter patterns on their faces, and sunglasses, as if they are going to a music festival. But it’s not your average festival: it’s a Tiny Grooves family rave. And every parent has their kid in tow (or in a pram).
Inside the venue lies a free glitter bar, craft corner, play zone, and of course, a DJ set. The event is a chance for the young ones to dance their energy out, making naptime even easier. But parents can also unwind with their kids in sight, drink in hand.
Family raves have become a phenomenon over the past decade, most recently with toddler techno taking the world by storm. Tiny Grooves brings a similar concept to the Netherlands, providing a space for parents – and their kids – to dance, socialise, and connect.
“It’s a way to introduce your kids to the music you love, and the scene that you love, at a safe time, in a safe place, and at a time that suits your family,” says co-founder Morgan Andrews.
It originally started as a joke. Andrews and co-founder Samantha Barker had connected in 2020, connecting over their shared experience as Aussies in the Netherlands. They stayed friends, having their first kids within a few weeks of each other. And two years ago, when they were on maternity leave at the same time, they started to “lose their minds” during baby sensory classes and the like.
“They’re very much focused on your kid,” explains Barker. “We felt like there’s nothing really where us parents could really go and share an experience with our kids but have it be more catered.” Not to mention, going out to a festival – which both mothers enjoy – can be tough as a parent. The two wanted to find a way to host events for parents to connect with the person they were before having a kid, without disconnecting from being a parent. And thus, Tiny Grooves was born.
In May 2024, the two printed flyers for their first event, handing them out at parks and putting them in Bakfiets around their neighbourhood. Next thing they knew, they had a sold-out event, an equal mix of Dutchies and internationals just looking for a chance to groove with their kids.
Since then, Tiny Grooves has grown: Sunday’s event sold out all 600 tickets (priced at €18 per adult, €9 per kid, and free for those under 18 months). Some parents were hoping to just get at the door – one joking that securing tickets for this was “harder than tickets for Beyoncé.”
Yuri (who wished not to disclose his last name) was one of the lucky ones to score tickets. He used to go to many adult-only festivals, but this has slowed since having kids.
“I was drawn to this idea of having a parent meetup with a good background atmosphere and kids experience,” he says, feeding a bottle to his eight-month-old son in a Baby Bjorn. “I hope the kids catch on because it’s my fave music.”
Karlijn de Koning Strik emphasises that she has not stopped going to festivals since having a kid. But her two-and-a-half-year-old daughter always sees Strik dress up for festivals and feels left out. “Now, we can bring her too,” she jokes. “It’s nice to have a party altogether with the whole family.”
Damien and Manuela Rast appreciated the event for a different reason. Based in Zurich, they spend a few weeks each year in Amsterdam to assess whether they want to move to the city long-term with their five-and-a-half-year-old daughter.
When they saw the event advertised online, they thought it could be a great opportunity to connect with parents in Amsterdam, while still having their child by their side. It was also fitting for their daughter, who loves dancing, and immediately dragged her parents to the glitter bar.

Dutch women lose hockey World Cup final to Argentina
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The Dutch women’s hockey team have lost the World Cup final, beaten by Argentina in a shoot-out at the Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen on Saturday.
 The match finished 1-1, and Argentina then won the shoot-out 3-1 to take the title.
The result denied the Netherlands, the nine-time and reigning world champions, the chance to become the first nation to win four World Cups in a row. They played the final unbeaten in their previous 38 matches.
Yibbi Jansen had put Oranje ahead just before half-time, her eighth goal of the tournament as its top scorer. But Maria Granatto levelled from a penalty-corner move six minutes from time, and in the shoot-out only Marijn Veen scored for the hosts.
The defeat ended a run of 35 wins in those 38 games. The Dutch team’s last loss, some 18 months ago, also came against Argentina, who now win their third world title after 2002 and 2010.
“Bitter, very bitter,” said the national coach, Raoul Ehren. Jansen said she could not take in the outcome: “I just can’t believe it turned out this way.”
The Dutch men’s team had already missed out on a home final, losing their semi-final to Spain 4-3 on Friday.

items.body_text:
Dutch men out of hockey World Cup as women prepare for final
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The Dutch men’s hockey team have missed out on a home World Cup final, losing their semi-final to Spain in Amstelveen on Friday, the day before the Dutch women play for the title.
Spain, coached by the former Netherlands manager Max Caldas, won 4-3 at the Wagener Stadium.
The game turned in the final quarter, with the score at 1-1, when striker Duco Telgenkamp was sent to the sin bin for 10 minutes for pushing a Spanish defender to the ground.
With Telgenkamp off the pitch, Spain scored three times to go 4-1 ahead, José Basterra completing a hat-trick. Jip Janssen and Joep de Mol pulled two goals back late on, but Spain held the lead.
The result ended the Dutch men’s hopes of a first world title since 1998. They will play Argentina for bronze on Sunday in Wavre, Belgium, where Spain will meet defending champions Germany in the final.
The Dutch women, meanwhile, reached the final with a 1-0 win over Belgium and will face Argentina at the Wagener Stadium at 4pm on Saturday. Victory would give them a fourth successive world title, a feat no country has achieved.

items.body_text:

By Daniel Tilles
Two incidents this month have highlighted how state-led efforts to promote Poland abroad often disappoint. Yet, at the same time, the country has never had better international press. Politicians should let Poland’s successes speak for themselves, and support those already telling its story.
Poles care a lot about what the world thinks of their country. Major Polish media outlets regularly devote entire articles to what Western journalists, commentators and influencers are saying about Poland.
“A German showed what he saw on the streets of Poland,” read one typical recent headline by Onet, Poland’s biggest news website, which devoted an entire report to one video by a German-speaking TikToker with around 7,000 followers. One rarely sees such reports in more self-confident Western countries.
Given Poland’s history, such sensitivity regarding the country’s status is not surprising.
Poland was, up until the 18th century, a major European country. But, for most of the last 250 years, it has been under foreign subjugation. Only since 1989 has it been able to develop independently, and Poles are understandably keen for the world to take note of their return to the top table.
Poland has emerged as Europe’s undisputed growth champion over the past 35 years.
In the first part of a new series of articles and podcasts, @AlicjaPtak4 explores the reasons behind Poland's rapid economic development, and the dangers that may lie ahead https://t.co/bW3bnV7Ozn
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 7, 2025
Polish politicians are also inevitably eager to capitalise on such sentiment by showing voters that they are making an effort to promote Poland abroad. The problem is that such efforts are often poorly conceived and executed – as two examples this month have shown.
In mid-August, the sport and tourism ministry launched a new advertising campaign intended to attract visitors from western Europe and the United States.
However, the first advert – featuring Polish football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, and actor Nikodem Rozbicki playing Fryderyk Chopin – was widely panned in Poland. Res Futura, an organisation that monitors social media sentiment, found that 85% of comments about the advert were negative.
The campaign’s slogan – “Poland. More than you expected” – is negative and lacking confidence. The Polish Tourism Organisation says it is based on research showing that visitors to Poland are often positively surprised by how nice it is. Yet, while that is undoubtedly true, it does not mean it is a good idea to try to attract potential tourists by focusing on their low expectations.
Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to attract tourists from Europe and the US.
The first video, under the slogan "Poland. More than you expected", features footballer Robert Lewandowski, Hollywood star Jesse Eisenberg and supermodel Anja Rubik https://t.co/3jtqyUWQyy
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 19, 2026
The video also has no narrative, with the creators seeming to think that showing famous faces will be enough. Rubik does not speak a single word, while Eisenberg says only “Poland” and Lewandowski “More than you expected”.
The film itself does nothing to show that Poland is more than anyone expects. In fact, its depressingly colourless palette and focus on Warsaw’s Stalinist Palace of Science and Culture actually reinforce (false) stereotypes of Poland as grey, dull and post-communist. The country has so many interesting and colourful places that could have been showcased instead.
The advert is also a wasted opportunity to tell a story about the film’s stars, especially Eis

items.title: Polish government sets out draft 2027 budget with deficit remaining at 7.1% of GDP
items.summary: Defence, healthcare and the energy transition are among the spending priorities.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Poland’s government has approved a draft budget for 2027 that keeps defence, healthcare and the energy transition among its spending priorities, while projecting another year of heavy borrowing.
The deficit is forecast at 7.1% of GDP, unchanged from 2026 but well above the level of 3.7% the government had committed to reach by 2027 after Poland was placed under the European Union’s excessive deficit procedure in 2024.
Rada Ministrów przyjęła projekt ustawy budżetowej na 2027 rok.
Projekt odpowiedzialnie łączy finansowanie bieżących potrzeb państwa i przedsięwzięć wzmacniających jego bezpieczeństwo oraz potencjał rozwojowy.#BudżetPolaków
🔗 https://t.co/SjWyBUwi8U pic.twitter.com/X9ue6cw5ns
— Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 28, 2026
The budget – which must still be consulted with business and trade union representatives before being approved by parliament and then signed by opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki – sets total expenditure at 977.6 billion zloty (€225.4 billion), 58 billion zloty more than this year.
Revenues are projected to rise by 68.4 billion zloty to 695 billion zloty, leaving a nominal budget deficit of 282.6 billion zloty, the highest on record and 10 billion zloty more than this year.
Defence spending will remain high, at 198.1 billion zloty, equivalent to 4.5% of GDP, one of the highest levels in NATO. The healthcare budget will reach 274.1 billion zloty, up 26.3 billion zloty from 2026. Spending on energy security and transformation will rise 8.3% year-on-year to reach 19.7 billion zloty.
The government expects GDP growth to remain strong, at 3% in 2027, while average inflation is forecast at 2.8%, within the central bank’s target of 2.5%, plus or minus one percentage point.
Average wages are expected to rise by 5.9% next year in nominal terms, slightly slower than the 6.4% forecast for this year. The government expects that unemployment, measured according to the national methodology, will stand at 6% at the end of 2027, broadly unchanged from its current level.
Poland’s gross borrowing needs are projected at 565 billion zloty in 2027, below the 688 billion zloty budgeted for this year. Debt-servicing costs, however, are expected to rise to 107 billion zloty, up 17 billion zloty from this year.
Finance minister Andrzej Domański said that the rise in debt-servicing costs is driven by an increase in the overall volume of debt and the need to refinance bonds issued in 2020 and 2021 at very low interest rates.
Poland's debt has been growing at the second-fastest rate in the EU this year, and is set to continue rising.
What is behind this trend – and should we be worried – asks Alicja Ptak in the latest of her series of articles and podcasts on Poland’s economy https://t.co/1pvnb2ZxoY
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 30, 2025
The projected deficit leaves Poland under continued pressure to bring its public finances into line with EU fiscal rules.
In 2024, the country was placed under the EU’s excessive deficit procedure after its deficit exceeded the bloc’s limit of 3%. Warsaw pledged at the time to bring the deficit below 3% by 2028.
However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record.
“The 2027 budget represents a continuation of expansionary fiscal policy, and Poland is making no progress in correcting its excessive deficit and is taking no action to bring it below 3% of GDP,” wrote analysts at ING Bank Śląski today. “The result is a further increase in public debt.”

items.title: Polish “vampire” burial sheds light on 17th-century efforts to keep the dead in their graves
items.summary: The remains of a teenage girl were found with a padlock fastened to her toe and a sickle placed across her neck.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Researchers investigating an unusual 17th-century burial in northern Poland, in which the remains of a teenage girl were found with a padlock fastened to her toe and a sickle placed across her neck, believe the measures may have been intended to stop her returning from the dead.
The burial, discovered in 2022 at an unmarked cemetery in the village of Pień, is an example of what archaeologists describe as “anti-vampiric” or “anti-demonic” burial, in which precautions were taken to protect the living from a deceased person believed to pose a danger.
In a newly published academic paper, a team of researchers led by Dariusz Poliński, an archaeologist at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, say that the girl, whom they have named “Zosia”, may have been blamed by her contemporaries for misfortunes such as disease and famine.
The unusual combination of objects that Zosia was buried with – a triangular padlock attached to her left big toe and an iron sickle laid across her throat, with the blade facing towards her neck – immediately attracted archaeologists’ attention when they were discovered.
Poliński and his colleagues have used radiocarbon dating, DNA sequencing, isotope analysis and X-ray and microscopic imaging to investigate the burial. Their findings have now been published in the Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports.
The researchers have established that Zosia, who was aged between 17 and 19, died around the mid-17th century, most likely between 1620 and 1674. Her grave appears to have been secured in two stages, with analysis of soil layers showing that it was reopened after the initial burial and the sickle added later.
“It was unusual that there were two precautions, two methods of showing that this skeleton should be kept in the grave – so the fear of the body coming back to life was greater,” Poliński told CNN.
The researchers say the padlock had several possible meanings in funerary symbolism. It could mark the end of earthly life and the transition to the world of the dead, prevent contact between the living and the dead, break a run of bad luck, or protect the community from the deceased returning.
“In some interpretations, it was also believed to help halt the spread of epidemics,” Poliński told the Polish Press Agency (PAP).
The sickle had a more direct purpose: if the deceased tried to rise from the grave, it was positioned to sever the head or slit the throat, preventing her from returning to the world of the living.
However, the latest findings suggest there may have been a third protective element.
Researchers found “a distinct green discolouration” in the oral cavity, suggesting that an object containing a high proportion of copper had been placed in the girl’s mouth. Given the extent of the discolouration, they have largely ruled out the possibility that it was simply a coin.
“The protective measures taken at the time of the original burial and subsequently after the grave was opened clearly demonstrate the immense fear of Zosia,” said Poliński, quoted by news website Wirtualna Polska.
The grave of a "vampire child" – who was turned face down and secured with a padlock to ensure he could not rise from the grave – has been discovered in Poland
Researchers believe the site was a cemetery for those excluded or feared by the local community https://t.co/Ez2QgvMnuX
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2023

items.title: Opposition parties call for early elections
items.summary: Riigikogu opposition parties Isamaa, Center and EKRE are calling for new elections to remove the Reform Party and Eesti 200 minority government from power.
items.body_text:
Opposition parties call for early elections
Riigikogu opposition parties Isamaa, Center and EKRE are calling for new elections to remove the Reform Party and Eesti 200 minority government from power.
The governing coalition lost its parliamentary majority three weeks ago when Eesti 200's Kalev Stoicescu and Reform's Meelis Kiili left their respective parties. The next Riigikogu elections will take place in March 2027.
On Sunday, the most popular opposition party, Isamaa, published a statement calling for a vote of no confidence in the government
"Isamaa proposes that all Riigikogu parties and independent MPs begin consultations to hold new, early Riigikogu elections without delay, as provided for in the Constitution," the statement said. "To initiate this, it would be appropriate, in accordance with the Constitution, to express no confidence in Kristen Michal's government."
Isamaa claimed Estonia will only be able to move forward if the government resigns.
"New elections are the beginning of restoring trust and an opportunity for honest feedback from citizens and for defining expectations for the future," it wrote.
On Saturday, the Center Party also called for early elections. It said the coalition's inability to govern the country poses a security risk.
Party Chairman Mihhail Kõlvart said the National Audit Office's latest report about the problems in the defense sector is evidence of the government's systemic failure.
"The current government has used defense spending to justify both unexpected tax increases and allowing the state budget to fall deeply into deficit, as well as people's worsening ability to cope," Kõlvart said.
"Now shortcomings have come to light that no country can afford in the current security situation. The large-scale disorder in national defense endangers the security of the entire country. The resignation of a few officials or ministers is no longer enough. The entire government must resign, and early elections must be called," he continued.
Kõlvart also said the latest economic forecasts show the "government has no substantive plan for reviving the economy and bringing the national debt under control" and that problems also exist in the education, energy and social sectors.
"The current government does not solve crises but postpones them and communicates a prettier version of reality. This is not leadership," he said.
Kõlvart said solutions cannot wait until the Riigikogu elections in March because Estonia is losing valuable time and solving the problems will become even more difficult.
This week, EKRE's board decided to send an appeal to all members of parliament proposing that Michal's minority government be removed as soon as possible.
The appeal sent by party Chairman Martin Helme states that Michal's government has long since lost the support of the majority of society and has now also lost the support of the majority in the Riigikogu.
"Support for the coalition parties has for some time been languishing at around a dozen percent, which is unprecedented in Estonia's history and abnormal in a democratic system," he wrote.
Helme proposes two alternatives to the Reform Party and Eesti 200 governing coalition.
"First, we form a so-called interim government until the elections, involving all political forces except the Reform Party and Eesti 200 and including, as extensively as possible, experts who do not participate in day-to-day politics. Such a government cannot and must not make important decisions or decisions with long-term consequences, but has one simple task: to take the country to elections without abusing the instruments of executive power in the knowledge that there is nothing left to lose," Helme said.
The second option would be early elections.
