items.title: Some migrants ready to pack bags fearing far-right win in east German state
items.summary: As a far-right regional election victory looms in an ex-communist eastern German state, many migrants are readying to pack their bags, fearful of the AfD party's threatened "deportation and remigration offensive".
items.body_text:
A week from now, the anti-immigration, Islamophobic and Russia-friendly Alternative for Germany party is expected to score a historic win in the small state of Saxony-Anhalt, with hopes of taking its first-ever governing majority.
It is an ominous scenario for Syria-born cardiologist Ayman Alyoussef, head physician in a clinic in the picturesque town of Quedlinburg, who voiced a common sentiment: "I fear that hatred of foreigners will spread."
Alyoussef, who arrived in the country in 2014 and is now a German citizen, said he has been welcomed by patients and colleagues but sometimes faces hostility on the streets, as do his wife and daughter who wear Muslim headscarves.
"There are patients who arrive at 3:00 am with a heart attack. I am able to get them through an acute crisis," Alyoussef told AFP. "Afterwards, they are very grateful when they realise that a foreigner helped them.
"But out on the street, they don't know that I am a cardiologist. They think I am just a foreigner receiving assistance from the city. That is why they say they don't want someone like me here. That is the problem."
Many foreign-born residents share such experiences and fears.
Last week, some 150 migrant-run restaurants, kiosks and barber shops in the state capital Magdeburg temporarily closed their doors to protest what they warned is an increasingly xenophobic climate.
Support group the Refugee Council said many migrants had already reported "experiences of racism and social exclusion" and that talk of mass deportations had sparked growing "fear and uncertainty".
'Up in flames'
It is a feeling shared by Afghan migrant Rezwaan Talash, 24, who arrived in Germany six years ago and works in a Magdeburg computer repair shop.
"Whether I'll still have my life the way it is now, that's a question and a fear that's always on my mind," he told AFP.
Talash, who also volunteers in a migrant support group, said that "from our association, quite a few people from Saxony-Anhalt have recently moved away because it could be unsafe here for us after the elections.
"We don't want everything we've worked to achieve here so far -- starting a calm, good life here -- to suddenly go up in flames."
AfD top candidate Ulrich Siegmund, who wants to become state premier, has vowed to deport all foreigners without legal status "from minute one" in office.
Speaking to AFP on Saturday at a campaign event, Siegmund insisted that his party wants to deport “people who are here illegally, who are required to leave the country”, while “regular immigration based on strict criteria … would not be a problem”.
Whatever happens after Sunday’s election, the heated campaign rhetoric has already deepened “societal divisions”, said Mamad Mohamad, a candidate for the left-leaning Greens party who was recently handing out flyers outside an Islamic cultural centre in the city of Halle.
"There are people who want to talk to us and have questions, but there are also people who walk by and hurl insults or shout at us," he told AFP.
Mohamad, a Yazidi Kurd who arrived in Germany from Syria in 1996 as a 16-year-old, said he and his fellow campaigners "always have to keep an eye on where we are, who we are talking to, and ensure we are never alone.
"We always go out in groups of three or four when campaigning in the city."
Demographic crisis
Economists warn that the AfD's anti-migrant campaign, aside from the human toll, would spell an economic own-goal for the small state, which has already lost nearly a quarter of its population since Germany's reunification in 1990.
"Today, for every two people leaving the workforce, only one enters it -- a gap that cannot be filled by the residents of Saxony-Anhalt and neighbouring regions alone," says conservative CDU candidate Sven Schulze.
The AfD has proposed to counter the demographic crisis with "baby bonuses" for German parents and by seeking to lure back Germans living abroad, but employers say they are already struggling to find qualified staff.

items.title: 'Welcome culture to farewell culture': The AfD's plans for Saxony-Anhalt
items.summary: In one week, Germans in Saxony Anhalt will vote in a state election that could see the far-right AfD party take power. What would the party's proposed policies mean for the foreign residents who live there?
items.body_text:
This article was originally published 100 days ahead of the election in May. It has been updated as of the end of August, with one week to go to the election in Saxony-Anhalt.
Until now the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has effectively played the role of a very loud but politically powerless opposition party in national (and even state-level) politics.
But now it appears the anti-immigration and Eurosceptic party appears to have a real chance at taking power in a German state.
That state is Saxony-Anhalt, where polls over recent weeks and months have consistently shown the party having just over 40 percent of voters. Depending on how the other parties fair, the AfD are seen at being within reach of winning an absolute majority -- or enough of a lead to take power as a single-party government.
Approximately 2.14 million people live in the state, of whom 11.2 percent have an immigration background.
With a week to go until state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, on September 6th, it’s worth looking at what Germany’s leading party is campaigning on, and how these plans would affect foreign residents living there.
The AfD adopted its election manifesto for Saxony-Anhalt in April – a more than 150 page document that proposes a "radical blueprint" for the state, including a "180-degree turn" in migration policy. This would include widespread deportations of Ukrainians and the segregation of refugee school children to give just a couple examples.
Many of these policies would not be possible to implement at the state level as they are under the jurisdiction of the federal government in Berlin.
But the manifesto shows what kind of policies the AfD will pursue if they take a position of power.
‘Deportation offensive’
The AfD continues to push "remigration" – a term linked to neo-Nazi ideologies that here implies the mass removal of people with ‘non-German’ origins.
To that end, the party plans a massive “deportation offensive” with €100 million in funding. This would include increasing the number of deportation detention facilities tenfold in the state, from 30 to at least 300, and organising deportation flights at the state-level from the Halle/Leipzig airport.
Carrying out mass deportations would require a significant amount of people and effort by various authorities. This year, the AfD’s Bavarian chapter suggested creating an “Asylum Search and Deportation Group” that it said would be “similar to ICE in the US”.
READ ALSO: Anti-immigration AfD party wants to bring ICE to Germany
The manifesto for Saxony Anhalt does not mention this authority specifically, but it does call for the creation of a deportation task force and a “Staff Office for Remigration”. It envisions these new authorities coordinating with existing authorities like the Center for the Support of Return (Zentrum zur Unterstützung der Rückkehr - ZUR) and municipal immigration offices.
Target on Ukrainians
Ukrainians in particular would be specifically targeted by the AfD’s deportation efforts.
The manifesto outlines plans to stop recognising Ukrainian asylum seekers as war refugees. It suggests they can instead find safety in western Ukraine
It also calls for cutting off their access to social and welfare benefits to incentivise their return.
Critics of the AfD have long charged that the party is a pro-Putin or pro-Russia party because of its political alignment with Moscow’s geopolitical interests.
The AfD’s manifesto says Germany's “current anti-Russian policies” are not in the country’s interest. It calls for lifting sanctions on Russia as well as “preserving Russian classes” in German schools and reviving German-Russian student exchanges.
Integration made harder
Not just asylum seekers but foreign skilled workers in Saxony-Anhalt can expect life to be made more challenging under an AfD-led government.
The manifesto explicitly rejects the recruitment of foreign skilled workers, and suggests that Germany’s labour shortage can instead be addressed with AI, digitalis

items.title: Indonesian military leads ecosystem restoration after Kalimantan fires
items.summary: Indonesia’s VI/Mulawarman Regional Military Command and other agencies have begun restoring ecosystems and ...
items.body_text:
“This month, we are restoring vegetation by planting trees in burned and degraded areas, including along riverbanks,” VI/Mulawarman Regional Military Commander Major General Krido Pramono said.
Restoring vegetation was essential to restoring the ecological functions of areas that have lost tree cover because of forest and land fires, he said here on Saturday.
Tree planting will be carried out gradually with the involvement of the military, police, Regional Agency for Disaster Countermeasures, search and rescue agency, religious leaders and communities.
Such cooperation is needed not only during disasters but also to protect the environment and reduce the risk of fires returning during the dry season.
Besides reforestation, the government and relevant agencies are optimizing existing water infrastructure to improve water availability.
Reservoirs that had previously been built are being reactivated to provide water amid low rainfall.
“Drilled wells that we have built also provide clean water and can support forest and land fire prevention and firefighting,” Krido said.
He said water availability was increasingly critical amid dry conditions and rising temperatures.
Water is needed not only for communities but also to support firefighting operations if hotspots re-emerge.
Authorities are also taking a spiritual approach, holding joint prayers and salat istisqa, or prayers for rain, simultaneously in parts of East and North Kalimantan.
“We recognize our limitations and weaknesses. Only Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala can provide help, including rain, and protect us from disasters,” he said.
Krido stressed that protecting the environment is not solely the responsibility of the government and security forces, adding that communities must also plant trees, protect water sources, and avoid burning land.
The measures are expected to preserve environmental functions while reducing disaster risks whose impacts are felt directly by communities.

items.title: Indonesian military deploys 583 personnel to prevent wildfires
items.summary: A total of 583 wildfire prevention educators from the Indonesian military, deployed to prevent forest and land fires, ...
items.body_text:
The team, comprising wildfire prevention educators and Alpha wildfire teams, arrived aboard an Indonesian Air Force C-130H Hercules aircraft.
The deployed 583 wildfire prevention educators comprise 50 senior officers and 533 mid-ranking officers from the Army, Navy, Air Force and military headquarters.
"We want prevention to start early. The personnel will educate communities, raise awareness, and encourage residents to work together to protect the environment," VI/Mulawarman Military Command Chief of Staff Brigadier General Andy Setyawan said here on Saturday.
The team was also welcomed by Dhomber Air Base Commander Colonel I Gusti Ngurah Sorga Laksana, Balikpapan Military District Commander Colonel Denny Salurerung and Balikpapan Naval Base Commander Colonel Rudhiro Pratomo.
All personnel immediately departed Dhomber Air Base for their respective deployment locations.
Related news: Puan seeks Foreign Ministry talks over Kalimantan wildfire haze
The wildfire prevention education team was assigned to the Balikpapan Hajj Dormitory, while the Alpha team headed to the Dodikjur VI/Mulawarman Barracks to prepare for field operations.
Andy said tackling wildfires requires more than firefighting once fires have started. Prevention, education, and community involvement are crucial during the dry season.
"Prevention must be a joint effort. Public education, awareness, and concern are the foundations for reducing wildfires from an early stage," he said.
Besides East Kalimantan, military wildfire prevention personnel are being deployed gradually to other vulnerable provinces, including West Kalimantan, South Sumatra, Lampung, Riau, and North Kalimantan.
The cross-regional deployment is part of the military’s commitment in supporting government efforts to reduce wildfire risks nationwide.
The deployment of educators and specialised teams is expected to strengthen coordination among the military, local governments, relevant agencies and communities to suppress hotspots more effectively.

items.title: Jelang Pemilihan Ketum PBNU, Gus Yahya Ingatkan Muktamirin soal Kepentingan NU
items.summary: Jelang pemilihan Ketua Umum PBNU, Gus Yahya mengingatkan muktamirin agar mengutamakan masa depan dan kemaslahatan NU
items.body_text:
Muktamar NU
Jelang Pemilihan Ketum PBNU, Gus Yahya Ingatkan Muktamirin soal Kepentingan NU
Jelang pemilihan Ketua Umum PBNU, Gus Yahya mengingatkan muktamirin agar mengutamakan masa depan dan kemaslahatan NU
Ringkasan Berita:
- Menjelang pemilihan Ketua Umum PBNU dalam Muktamar ke-35 NU, Gus Yahya meminta muktamirin menempatkan masa depan dan kemaslahatan NU di atas kepentingan pribadi maupun kelompok
- Pemilihan kali ini menggunakan mekanisme baru dengan penjaringan maksimal lima nama yang kemudian dipertimbangkan AHWA
- Hasil muktamar akan menentukan arah NU memasuki abad kedua
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JOMBANG - Pemilihan Ketua Umum Pengurus Besar Nahdlatul Ulama (PBNU) dalam Muktamar ke-35 NU memasuki tahap penentuan, Minggu (30/8/2026).
Di tengah proses memilih pemimpin organisasi untuk periode berikutnya, Ketua Umum PBNU KH Yahya Cholil Staquf atau Gus Yahya menyampaikan pesan kepada para peserta muktamar agar tidak menjadikan kontestasi sebagai ruang untuk memperjuangkan kepentingan pribadi maupun kelompok.
Gus Yahya meminta para muktamirin menempatkan masa depan dan kemaslahatan Nahdlatul Ulama sebagai pertimbangan utama dalam menentukan kepemimpinan organisasi.
"Saya hanya ingin menitipkan satu pesan kepada Muktamirin. Mari kita pikirkan sungguh-sungguh, kita hayati sungguh-sungguh komitmen untuk memikirkan nasib Nahdlatul Ulama, masa depan Nahdlatul Ulama, kemaslahatan Nahdlatul Ulama di masa depan, lepas dari kepentingan apa pun selain itu," kata Gus Yahya melalui pernyataan video yang disampaikan kepada wartawan menjelang pemilihan ketua umum.
Pesan tersebut disampaikan ketika Gus Yahya sendiri kembali berada dalam bursa calon ketua umum.
Ia merupakan petahana yang memimpin PBNU sejak Muktamar ke-34 di Lampung.
Baca juga: Kiai Sepuh Nahdlatul Ulama Sampaikan Tausiah Moral Jelang Muktamar ke-35
Karena itu, pernyataan tersebut tidak hanya berkaitan dengan siapa yang akan terpilih, tetapi juga menyentuh bagaimana proses pergantian atau keberlanjutan kepemimpinan NU dijalankan.
Bagi Gus Yahya, kepentingan organisasi seharusnya ditempatkan di atas kepentingan kandidat maupun kelompok yang mendukungnya.
Pemilihan dengan Mekanisme Baru
Pemilihan Ketua Umum PBNU kali ini memiliki mekanisme berbeda dibandingkan proses pemilihan sebelumnya.
Muktamar melakukan penjaringan awal dengan meminta peserta mengusulkan maksimal lima nama calon ketua umum.
Nama-nama yang memperoleh suara terbanyak kemudian diserahkan kepada Ahlul Halli wal Aqdi (AHWA) setelah para calon menyatakan kesediaannya, baik secara lisan maupun tertulis.
AHWA merupakan forum yang terdiri atas sembilan kiai yang dipilih untuk menjalankan fungsi musyawarah dalam menentukan kepemimpinan PBNU.
Dengan mekanisme tersebut, suara peserta muktamar menjadi tahap penjaringan, sementara keputusan akhir mengenai Ketua Umum PBNU berada di tangan AHWA.
Proses ini membuat pemilihan tidak semata-mata menjadi pertarungan perolehan suara antarkandidat.

items.title: Panitia Tegaskan Tak Bisa Intervensi Aturan Muktamar NU, Gus Ipul: Semua Tergantung Muktamirin
items.summary: Saifullah Yusuf (Gus Ipul), menegaskan bahwa keputusan akhir atas substansi aturan sepenuhnya berada di tangan para muktamirin.
items.body_text:
Muktamar NU
Panitia Tegaskan Tak Bisa Intervensi Aturan Muktamar NU, Gus Ipul: Semua Tergantung Muktamirin
Saifullah Yusuf (Gus Ipul), menegaskan bahwa keputusan akhir atas substansi aturan sepenuhnya berada di tangan para muktamirin.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JOMBANG — Panitia Penyelenggara Muktamar ke-35 Nahdlatul Ulama (NU) menegaskan posisinya sekadar memfasilitasi jalannya forum, menyusul dinamika unjuk rasa Nahdliyin muda yang sempat melumpuhkan Sidang Pleno IV di Gedung Serba Guna (GSG) Pondok Pesantren Bahrul Ulum Tambakberas, Jombang, Minggu (30/8/2026) sore.
Massa sebelumnya memadati lokasi sekitar pukul 13.30 WIB dan terlibat aksi saling dorong dengan petugas Banser serta panitia.
Mereka memprotes aturan Peraturan Perkumpulan (Perkum) terkait masa iddah (masa tunggu) politik selama satu tahun bagi eks pejabat politik yang dinilai mengganjal peluang sejumlah kader dalam bursa pencalonan Ketua Umum PBNU.
Ketua Organizing Committee (OC) Muktamar ke-35 NU, Saifullah Yusuf (Gus Ipul), menegaskan bahwa keputusan akhir atas substansi aturan sepenuhnya berada di tangan para muktamirin sebagai pemegang kekuasaan tertinggi organisasi.
"Dan nanti itu muktamirin. Paling kita hanya memfasilitasi bagaimana semua lancar. Untuk pembahasan materinya di dalam," kata Gus Ipul saat dikonfirmasi di sela acara.
Dinamika Persidangan dan Posisi Hukum Forum
Gus Ipul menekankan bahwa arena Muktamar berwenang mengubah atau mempertahankan regulasi yang sedang dipersoalkan, termasuk poin-poin tata tertib pemilihan Rais Aam dan Ketua Umum PBNU.
"Itu tergantung, tergantung nanti. Tergantung muktamirin. Muktamar, posisinya lebih tinggi," ujarnya.
Ia juga menambahkan bahwa panitia tidak memiliki kapasitas untuk mengintervensi perubahan aturan di luar mekanisme resmi persidangan.
"Jadi bisa mengambil keputusan apa. Belum tahu saya kalau merubahnya. Semua tergantung muktamirin," jelasnya.
Lebih lanjut, Sekjen PBNU ini mengingatkan pentingnya menempuh jalur musyawarah di dalam forum resmi karena setiap hasil yang disepakati akan mengikat seluruh elemen organisasi.
"Keputusan-keputusan di sini adalah keputusan yang mengikat. Dan kalau nanti istilahnya mau dirubah, ya tentu atas persetujuan beserta pembahasan. Kita tunggu aja ya," beber Gus Ipul.
Mengenai tensi di lapangan yang sempat memanas hingga menunda persidangan hampir dua jam, Gus Ipul memastikan situasi di area Tambakberas telah terkendali.
"Dan sekarang suasananya udah reda agar sidang berjalan dengan baik. Itulah NU ya," tuturnya.
Situasi Terkini di Arena Muktamar
Kondisi di sekitar GSG Pesantren Bahrul Ulum kini kembali kondusif di bawah pengawalan ketat gabungan Banser, panitia lokal, serta aparat TNI-Polri:
- Pukul 15.45 WIB: Ketua Umum PBNU KH Yahya Cholil Staquf (Gus Yahya) tiba di lokasi untuk memantau langsung dinamika muktamar.
- Pukul 16.00 WIB: Enam logistik kotak suara untuk proses pemilihan Ahlul Halli wal Aqdi (AHWA) mendarat di area sidang.
- Pukul 16.30 WIB: Para muktamirin kembali memasuki ruangan secara bertahap setelah melalui pemeriksaan ketat untuk melanjutkan agenda penghitungan tabulasi usulan anggota AHWA secara tertutup.
Untuk diketahui suasana Muktamar ke-35 Nahdlatul Ulama (NU) memanas setelah pimpinan sidang pleno mengesahkan klausul mengenai masa iddah politik.

items.title: Besok, Ibrahim Arief Jalani Sidang Putusan Banding Kasus Korupsi Chromebook
items.summary: PT DKI Jakarta akan membacakan putusan banding Ibrahim Arief dalam kasus Chromebook. Ibam sebelumnya divonis 4 tahun penjara dan denda Rp500 juta
items.body_text:
Dugaan Korupsi di Kemendikbud
Besok, Ibrahim Arief Jalani Sidang Putusan Banding Kasus Korupsi Chromebook
PT DKI Jakarta akan membacakan putusan banding Ibrahim Arief dalam kasus Chromebook. Ibam sebelumnya divonis 4 tahun penjara dan denda Rp500 juta
Ringkasan Berita:
- Pengadilan Tinggi DKI Jakarta akan membacakan putusan banding Ibrahim Arief alias Ibam dalam perkara dugaan korupsi pengadaan laptop Chromebook pada Senin (31/8/2026)
- Sebelumnya, Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta Pusat menjatuhkan hukuman 4 tahun penjara dan denda Rp500 juta
- Ibam berharap hakim mempertimbangkan posisinya sebagai konsultan independen, bukan pengambil keputusan di kementerian
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA - Pengadilan Tinggi DKI Jakarta akan menggelar sidang lanjutan perkara banding terdakwa Ibrahim Arief alias Ibam dalam kasus dugaan korupsi pengadaan laptop Chromebook, Senin (31/8/2026).
Sidang tersebut beragendakan pembacaan putusan oleh majelis hakim tingkat banding.
"Sidang putusan Insya Allah besok jam 10 pagi," ucap pejabat Humas PT DKI Jakarta, Catur Irianto dihubungi Minggu (30/8/2026).
Sebelumnya Terdakwa Ibrahim Arief alias Ibam telah menegaskan bahwa dirinya menghormati proses hukum yang sedang dijalaninya.
Meski begitu, Ibam berharap proses banding dapat melihat secara utuh posisi, kewenangan, dan tindakan yang dilakukannya sebagai konsultan independen.
"Saya menghormati proses hukum yang sedang berjalan dan percaya bahwa majelis hakim akan melihat perkara ini secara objektif dan menyeluruh. Sejak awal, posisi saya adalah sebagai konsultan yang memberikan keahlian dan masukan profesional, bukan sebagai pengambil keputusan di lingkungan kementerian," ujar Ibam.
Ibam berharap proses banding dapat memberikan penilaian yang utuh terhadap peran dan tindakan masing-masing pihak dalam perkara pengadaan Chromebook tersebut.
Baca juga: Banding Vonis Kasus Chromebook, Ibrahim Arief Berharap Dibebaskan dari Jerat Hukum
"Bagi saya, ini bukan hanya tentang nama baik, tetapi juga tentang kepastian bahwa masukan profesional tidak dimaknai sebagai kewenangan mengambil keputusan," jelasnya.
Sementara itu, kuasa hukum Ibam, Boy Bondjol, menilai persoalan yang dihadapi kliennya tidak hanya menyangkut kepentingan pribadi, tetapi juga menyentuh kepastian hukum bagi para profesional yang memberikan keahlian kepada pemerintah.
Menurutnya, dalam praktik pemerintahan, masukan dari konsultan, ahli hukum, auditor, akademisi, hingga tenaga profesional dibutuhkan untuk membantu pengambilan keputusan. Namun, fungsi memberikan masukan tetap berbeda dengan kewenangan mengambil keputusan.
"Jika pemberian masukan atau keterlibatan dalam rapat kemudian dijadikan dasar untuk membebankan pertanggungjawaban pidana tanpa terlebih dahulu melihat kewenangan, tindakan, dan peran nyata seorang konsultan, maka batas tanggung jawab profesional menjadi penting untuk diuji," jelas Boy.
Boy menegaskan seorang konsultan tidak dapat disamakan dengan pejabat yang memiliki kewenangan formal hanya karena aktif memberikan masukan atau berinteraksi dengan pejabat dan tim teknis pemerintah.
Untuk diketahui, Pengadilan Tindak Pidana Korupsi (Tipikor) Jakarta Pusat sebelumnya telah menjatuhkan putusan 4 tahun penjara terhadap Ibrahim Arief alias Ibam.
Selain pidana penjara, majelis hakim yang diketuai Purwanto S. Abdullah juga menghukum Ibam membayar denda Rp500 juta subsider 120 hari kurungan.

items.body_text:
Midnight blaze hits Mabolo warehouse; damage reaches P1.4M
CEBU CITY, Philippines — A fire broke out shortly after midnight on Wednesday, gutting a hardware warehouse along St. Jude Street in Barangay Mabolo, Cebu City.
Fire authorities estimated the damage caused by the fire at P1.4 million.
Ronieglen Lopez, a 20-year-old mechanic at the warehouse, said he noticed smoke coming from inside the building at around 11 p.m. on Tuesday, August 25.

Lopez lives in a company-provided workers’ housing facility adjacent to the warehouse.
“Pag-abli nako sa bintana, didto nako nakita nga nagbaga na. Mao to nibaba ko kay nagkuha og tubig kay abi namo nga matabang ra namo pero wala na jud. Mao to namukaw nalang ko sa akong mga kauban,” he said.

(When I opened the window, I saw that the fire was already blazing. So I went downstairs to get some water because we thought we could still put it out, but we really couldn’t anymore. So I just woke up my companions.)
The fire was reported to authorities shortly after midnight.
The first alarm was raised at 1:06 a.m. as flames rapidly spread through materials stored inside the facility. The fire was placed under control at 1:14 a.m. and declared out at 1:24 a.m.
As of this posting, fire investigators are continuing to determine the cause of the fire.
The 13 warehouse employees displaced by the fire were also transferred to another area, where they will stay temporarily.

items.title: Pilandok maintains strength, enhances southwest monsoon
items.summary: The enhanced southwest monsoon or habagat is bringing monsoon rain to Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, and Pampanga
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- Tropical Depression Pilandok is enhancing the southwest monsoon, bringing heavy rainfall to various areas in the Philippines.
- PAGASA forecasts Pilandok to move west northwestward and weaken into a remnant low by September 1, with a low likelihood of making landfall.
- The enhanced southwest monsoon is expected to cause strong gusts and rough seas in many areas, with warnings for small vessels to avoid venturing out to sea.
MANILA, Philippines – Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength on Sunday afternoon, August 30, and is enhancing the southwest monsoon or habagat.
In its 5 pm bulletin on Sunday, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said Pilandok was located 1,180 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon. It is moving northwestward slowly, with maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour and gustiness of up to 55 km/h.
PAGASA said Pilandok is seen to move west northwestward on Monday, August 31, before turning generally northwestward.
It is less likely to make landfall and is expected to be a short-lived tropical cyclone, remaining a tropical depression before weakening into a remnant low over the Philippine Sea south of the southern islands of Japan on Tuesday, September 1.
While it is not directly affecting the country, Pilandok is enhancing the southwest monsoon, which is bringing monsoon rain to Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, and Pampanga, and occasional rain to Metro Manila, the rest of Cordillera Administrative Region, Nueva Vizcaya, Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro.
It is also causing scattered rain and thunderstorms to the rest of Luzon, Western Visayas, and Negros Island Region, and isolated rain showers or thunderstorms to the rest of Visayas.
Below is PAGASA’s latest heavy rainfall outlook due to the southwest monsoon for the next three days:
Sunday afternoon, August 30, Monday afternoon, August 31:
- Heavy to intense rain (100-200 millimeters): Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Abra, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, and Pampanga
- Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Metro Manila, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro
Monday afternoon, August 31, to Tuesday afternoon, September 1:
- Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, and Bataan
- Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Pangasinan, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Batanes, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, and Cavite
Tuesday afternoon, September 1, to Wednesday afternoon, September 2:
- Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Abra, and Benguet
- Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Batanes, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, La Union, Pangasinan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Zambales, and Bataan
These areas should watch out for flash floods and landslides.
The enhanced southwest monsoon is also bringing strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas, especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds:
Sunday, August 30:
- most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental

Tuesday, September 1:

items.title: LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections
items.summary: Bookmark and refresh this page for the latest news, photos, videos, and analyses as Rappler closely follows the historic elections
items.body_text:
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao is holding its first parliamentary elections on September 14, 2026, after being postponed at least four times: first in May 2022, then in May 2025, October 2025, and again in March 2026.
The historic polls are seen as a pivotal moment in the decades-long peace process in a region that was mired in conflict and socioeconomic and political challenges. The upcoming elections are also a test for the Bangsamoro transition and the institutions and systems established in the last seven years.
Bookmark and refresh this page for the latest news, photos, videos, and analyses as Rappler closely follows the regional elections.
LATEST UPDATES
For Moros, the price of peace is life
Many Muslims in Mindanao who dedicated themselves to jihad are supposed to reap the rewards of the peace process. But breaches of trust between the Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front threaten the fulfillment of the peaceful lives they were promised.
Read more here.
Blood, rebellion, and uneasy peace: The Bangsamoro’s unfinished journey
History rarely moves in straight lines. In Mindanao, it lurched forward through cycles of grievance, reprisal, and uneasy compromise. What began centuries earlier as resistance to foreign rule would, by the late 20th century, erupt into a far more intimate and brutal conflict — one fought not between empire and frontier but among people from the same archipelago themselves.
Read more here.
From ‘Moro wars’ to BARMM: Centuries of resistance and struggle for self-rule
For many in Mindanao, the creation of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao represents the culmination of the centuries-old struggle for self-determination among the region’s Muslim communities. It’s a struggle that predates the Philippine Republic itself and traces its roots to the earliest encounters between local sultanates and foreign powers.
Read more here.
Comelec, election watchdogs sign MOA for 2026 BARMM parliamentary vote audit
Commission on Elections Chairman George Erwin Garcia, along with representatives from the Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting, National Citizens’ Movement for Free Elections, Philippine Statistics Authority, and Department of Education, signs a memorandum of agreement for the random manual audit of the 2026 Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary elections during a ceremony at the Comelec office in Manila on Friday, August 28.
Photos by Rappler
Comelec affirms cancellation of Moro Ako Party registration
The Comelec en banc rejected the motion for reconsideration of the Moro Ako Party, affirming the earlier cancellation of its registration as a regional parliamentary political party for the September 14 regional elections.
In a resolution promulgated on Friday, August 28, the commission upheld its August 4 decision to grant a petition against the party over alleged misrepresentation.
The ruling seals the exclusion of the Moro Ako Party from the parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
How the BARMM vote works
How will those in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) vote?
Because this is a parliamentary election, they will vote for a regional political party and one district representative. Voters don’t get to choose the BARMM chief minister. Rather, the elected parliament will pick the chief minister.
The BARMM parliament will have 80 members. Forty seats will go to party representatives (from the regional political parties), 32 seats go to parliamentary district representatives, and eight seats are reserved for sectoral representatives.

items.title: [Inside the Newsroom] Trust and public funds: why and how we obsess over the national budget
items.summary: There are reasons why 'trust' should never be something you assume when it comes to the people’s money, even if (and maybe, particularly if) they are labelled confidential or intelligence funds
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- The author reflects on the reliance on 'trust' in handling confidential and intelligence funds, emphasizing the need for skepticism and accountability in government spending.
- Historical abuses of confidential funds highlight the importance of checks and balances, as demonstrated by past scandals involving military funds.
- Rappler is committed to scrutinizing the budget process and providing transparency through training and accessible data, urging public support to combat corruption.
Ten years ago, when funds allocated to confidential and intelligence expenditures skyrocketed under the Duterte administration, I asked then Budget Secretary Benjamin Diokno for his thoughts on what safeguards should be put in place to prevent potential abuse of these funds.
Diokno’s response then: “We just have to trust him (President Rodrigo Duterte) na mabuting tao siya (that he is a good person),” he said.
I was astounded. Trust? Journalists are trained to be skeptical and suspicious, particularly when it comes to matters that involve power and money.
The word “trust” is also anathema to the checks and balances that is embedded in our system of government.
It therefore felt surreal that — 10 years later — there is that word again: trust.
People reporting to Duterte’s daughter, Vice President Sara Duterte, are saying the same thing before an impeachment court: they trusted Colonel Raymund Lachica, the VP’s chief security officer. They trusted the Vice President.
Hello! I am Gemma Mendoza, head for strategic programs at Rappler. As a journalist, I am particularly obsessed with the budget process. I have been scrutinizing budget, procurement, and audit documents for over two decades now.
There are reasons why “trust” should never be something you assume when it comes to the people’s money, even if (and maybe, particularly if) they are labelled confidential or intelligence funds.
Former heads of the Commission on Audit (COA) have already said that confidential and intelligence funds are difficult to audit.
Prior to that specific interview with Diokno, I co-wrote the book The Enemy Within with Aries Rufo and Glenda Gloria. That book dived deep into how the military top brass abused confidential and intelligence funds allocated to the armed forces and, among other things, diverted these funds to their pabaon retirement system.
A former military general took his own life following congressional investigations into this scandal.
While there are legitimate reasons why certain funds cannot go through the usual processes, the Constitution is explicit about subjecting all kinds of funds to audit.
It says: “No law shall be passed exempting any entity of the Government or its subsidiary in any guise whatever, or any investment of public funds, from the jurisdiction of the Commission on Audit.”
This was precisely why in 2015 the budget department and COA worked with the local government and defense departments to come up with Joint Circular No. 2015-01.
Within each government office, each vote and signature in the budget request, procurement, and liquidation process is supposed to represent checks to misuse. Each signatory is supposed to be responsible. They are not supposed to “trust” each other.
The fact that the confidential funds of Sara Duterte are now at the center of an impeachment trial is a demonstration of how various steps in this process of checks and balances failed the Filipino people. Rappler has reported on this every step of the way.
This is why we require every journalist at Rappler to be familiar with the national budget and the budget process. We remind our reporters that the scrutiny of how public funds are allocated and spent needs to happen at each phase of the process: planning and formulation, approval, implementation, and audit.
Beyond the numbers themselves, everything requires sharp eyes: the logic of the budget, the expected outcomes, the process of fund release up to the point the project funded by said item is

items.summary: More than 8.1 million people have been affected by Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng and the enhanced habagat.
items.body_text:
32 dead, 8.1 million affected by recent storms, habagat
MANILA, Philippines — More than 8.1 million people have been affected by Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng and the enhanced southwest monsoon, or habagat, across 10 regions, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council said Sunday.
In its Aug. 30 situation report, the NDRRMC said around 2.3 million families, or 8.1 million individuals, were affected across the Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Bicol Region, Western Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, the Cordillera Administrative Region and Metro Manila.
Some 43,500 people from 13,500 families were staying in 523 evacuation centers.
The NDRRMC also reported 32 deaths, three missing persons and 19 injuries.
The following are reported deaths, according to the NDRRMC:
- Benguet (15): Baguio City reported 10 landslide-related deaths, Atok recorded 3, and La Trinidad reported 2.
- Batangas (4): Drowning deaths occurred in Batangas City and Mabini, alongside a landslide fatality in Santa Teresita and an electrocution in Lipa.
- Rizal (4): Two died from a rockslide in Rodriguez, one from a fallen tree in Antipolo, and one from drowning in Binangonan.
- Occidental Mindoro (2): Two fatalities were reported in Rizal due to electrocution and drowning.
- Caloocan (2): Two individuals drowned.
- Quezon (1): Drowning deaths were reported in Candelaria and Sariaya.
- La Union, Oriental Mindoro, and Negros Occidental: One drowning/storm fatality each in Luna, Puerto Galera, and Cadiz, respectively.
P8.48-billion in damage. Infrastructure damage has reached P6.16 billion, while agricultural losses were estimated at P2.32 billion.
The NDRRMC also reported around 3,200 damaged houses, including 355 that were destroyed and about 2,800 that were partially damaged.
A total of 117 local government units have declared a state of calamity, including province-wide declarations in Benguet, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, Zambales and Cavite.
Government agencies and local governments have so far distributed P1.69 billion in humanitarian assistance to affected communities.

Las Piñas maintenance chief axed over 'slow' calamity response
MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon relieved the maintenance chief of the DPWH Las Piñas-Muntinlupa District Engineering Office over repeated reports of slow response to calamities and lack of urgency as Metro Manila continues to bear the brunt of continuous rainfall and flooding.
In a memorandum dated August 29, Dizon ordered the immediate relief of engineer Loreto Balena Jr. as maintenance chief.
"In view of repeated reports concerning your unsatisfactory performance, lack of urgency, and delayed response to calamities, you are hereby relieved of your duties as Maintenance Chief of the Las Piñas-Muntinlupa District Engineering Office, effective immediately," Dizon said in the memo.
Balena was directed to complete an inventory, sign and finish pending documents and deliverables, and turn over official records, papers and government properties in his custody.
The Department of Public Works and Highways said the action followed President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s directive to remove officials who neglect their duties and tighten discipline within the agency.

items.title: Tropical Depression Pilandok forms inside PAR, set to enhance habagat
items.summary: No wind signals are up and landfall is unlikely, but PAGASA says it will continue enhancing the habagat.
items.body_text:
Tropical Depression Pilandok forms inside PAR, set to enhance habagat
MANILA, Philippines — The low pressure area east of the country developed into Tropical Depression Pilandok on midday Sunday, August 30.
State weather bureau PAGASA said that Pilandok is expected to even enhance the persistent rains from the southwest monsoon, locally known as habagat.
As of 11 a.m, the tropical cyclone is estimated to be at 1,225 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon, packing maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour near the center and gustiness of up to 55 kph.
It was moving west-northwestward at 15 kph, with winds extending up to 420 kilometers from its center.
As of press time, no Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal was in effect.
PAGASA said Pilandok is unlikely to make landfall and is forecast to remain far from the Philippine landmass. The tropical depression is expected to move west-northwestward through Monday before turning northwestward to north-northwestward.
Pilandok is also forecast to be short-lived, remaining a tropical depression before weakening into a remnant low over the Philippine Sea south of Japan by Tuesday, September 1.
Habagat effects
While Pilandok poses no direct landfall threat, it is actively enhancing habagat, which is expected to bring heavy rainfall and severe winds to large parts of the country.
PAGASA forecasts strong to gale-force gusts caused by the enhanced monsoon expected to affect the following areas:
- August 30: Most of Luzon and Visayas, alongside Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental

items.title: Vietnamese lecturer turns her Chinese mastery into fully funded PhD scholarship
items.summary: A Vietnamese lecturer has secured a fully funded PhD scholarship in China after mastering advanced Chinese and developing a research proposal on how learners acquire thousands of Chinese words.
items.body_text:
Duong Thi Hong Nhung, 25, won the prestigious Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) with an HSK 8 certificate, just seven points short of the highest level's 390.
The lecturer at the Department of Chinese Language at Phenikaa University in Hanoi learned about the scholarship in May. She will study at Beijing Normal University (BNU), which describes itself as a "key university" directly under China’s Ministry of Education and being "among the country's leading institutions for teacher education."
Under the CSC scholarship, Nhung’s tuition, accommodation and health insurance will be fully covered, and she will receive a monthly living allowance of 3,500 yuan (US$487).
Nhung said she was not surprised by the result, as she had anticipated it following her interview with the admissions panel.
"They kept asking in depth about my research topic, which I considered a positive sign," she said.
Nhung earned a master’s degree in International Chinese Language Education at BNU on a CSC scholarship two years ago. To pursue a PhD, she applied to become a lecturer at Phenikaa University’s Department of Chinese Language, where she could gain teaching experience, supervise students’ research, write academic papers and spend time building her application profile.
Pham Thuy Hong, deputy head of the Department of Chinese Language at Phenikaa, said Nhung is a highly regarded young lecturer with expertise, research capabilities and a strong sense of responsibility.
"She uses modern teaching methods, inspires students and is very enthusiastic about all the department’s work," Hong said.
All of Nhung’s choices at the time were aimed at pursuing higher education. Preparing her application was also the busiest period of her life as a lecturer. At times, she slept only three to four hours a day.
"The pressure was so intense that sometimes I busted into tears while working," Nhung said.
She said research ability is what admissions panels care about most when evaluating PhD applications. She therefore invested heavily in her research proposal.
Nhung initially planned to study the Chinese phonetics of Vietnamese speakers. After months of reading materials and discussing the topic with lecturers, she shifted her focus to the cognitive processes involved in vocabulary acquisition among Chinese language learners. She believes the topic offers long-term research potential and still contains many gaps.
"The research direction I choose for my PhD will affect my entire academic career, so I want to make the choice carefully," Nhung said.
She subsequently prepared a detailed research plan outlining the procedures and specific methodologies, along with a reference list of 40 to 60 sources.
Nhung also traveled to China to take the HSK, an international Chinese-language proficiency test with nine levels. Despite studying for only about 10 days, she scored 383 on HSK 8, just seven points short of the highest level.
She believes differences in Chinese proficiency among learners mainly stem from vocabulary. To reach HSK levels 7, 8 or 9, learners need to acquire around 12,000 words while also practicing with test papers to become familiar with the exam structure and time allocation.
For the essay section, she practiced writing from a native speaker’s perspective and used AI tools to evaluate and revise her writing.
For students hoping to win scholarships, she recommends preparing early rather than waiting until their final year of university. In addition to GPA and language certificates, applicants should invest in a research proposal if they plan to pursue a master’s or doctoral degree.
Thai Linh, also a Chinese language lecturer at Phenikaa, said she was not surprised that her colleague had won the PhD scholarship.
"What I admire most about Nhung is her discipline and commitment to self-study. Outside teaching hours, she almost exclusively reads materials, writes and conducts research," Linh said.
In early September, Nhung will move to Beijing to begin her studies. Sh

items.title: Punished with 200 squats for missing her sales quota, saleswoman suffers muscle breakdown
items.summary: A 29-year-old telesales worker in Hangzhou, eastern China, was hospitalized with severe muscle breakdown after taking 200 squats as punishment for missing her daily sales quota rather than pay a fine she could not afford.
items.body_text:
She has since quit and lodged a complaint with the labor inspection unit that oversees the company, which told her it would investigate, the South China Morning Post reported.
The woman, surnamed Yang, had recently moved to Hangzhou, in Zhejiang Province, and began her first job in June as a financial consultant on a monthly salary of CNY4,500 (US$670).
The role was in practice telesales, at a loan assistance company that Hong Kong's Sing Tao Daily identified as the Hangzhou branch of Suzhou Dongrong Information Technology.
Her team manager, surnamed Zhang, set each member a daily quota of 200 calls, one client visit and one client expressing an intention to work with the firm, according to the SCMP.
On July 28, after missing two of those targets, Yang was told she could do 100 squats or pay a CNY50 ($7) fine for each. She said she had no money and opted for the full 200.
Zhang named her in the company's WeChat group and required her to film the punishment as proof, Sing Tao Daily reported, citing the Zhejiang consumer affairs programme "1818 Golden Eye".
Footage running close to five minutes shows her moving between spots in the office building to get through the sets, her limbs shaking. By the end she is gripping a door frame to stay upright.
She told the programme her legs hurt so badly they felt as though they would burst, and that she could no longer walk.
Muscle breakdown
Short of money, Yang did not see a doctor for five days. She took a taxi to the nearest hospital on Aug. 2, after her urine turned dark.
Tests put her creatine kinase, an enzyme released into the blood when muscle tissue is destroyed, above 16,000 U/L, the SCMP reported, far beyond the roughly 1,000 U/L usually sufficient to diagnose rhabdomyolysis.
The condition floods the bloodstream with proteins that can block the kidney's filtering tubules and cause kidney failure.
Yang avoided that and was told to rest and stay off strenuous exercise. Her treatment cost CNY1,400 ($208).
She resigned on July 30, unable to work, and told the SCMP she believed the company had set targets it knew she could not meet in order to push her out.
She asked Zhang to reimburse her medical and transport costs and pay CNY15,000 ($2,230) for personal injury, enough to cover 75 days of living expenses until she was well enough to look for another job. He refused and told her to sue.
Speaking to "1818 Golden Eye", Zhang said he knew the punishment violated labor law but argued that a sales company has to apply a degree of pressure to hit its targets, Sing Tao reported.
He said the matter had nothing to do with the company and that the sum Yang wanted was unacceptable.
A court in an earlier case held a company 70% liable after an employee developed rhabdomyolysis from 100 squats ordered by managers in a work WeChat group, ruling that instructions posted there carried the company's authority and bound employees rather than merely encouraging them, The Paper reported.
Under China's Labor Law, an employer who humiliates or physically punishes a worker can leave the individual responsible facing administrative detention of up to 15 days.

items.title: Vietnamese student admitted to China's top three universities after nearly being kicked out of Chinese class
items.summary: Phung Minh Phuong enrolled at Tsinghua University's School of Economics and Management in late August with half her tuition covered, turning down offers from Peking University and Fudan University.
items.body_text:
The three rank as mainland China's best universities in Times Higher Education's 2026 World University Rankings. Tsinghua places 12th globally, Peking 13th and Fudan 36th.
"I applied just to test myself, so when the results came I was both surprised and happy," Phuong, 18, said. "I think I was lucky, but I'm also proud that the effort paid off."
Phuong started learning Chinese in grade 6 at her parents' urging. She had not settled on it as a long-term path then, she said, and studied only casually.
It was at the start of grade 9, when she decided to sit the entrance exam for a specialized Chinese class, that she began working at it seriously.
In her first lessons with Nguyen Thi Hong Nhan, a university lecturer in Chinese, she could not read a single character, got every grammar exercise wrong and mispronounced the words she did know.
Nhan eventually raised with the family whether she should continue. Phuong's mother asked for a three-month trial before they looked at other options.
"What I was lucky about is that my mother never passed on the teacher's worries, or the family's, so I just thought I was a little behind my classmates and kept going to class carefree and confident," Phuong said.
Over the following weeks she made fewer mistakes and began drawing praise for her pronunciation. She cleared the trial and stayed with the language.
In the summer of 2023 she won a place in the Chinese stream at the Foreign Language Specialized School, a selective public high school in Hanoi run by Vietnam National University. Her score in the specialized subject was nearly 8.5 out of 10.
There she drilled past papers, practiced speaking, built vocabulary and listened to podcasts daily.
In grade 10 she passed HSK 6, the top band of the standard six-level Chinese proficiency test. In grade 12 she took second prize in the national Chinese contest for gifted students.
"Seeing older students at my school get into top Chinese universities, I decided to try. I thought I would fail, so I was reluctant for people to know and applied quietly," she said.
Her application essay described watching her father run the family business in gemstones and feng shui stones. On trips to the shop he showed her how to market products and keep faith with customers, experiences she said pushed her toward business, economics and finance.
International applicants must also sit the China Scholastic Competency Assessment, a standardized entrance exam China established in 2025 to replace a patchwork of transcript and language requirements.
The first sitting was held in December 2025, and the test becomes mandatory for all international undergraduate applicants by 2028. Mathematics is compulsory for every candidate, including humanities applicants, and an HSK certificate cannot substitute for it.
The new requirement worried her, Phuong said, until she worked through the test structure and realized she could prepare on her own using material available online.
That stretch overlapped with her preparation for the national contest, her end-of-term exams, and a separate entrance exam at Peking University. Each carried its own difficulty, she said, forcing her to keep adjusting how she studied and how she allocated her time.
The Peking University interview ran as a debate, with each group of five candidates defending a position while demonstrating their command of the language.
Candidates cannot memorize answers or drill to a template in that format, Phuong said, and need vocabulary and fast reflexes instead.
At Tsinghua, examiners questioned her directly and ranged well beyond the finance program she had applied to. She was tense at first but steadied herself, breaking each question into parts and answering point by point.
Three years of work as a teaching assistant and Chinese tutor during high school, she said, trained the delivery and composure that carried her through both.
Bui Quynh Van, a lecturer in the Chinese department at Hanoi University who has advised Phuong sin

items.title: No evidence yet of arson in Klongthom Centre fire
items.summary: Police have so far found no evidence of arson in the Klongthom Shopping Centre fire to support speculation of a conspiracy to force some businesses out, Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said on Sunday.
items.body_text:
Police have so far found no evidence of arson in the Klongthom Shopping Centre fire to support speculation of a conspiracy to force some businesses out, Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said on Sunday.
He said the stability of the fire-ravaged structure was now being assessed before a full forensic inspection could begin.
Police have questioned nearly 100 witnesses and affected parties, with most accounts indicating that smoke was first seen emerging from the central section of the building before the fire spread rapidly through the complex, according to Pol Maj Gen Chaikrit Pho-a, commander of Metropolitan Police Division 6.
A huge fire tore through the popular shopping centre on Worachak Road on Friday night, causing extensive damage, including the collapse of large sections of the building.
- Structural assessment under way -
Mr Chadchart inspected the site on Sunday with officials from the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) and local police. He said authorities were focusing on three priorities: extinguishing lingering hotspots, assessing the building's structural integrity, and preparing for its eventual demolition.
Access to the interior remained restricted because the collapse of the second floor left columns, beams and debris piled up in the lower-level retail area, creating safety risks for emergency personnel.
Material trapped inside could also still fuel flare-ups, making it unsafe for officials to carry out a full inspection.
The BMA would ask structural experts who previously assisted in the response to the collapse of the State Audit Office tower to help determine which sections could be safely removed to allow crews to reach areas where there were still hot spots.
- Forensic inspection -
Authorities spent Sunday preparing a map of the area where the fire is believed to have begun and them spread through the building, drawing on CCTV footage, video clips and images shared on social media.
If safety conditions permit, forensic police and BMA engineers were expected to enter the site at 8am on Monday to begin looking for the cause of the blaze.
The investigation would focus on the suspected ignition point, electrical systems and records of access to the building.
Mr Chadchart said the building's main power supply was normally shut off about 8pm each day, yet the fire broke out shortly before 9pm. Investigators would therefore need to verify the electrical system and determine exactly when power was cut.
- Traders still barred from site -
Pol Maj Gen Chaikrit confirmed the investigation had so far uncovered no indication that the blaze was linked to arson or any alleged attempt to force businesses from the market building. Most of those questioned had filed complaints over damage to goods and property.
Police have maintained round-the-clock security at the site and are not allowing traders or business operators to enter because the structure remains unsafe.
The cause of the fire will not be determined until forensic examinations and structural assessments are completed, he said.

items.title: Gunmen storm Pattani department store, set off bombs
items.summary: PATTANI - Armed insurgents stormed into a big department store in Pattani on Saturday evening, forcing customers and employees to leave before detonating three bombs.
items.body_text:
PATTANI - Armed insurgents stormed into a big department store in Pattani on Saturday evening, forcing customers and employees to leave before detonating three bombs.
Security officials believe the insurgents were attempting to fuel unrest in the southern border province ahead of floated, approaching talks in Malaysia.
The attack on the Global House store in tambon Bana of Muang Pattani district began shortly before 7pm.
Armed men first evicted customers and staff. Three explosions rocked the building minutes later.
Five masked men armed with assault rifles and handguns had arrived on two motorcycles and a motorcycle-sidecar combination, Pol Col Jeffrey Salaimankul, chief of Muang Pattani police station, said on Sunday.
Two of the attackers subdued security guards at the entrance, while two others entered the store and ordered staff and customers to leave. The men then planted three explosive devices at different locations inside the building.
A fifth suspect parked the bomb-laden sidecar in the store's loading area.
Before fleeing, one of the attackers told a security guard: “If you do not want anyone to be killed, hurry and get everyone out of the store.”
The suspects escaped on motorcycles. About five minutes later, three bombs exploded inside the store. No deaths or injuries were reported.
Security forces sealed off the area amid fears that additional explosives had been left behind.
An explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) unit led by Pol Lt Gen Piyawat Chalermsri, commissioner of Provincial Police Region 9, inspected the sidecar combination left in the loading bay. A drone detected suspicious objects inside the vehicle and the team deployed a robot to disable the device before moving the sidecar to a safe area for examination.
The vehicle contained an improvised bomb packed into a gas cylinder weighing nearly 50 kilogrammes, along with seven gallons of petrol. They spent two hours safely dismantling it.
Images released by the Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 show the gas cylinder used as an improvised bomb, along with fuel containers, on a motorcycle and sidecar left inside the loading area at the Global House store bombed in Pattani on Saturday night. (Photo: Isoc Region 4)
Police said the device may have malfunctioned after its triggering mechanism was disturbed during transport, but was capable of causing extensive damage had it detonated.
Pol Lt Gen Piyawat said the motorcycle-sidecar appeared to be a booby trap, intended to be remotely detonated after security personnel were lured to the scene.
“EOD personnel have disabled part of the triggering system and are continuing inspections to ensure the area is safe,” he said.
Security personnel remained at the scene on Sunday morning to assess damage and gather forensic evidence.
Global House department store (Photo supplied)

items.title: Nepal flood survivors return to ruins to salvage memories
items.summary: DHUNGE (NEPAL) - Days after a wall of water and debris ripped through Nepal, Shanti Lamichhane sat on a fruit crate in the dirt where her village once stood, staring at what remained of her home.
items.body_text:
DHUNGE (NEPAL) - Days after a wall of water and debris ripped through Nepal, Shanti Lamichhane sat on a fruit crate in the dirt where her village once stood, staring at what remained of her home.
Across Nepal's flood disaster zone, survivors are returning to villages reduced to mud and debris, searching for belongings, documents and fragments of lives swept away in minutes.
Lamichhane said she was waiting for bulldozers to finish clearing the path so she could return.
"I want to retrieve a few things, but it is not just about that," she told AFP. "All my memories are there too."
The village of Dhunge, once home to roughly 150 families, now lies in ruins, reduced to a swampy expanse with an ominous rotting stench -- one of dozens of settlements obliterated by the Himalayan floods.
The US Geological Survey said the disaster on Wednesday morning on the China-Nepal border was caused by a glacial collapse, sending an icy torrent downstream driving boulders with its sheer force, cutting a swathe through Nepal from north to south.
As of Sunday morning, figures from Nepal and China put the total number of missing close to 3,000, with 691 bodies recovered.
Forced to flee for their lives without time to take anything with them, many survivors are now returning to salvage whatever might remain -- or simply to see what became of what they once called home.
- 'Stench' -
Hari Prasad Rimal returned to his home in the village of Devighat, hoping to recover treasured belongings -- not least some jewellery and cash. He brought back a photograph of his daughter.
"It was pasted on a chest that was floating," said Rimal, 44. "There was nothing else I could retrieve, but that photo also means a lot."
Rimal's warehouse business, a few kilometres upstream, remained inaccessible, he said. Drone images taken by a volunteer showed only mud and debris where it had stood.
"It is gone, but I should not complain perhaps," he said. "At least, everyone in my family survived."
In Dhunge, Navraj Upretti waded through knee-high sludge towards his home, flanked by two rescuers carrying shovels by his side.
"I have some important documents I really need," he implored.
After an hour-long search, documents did emerge from beneath the silt -- but they belonged to a neighbour and were duly returned.
Upretti, 40, said he had less than a minute to escape when the floods struck.
"The house was inundated, I had managed to get barely 100 metres away," said Upretti, who ran a restaurant in the area. That was completely destroyed.
Santosh Adhikari was in Kathmandu when the deluge swept away his home in Dhunge. He returned three days later to find the house buried.
"There was nothing," he said.
Workers clearing silt from the flood-struck region say they occasionally come across personal belongings, including gold jewellery.
"But the debris is still knee-high and there is a stench in many places," said Ayushman Kuinkel, a rescuer from the Nepal Scouts youth group.
"One knows that there are also likely bodies under it."

items.title: Grisly search for missing as Nepal morgues overflow, burials begin
items.summary: BHÂRATPUR (Nepal), Aug 30 — Distraught families in Nepal watched grisly images of mangled corpses on a scree...
items.body_text:
BHÂRATPUR (Nepal), Aug 30 — Distraught families in Nepal watched grisly images of mangled corpses on a screen today, seeking to identify relatives as overflowing morgues forced authorities to begin burying flood victims.
In a building next to a makeshift morgue in Bharatpur, Shobha Adhikary emerged from the crowd after scanning the LED screen.
She told a local coordinator she believed the 37th image — showing the pale, swollen face of a man lying on a pebbled riverbed — was her childhood best friend.
“It looks like him, for sure,” she said, showing coordinators a photograph of a smiling, middle-aged man.
“My husband and I are best friends with Rajkumar and his wife Geeta,” she said. Geeta has also been missing since a lethal wall of water and debris ripped through the Nepal-China border on Wednesday.
Nepal’s disaster agency said today it had recovered more than 750 bodies, with at least 2,500 people missing.
Hundreds of bodies were swept downstream, and the tolls continue to rise.
Bharatpur is close to the Indian border — roughly 160 kilometres downstream of the epicentre of the disaster which the US Geological Survey said was caused by a glacial collapse.
More than 250 bodies have been recovered in the southern district of Chitwan. Only nine have been identified by relatives.
‘Number-tagged’
Grieving relatives alternated between watching intently and closing their eyes, overwhelmed by the grim exercise.
“My brother’s wife is missing,” Vinod Kumar Basnet said.
“My brother died of Covid during the pandemic, and their kids are waiting at home for their mother. If I see her body, I can at least tell them she is not coming back.”
The morgue at the local hospital in Bharatpur is equipped to hold only a couple dozen bodies.
Authorities have been forced to store corpses at a temporary holding centre — the air-conditioned offices of the district commerce association.
But without proper freezing facilities, it is only a short-term arrangement.
“Many of the bodies were starting to badly decompose, and there was an unbearable stench in the whole area,” said Rudra Adhikary, a member of the district Red Cross committee.
“So they were buried after collection of DNA.”
Some 90 bodies were buried in shallow graves yesterday, district authorities said in a statement.
An AFP correspondent saw workers digging dozens more graves today in a forest clearing on the outskirts of the town.
The dead are traditionally cremated on funeral pyres in Hindu-majority Nepal, and the burials are viewed as long-term storage until families can retrieve them.
“The depth of the graves is 1.5 metres; the bodies are 40 centimetres apart from each other,” Adhikary said.
“Each body is being number-tagged and wrapped in a plastic bag before burial.”
DNA records
Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai told reporters on Sunday the burials followed international protocols, adding that Nepal needed “more than a thousand” freezer units to store bodies.
Examining the pictures, volunteers said the only way to accurately identify people was through a DNA match — which would require a family member to provide a sample.
With many corpses badly disfigured, volunteers said several families had claimed the same body.
In some cases, families who initially identified a body from the screen withdrew their claims after seeing it in person, said Devendra Poudel, a local Red Cross volunteer.
“Yesterday, we had a case where two families said one of the dead bodies was their relative,” Poudel said.
“But when we showed them the body, one of the women realised it wasn’t her husband because there was a tattoo on the arm.”
Some bodies are so disfigured, Poudel added, “that often it is difficult to say if it’s a man or woman”.
“Tattoos, rings and earrings are the only way to really identify.” — AFP

items.title: Rescuers dig into tunnel as missing toll from Nepal, China flood tops 3,000
items.summary: BIDUR (Nepal), Aug 30 — Rescuers in Nepal and China battled through leg-sucking mud, as well as the threat of...
items.body_text:
BIDUR (Nepal), Aug 30 — Rescuers in Nepal and China battled through leg-sucking mud, as well as the threat of rising rivers and a newly formed lake, today to search for thousands missing after a deadly wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayas, engulfing entire villages.
Latest figures from both countries put the number of missing at 3,048, including hundreds of foreigners. There were 768 confirmed deaths, with reports of some bodies possibly swept downstream as far away as India.
Nepal said it had begun the grim task of burying some of the hundreds of bodies today, after first taking DNA samples so that families could later reclaim them and perform traditional funeral rites once they had been identified.
The disaster, which struck the China-Nepal border Wednesday morning, was caused by a glacial collapse, sending a wall of water and debris downstream, the US Geological Survey said.
Nepali army troops and engineers also drilled through debris on Sunday towards hydropower workers believed trapped in a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site in the Himalayan river valley after they successfully inserted a pipe into the passage.
They have “started sending air through the small opening”, Nepali Home Minister Sudan Gurung said in a statement.
Overnight rain and rising river waters hampered efforts earlier today, filling the excavation area with water before conditions eased, the Nepal army said.
Nepal’s disaster authority listed 933 hydropower workers among the missing in an area home to vast energy infrastructure projects.
Chinese rescuers near the Tibet border port that was hit by a deadly mudslide were “moved to a safe location” today after a new lake was formed by a landslide, state media reported.
China’s state news agency Xinhua reported today that experts had said “a glacier on the southern slope of Lirung Peak in Nepal” fractured, triggering an ice-rock avalanche.
The torrent plummeted rapidly, forming a massive debris flow that travelled more than 20 kilometres before crashing into Gyirong Port.
“The sudden glacial collapse and flash flood is a devastating reminder of how fragile these mountain environments can be,” UN climate chief Simon Stiell said in a statement.
‘Nothing left’
Survivors face an agonising wait to learn the fate of missing relatives and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away,” resident Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP in Nepal’s Nuwakot district.
“There is nothing left.”
Worried relatives crowded around lists of rescued people pasted on a wall at an army base serving as a rescue hub in the district capital Bidur.
Nepal’s disaster authority said today 592 foreigners, including trekkers and Hindu pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash, were among the missing.
The Isha Foundation, led by Indian guru Sadhguru, said in an Instagram post yesterday that 80 members had been on a group trip in the area.
“At this time, there seems to be no encouraging indications of survivors at the immigration office area,” it said.
‘Enormous’ trauma
The United States and Canada said they would provide US$3.6 million (RM14.5 million) each in humanitarian aid to Nepal.
The UK has offered US$6.8 million, while the UN released US$2.5 million in emergency funding, and aid pledges were made by the European Union, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and others.
Nepal’s economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said the reconstruction bill could run into “billions of dollars”.
He appealed for specialised assistance, including heavy-lift drones and technology to help locate people who are trapped.
Malaysia said it would send search-and-rescue specialists to assist.
Khanal also called for forensic testing kits to identify corpses and freezer units to store them, saying bodies that have been in water could decompose at a faster rate.
The deluge

items.title: Nepal begins burials as flood death toll rises to 752
items.summary: KATHMANDU, Aug 30 — Nepal said today it had begun burying some of the hundreds of bodies recovered after devastati...
items.body_text:
KATHMANDU, Aug 30 — Nepal said today it had begun burying some of the hundreds of bodies recovered after devastating floods, after taking DNA samples and marking them so families can later retrieve them.
The dead are traditionally cremated on funeral pyres in Hindu-majority Nepal, so the burials are viewed as long-term storage until families can retrieve them.
Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai told reporters that all those buried were carefully recorded, but also appealed for international support, saying Nepal needed “more than a thousand” freezer units to store bodies.
The announcement of the burials came as Nepal’s disaster ministry increased its toll again on Sunday to 752 bodies recovered and 2,502 people missing.
That list includes 589 foreigners unaccounted for.
Chinese state media earlier confirmed 16 dead in Tibet and 546 people missing following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the overall toll to 768 dead and 3,048 unaccounted for.
“Following standard and accepted protocols, such as those of ICRC (Red Cross), the mortal remains of the dead, especially those not recognisable… have been temporarily buried,” Rai told reporters.
“Medical teams took DNA samples from every victim prior to the burial so that families can match-reference later, and would be allowed to exhume for necessary rituals.”
Nepal has called for freezer storage units and DNA testing kits, as it is overwhelmed with the number of bodies to store safely.
“We have requested different countries for freezers; we will need more than a thousand,” Rai added.
“Many dead bodies have been collected, and they have started decomposing. To preserve public health, we had to bury the decomposing bodies,” he added. — AFP

items.title: England reduce Pakistan to 53-3 to close in on victory
items.body_text:
England reduce Pakistan to 53-3 to close in on victory
LONDON, Aug 30 : England closed in on a first home test series win for two years as Pakistan slumped to 53-3 at lunch on the fourth day of the second test at Lord's on Sunday.
Set a very tough target of 389 to square the series after bowling England out for 208, Pakistan's fragile batting was again exposed by the home pace attack.
Ollie Robinson removed Azan Awais with a delivery that nipped back off a length to trap him LBW and three balls later produced a stunning delivery that hit the top of Abdullah Shafique's off stump, leaving Pakistan reeling on 7-2.
There was no respite for Pakistan as it became 14-3 when captain Babar Azam tried to fend off a vicious Jofra Archer bouncer but edged it up on to his helmet and the ball looped to Jordan Cox at third slip.
Shan Masood and Saud Shakeel dug in before lunch but their task looks hopeless.
• England resumed their second innings on 177-7 but Mohammad Abbas helped mop up the tail to finish with five for 57, taking his total for the match to nine wickets.
• Dan Lawrence added only four to his overnight 50 before being bowled by an Abbas delivery that jagged back.
• Abbas got his name on the Lord's board by completing his 'five-for' as Robinson edged behind to Mohammad Rizwan.
• The innings ended with Josh Tongue run out.
• Pakistan opener Imam-ul-Haq will be unable to bat because of injury.
• England rattle through top order but Masood (15) and Shakeel (23) steer Pakistan through to lunch.

items.title: NASA launches powerful new Roman Space Telescope from Florida
items.body_text:
NASA launches powerful new Roman Space Telescope from Florida
CAPE CANAVERAL, Florida, Aug 30 : NASA's new flagship astronomical observatory was launched into space from Florida on Sunday on a mission to probe some of the biggest mysteries in astrophysics and cosmology.
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a roughly $4 billion project, was carried aloft from NASA's Kennedy Space Center aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket.
The telescope is designed to investigate cosmic enigmas such as dark energy and dark matter, while also testing gravity at vast scales and searching for exoplanets, as planets beyond our solar system are called.
There were some weather concerns ahead of the launch but the rocket carried the telescope into space through blue skies and some scattered clouds.
Roman will travel through space toward an orbital location called Lagrange Point 2, situated about a million miles (1.6 million km) from Earth. Its mission is planned for five years, though the U.S. space agency said the telescope may have enough fuel for five additional years.
Roman will build on the capabilities of other orbiting observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, and the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990.
"It will be as if Hubble and James Webb kind of peered through a keyhole at the universe, while Nancy Grace Roman will kick the door down," Nicola Fox, chief of NASA's Science Mission Directorate, told reporters on Saturday.
"Roman has broadly the same sensitivity and sharpness of vision as Hubble, but we survey the sky much faster," Julie McEnery, Roman's senior project scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, told reporters at a briefing in July.
McEnery said one month of Roman observations can survey our entire home galaxy.
"One month of observations to survey our Milky Way galaxy would take about a century with Hubble," McEnery said.
WIDE ANGLE AND ZOOM LENSES
Webb has provided a new understanding of the early history of the universe, finding among other things that primordial galaxies formed sooner and were bigger than previously known. Webb is capable of looking across vast distances and back into deep time, because of the time it takes light to travel.
Roman instead is able to take panoramic views. NASA likens Roman to a camera's wide-angle lens and Webb to a zoom lens.
"Webb is designed to be able to probe very deeply and with exquisite sensitivity into the universe, so we can find rare things in the early universe," McEnery said, while Roman offers "the large vision that complements the deep views that Webb provides."
Roman will help in the understanding of two mysterious cosmic components — dark energy and dark matter — by creating the most comprehensive 3D map of the universe to date. Its main survey, to take more than a year to complete, will cover more than two billion galaxies.
The Big Bang event roughly 13.8 billion years ago initiated the universe, and it has been expanding ever since. Scientists in 1998 disclosed that this expansion was actually accelerating, with an invisible force called dark energy as the hypothesized reason.
The universe's contents include ordinary matter — stars, planets, gas, dust and all the familiar stuff on Earth — as well as dark matter and dark energy. Ordinary matter represents perhaps 5 per cent of the contents. Dark matter, known through its gravitational influences on galaxies and stars, may represent about 27 per cent. Dark energy may represent about 68 per cent.
Using Roman to gauge dark matter's pull and dark energy's push across the universe will bring scientists closer than ever before to solving both mysteries, according to NASA.
Roman also will conduct one of the most comprehensive searches ever for exoplanets. It is expected to discover thousands of new ones and provide the first statistical census of planetary systems similar to our own.
